title: Positioning the Label and Features in Linear Learner Training Input
prompt: You will predict whether an order is canceled by using SageMaker built-in Linear Learner. The extracted CSV has a header, and the cancellation label is in the last column. Select two transformations required when recreating the training file.

choices.text: Keep the header row and include the first row as the model's first training example.
choices.explanation: Column-name strings are not observations, and the built-in CSV format does not expect a header.

choices.text: Keep the order unchanged and change only ContentType to application/json.
choices.explanation: The file remains CSV, so the input format and metadata do not match.

choices.text: Remove the header row.
choices.explanation: CSV input for supervised training with the built-in algorithm must not contain a header row.

choices.text: Move the cancellation label to the first column.
choices.explanation: The target variable for supervised training is placed in the first column of the CSV.

choices.text: Separate the cancellation label from the features and remove it completely from the CSV.
choices.explanation: Supervised training requires the correct labels that the model learns from.

learning.reason: For supervised training with the Linear Learner built-in algorithm, the CSV must have no header and the target variable must be in the first column. Set ContentType to text/csv.
learning.concept: SageMaker built-in algorithm supervised-training CSV format

title: Converting a Small Nominal Category Set into Numeric Features
prompt: A linear model for predicting delivery delays receives three transportation modes—rail, ocean freight, and truck. The modes have no inherent order, and you want the model to learn a different effect for each mode. Which transformation should you select in the existing Data Wrangler flow?

choices.text: One-hot encode the transportation mode.
choices.explanation: This represents each category with a separate indicator value without introducing a nonexistent ordering.

choices.text: Ordinal-encode rail as 1, ocean freight as 2, and truck as 3.
choices.explanation: This creates a single numeric feature, causing a linear model to infer differences and an order that do not actually exist.

choices.text: Rank the modes by their order of occurrence in the input and scale the rank values with min-max scaling.
choices.explanation: Scaling does not remove the original order or the relative differences.

choices.text: Replace every mode with the same constant and convert only the input column to numeric.
choices.explanation: This loses the differences between modes, so the model cannot learn different effects.

learning.reason: Categorical values without an inherent order can be represented with indicator variables. Converting categories into continuous values can incorrectly introduce relationships between adjacent categories.
learning.concept: One-hot encoding categories with Data Wrangler

title: Detecting Missing and Out-of-Range Training Labels Before Ingestion
prompt: Before sending used-equipment data in Amazon S3 to training, you review it with Glue Data Quality. You want NULL sale prices to fail only the completeness rule and non-NULL negative values to fail only the range rule. The compound rules are already configured for ROW evaluation. Which two rules should you select?

choices.text: Make the range rule a ColumnValues OR condition: “sale price is NULL OR sale price is greater than or equal to 0.”
choices.explanation: When the compound rule is evaluated at ROW level, NULL is not a range violation, while only negative values fail this condition.

choices.text: Apply only the range rule ColumnValues >= 0 to the sale price.
choices.explanation: With this ColumnValues comparison, both NULL values and negative values violate the range rule.

choices.text: Use IsUnique to check whether all sale prices are different.
choices.explanation: Duplicate prices can still be valid training labels, and a uniqueness check cannot separate missing values from negative values.

choices.text: Check whether the average sale price is greater than or equal to 0.
choices.explanation: Positive prices can make the average nonnegative even when rows with negative values are present, so this does not detect them.

choices.text: Apply IsComplete to the sale price.
choices.explanation: This detects rows whose sale price is NULL as completeness-rule violations.

learning.reason: Use IsComplete to identify missing values in a required column. Evaluate the range with a row-level OR condition that allows NULL so the two failure causes remain separate.
learning.concept: DQDL IsComplete and ColumnValues

title: Matching Semi-Structured Training-Data Issues with Glue Transformations
prompt: You are preparing semi-structured data for analysis with an AWS Glue DynamicFrame. Select the built-in transformation that corresponds to each transformation requirement. Use each candidate exactly once.

choices.text: DropNullFields
choices.explanation: Removes fields whose values are all null. It does not remove a single row with missing data.

choices.text: Relationalize
choices.explanation: Flattens nested structures and arrays into multiple related, easier-to-handle data frames.

choices.text: ResolveChoice
choices.explanation: Resolves multiple merged types in the same field, such as by converting them to the desired type.

learning.reason: Resolving type ambiguity, flattening nested structures, and removing empty fields are handled by different transformations.
learning.concept: Scope of AWS Glue DynamicFrame transformations

prompts.text: The same feature contains both integer strings and numeric integers. Standardize the type before training.
Flatten the variable-length line-item array within an order and split it into parent and child tables.
An attribute from additional data is null in every record. Remove the unused empty field.

title: Distributing Training-Worker Input by S3 Object
prompt: Demand-forecasting data has already been split into Parquet files of roughly equal size in Amazon S3, and the distributed training code can process worker-specific data. Each instance does not have enough disk capacity to store the entire dataset. Which setting should you select for the SageMaker training channel?

choices.text: Combine the training data into one S3 object and use ShardedByS3Key.
choices.explanation: This method distributes data by object key, so it does not split one large file itself across multiple workers.

choices.text: Set S3DataDistributionType to ShardedByS3Key.
choices.explanation: This distributes the objects from the same S3 input across the training instances.

choices.text: Set S3DataDistributionType to FullyReplicated.
choices.explanation: This delivers the entire dataset to every training instance.

choices.text: Change each worker’s Container Entrypoint and have the channel replicate all data.
choices.explanation: Changing how the code starts does not change the channel behavior; the channel still replicates all input to every disk.

learning.reason: Setting the channel distribution to ShardedByS3Key sends each instance a portion of the objects. This is different from changing the format of the input files.
learning.concept: SageMaker training with ShardedByS3Key and FullyReplicated

title: Imputing Missing Values with a Robust Central Value
prompt: In the training data for a regression model, some values are missing from the “package weight” column. The measurements include a small number of extremely large values, and dropping rows with missing values would leave too few training examples. Which Data Wrangler transformation should you choose to impute the missing values using a representative central value?

choices.text: Choose Drop under Handle missing.
choices.explanation: This deletes rows with missing values and does not satisfy the requirement to retain the training examples.

choices.text: Replace every numeric weight with 0.
choices.explanation: This also discards nonmissing observations and does not impute using a representative central value.

choices.text: Choose Impute under Handle missing and select Median.
choices.explanation: This assigns the median to missing values, preserves the row count, and limits the influence of extreme values.

choices.text: Choose Impute under Handle missing and select Mean.
choices.explanation: The mean can be substantially shifted by extremely large observations.

learning.reason: The median is less affected than the mean by a small number of extreme high observations. Assigning it to missing values preserves those rows.
learning.concept: Data Wrangler imputation based on a measure of central tendency

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Reducing the Weight of Formulaic Words That Appear in Many Documents
prompt: You are feeding inquiry text with identifiable word boundaries into a linear classifier. You want formulaic words that occur in most documents to receive low weights and discriminative terms that occur in only a few documents to receive high weights. Which transformation should you configure in Data Wrangler?

choices.text: Count only the number of occurrences of each token.
choices.explanation: The frequencies of common formulaic words would still be large, so their weight would not be reduced based on how common they are across documents.

choices.text: Use only the character count of each document as the input feature.
choices.explanation: The words themselves would be removed from the input, so discriminative terms could not be represented.

choices.text: Assign sequential numbers in word-occurrence order and use only the largest number.
choices.explanation: Sequential numbers do not represent document frequency or within-document term frequency.

choices.text: Tokenize the text, enable IDF, and generate TF-IDF vectors.
choices.explanation: This incorporates both a term’s occurrences within a document and how common it is across the document collection.

learning.reason: TF-IDF uses both within-document frequency and frequency across the corpus. It reduces the influence of common formulaic words while representing terms that help distinguish documents.
learning.concept: Data Wrangler text vectorization and inverse document frequency

title: Passing Images for Labeling by Reference from S3 Without Copying Them
prompt: As an existing customer, you are creating an image classification job in SageMaker Ground Truth. You will use images in S3 in the same Region, and the input manifest will be placed under a different S3 prefix. Which approach lets you configure the job without embedding the image binaries in the manifest?

choices.text: Create one JSON object per image, one per line, and record each image’s S3 URI in source-ref.
choices.explanation: This identifies each image to be labeled without copying the data to another location.

choices.text: Write the local PC path to each photo in the manifest as source-ref.
choices.explanation: A Ground Truth job cannot access images stored on a local PC.

choices.text: Create a headered CSV listing the images and record only the file extension in each row.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the line-based input-manifest format or the requirement for a key that references each image.

choices.text: Embed all image bytes as Base64 in a single row of a JSON array.
choices.explanation: This does not reference the original images and is not image-specific JSON Lines.

learning.reason: An input manifest that references images in S3 uses one JSON Lines record per image and specifies the S3 image URI in source-ref.
learning.concept: The source-ref field in a Ground Truth input manifest

title: Converting Continuous Values with Different Units into Features with Comparable Variance
prompt: The input to a model that uses feature distances includes response time in seconds and order counts. You want to bring the mean of each feature to 0 and its variance close to 1, limiting one feature from dominating the distance simply because the measurements use different units. Which Data Wrangler transformation should you use?

choices.text: Apply one-hot encoding to all continuous values.
choices.explanation: This converts each numeric value into a category and does not adjust the variance while preserving the continuity of the numeric values.

choices.text: Apply Standard Scaler to each continuous-value column.
choices.explanation: This centers and scales each column independently.

choices.text: Subtract the same constant from every value in each column.
choices.explanation: This can shift the mean, but it does not change the variance.

choices.text: Convert each column to numeric ranks and divide by the maximum rank.
choices.explanation: This discards differences between the original observations and does not directly standardize them to mean 0 and variance 1.

learning.reason: Standard Scaler subtracts the mean and scales values based on the standard deviation, making it appropriate for targeting unit variance across differently measured features.
learning.concept: Data Wrangler Standard Scaler and variance normalization

title: Reacquiring Previous Training Data When the Same S3 Key Is Updated
prompt: A bucket has S3 Versioning enabled, and the input under the same key is updated weekly. When reproducing a past training run, you need to retrieve each object that was read at the time of that run with the same content. How should the run manifest and reads be changed?

choices.text: Compare the S3 object’s last-modified date with the run date and continue retrieving the current version.
choices.explanation: The comparison can support a decision, but it does not retrieve the version that was used during the run.

choices.text: Use the run date as a tag value and retrieve the current version with the same tag.
choices.explanation: A tag cannot replace a version ID for fixing the content of historical data.

choices.text: Save the bucket, key, and version ID used during training, and specify the version ID in GetObject when rerunning.
choices.explanation: This directly references the previous version of the same key.

choices.text: Save only the key used during training and do not pass a version ID to GetObject.
choices.explanation: The latest content during the rerun may not be identical to the content used in the original run.

learning.reason: A GET that specifies only a key returns the current version. Record the version ID used during the run and specify that ID when retrieving the object.
learning.concept: S3 Versioning and fixing the content of training inputs

title: Turning Reused SQL Features into Columnar Training Inputs
prompt: Use Athena SQL to aggregate sales events on S3 by customer. You want to keep the resulting features in S3 as Parquet so that multiple training jobs can reuse the same contents and read only selected columns. Which SQL operation is best?

choices.text: Define only a view for the aggregation SELECT.
choices.explanation: A view is a query definition and does not materialize the aggregated Parquet data in S3.

choices.text: Change only the classifier to Parquet in the table definition for the existing JSON data.
choices.explanation: Catalog settings alone do not convert the existing files to Parquet.

choices.text: Run the same SELECT for each training job and use only the result produced at that time.
choices.explanation: Even with the same conditions, this does not satisfy the requirement to share aggregated Parquet data.

choices.text: Run CREATE TABLE AS SELECT from the aggregation SELECT, specifying Parquet as the output format.
choices.explanation: This saves the aggregation result as columnar data and creates a reusable table.

learning.reason: CTAS materializes the result of an aggregation query in S3 in the specified format and creates a table that references the result.
learning.concept: Parquet feature snapshots with Athena CTAS

title: Loading Validation Records into a New Online Feature Store
prompt: You are moving new customer features to SageMaker Feature Store. Confirm that registration is complete, then verify that values can be read online using a test customer ID. Arrange the steps in dependency order.

choices.text: Create the feature group using the defined schema and the online store, then wait until it becomes available.
choices.explanation: Confirm that the created group is available before ingesting data.

choices.text: Query the online store with the test customer ID and compare the result with the ingested value.
choices.explanation: After the record has been ingested, compare the query result with the original test value.

choices.text: Define the record identifier for the customer ID, the event-time field, and the name and type of each feature.
choices.explanation: Define the schema required to create the feature group first.

choices.text: Ingest a test record containing the customer ID and event time into the created group.
choices.explanation: Send the initial validation record after the group becomes available.

learning.reason: The schema, including the record identifier and event time, is required to create the group. After the group is created, ingest the test value and verify that it can be read by its identifier.
learning.concept: Dependency order for creating, ingesting into, and reading from a Feature Store feature group

title: Rerunning Only the Specified Historical Range of Training-Data Ingestion
prompt: A Glue job transforms Parquet data in S3 every day and uses existing job bookmarks. You corrected the transformation logic and want to re-output only the ranges from the previous two runs to a separate prefix for validation. Which setting reruns that range without advancing or resetting the bookmark used by the next day’s normal processing?

choices.text: Set the bookmark to Pause and specify the processing range with the run IDs in job-bookmark-from and job-bookmark-to.
choices.explanation: With both boundaries specified in Pause mode, the incremental data in that range is processed without updating the saved bookmark.

choices.text: Set the bookmark to Enable and specify only the current time.
choices.explanation: Enable performs normal processing and state updates. It does not reprocess a validation range bounded by past runs.

choices.text: Set the bookmark to Disable and use the original input prefix unchanged.
choices.explanation: This does not limit processing based on the bookmark and reads the entire input.

choices.text: Reset the existing bookmark and run the job normally.
choices.explanation: This changes the saved state and loses the current baseline used by the next day’s normal processing.

learning.reason: To reprocess part of the history, use Pause with both run-ID boundaries. In this scenario, use a separate output destination so the state and artifacts of normal runs are preserved.
learning.concept: Glue job bookmark Pause mode and partial reprocessing

title: Feature-training reads compete with another consumer
prompt: The full contents of the same Kinesis Data Streams are read by both a feature pipeline for training and an audit process. Writes remain within the shard limits, but feature freshness declines during periods when the audit process reads heavily. Without changing the existing audit process, which change reserves dedicated per-shard read capacity for the feature side?

choices.text: Switch the producer from PutRecord to PutRecords.
choices.explanation: This changes how multiple records are written; it does not change the consumer read capacity.

choices.text: Register the feature side as an enhanced fan-out consumer and subscribe with SubscribeToShard.
choices.explanation: The registered consumer receives independent read throughput for each shard.

choices.text: Only shorten the polling interval for GetRecords on the feature side.
choices.explanation: This changes the call frequency within the shared read throughput of the same shard; it does not provide dedicated capacity.

choices.text: Extend the stream retention period.
choices.explanation: This changes how long history remains available for retrieval; it does not eliminate contention for real-time reads.

learning.reason: Enhanced fan-out provides each consumer with up to 2 MB/s of read capacity per shard.
learning.concept: Dedicated consumer throughput for Kinesis Data Streams

title: Automate registration of additional date partitions
prompt: Training data is stored in S3 by date. The existing layout does not use Hive-style date keys and includes only the date in the path, such as /feeds/2026-11-20/. Data exists for most dates in the target period, and Athena is the only query engine used. Which two changes avoid changing the file layout and eliminate daily partition registration?

choices.text: Enable Athena query result reuse and increase the maximum age of results.
choices.explanation: This reuses eligible previous results; it does not define the locations of new partitions.

choices.text: Enable partition projection on the table and configure a date-type projection, date range, and format for the target date column.
choices.explanation: Athena can calculate the partition values to read from the configured range and format.

choices.text: Define storage.location.template to match the S3 layout.
choices.explanation: Even when the S3 prefix differs from the default Hive-style format, the read location can be calculated from the date variable.

choices.text: Register all partitions every day with a Glue crawler.
choices.explanation: This continues partition registration and does not meet the purpose of the change.

choices.text: Remove the date partition column and filter only on an ordinary column in the WHERE clause.
choices.explanation: This loses partition-level filtering based on the S3 layout.

learning.reason: By specifying the date range and path rule in table properties, Athena derives the S3 location at query time.
learning.concept: Athena date partition projection

title: Reduce human labeling for a large image dataset
prompt: SageMaker Ground Truth is already available to assign a single label to tens of thousands of images. You want to measure accuracy against human-provided labels and focus human effort on images that are difficult to classify. Which built-in approach is most appropriate?

choices.text: Label all images with an unvalidated classification model and create no human-verified data.
choices.explanation: Because the existing model's predictions are adopted in bulk, there is no accuracy check against human labels or selection of difficult images.

choices.text: Change the labeling to a streaming job and send all images with the default settings.
choices.explanation: Ground Truth streaming labeling jobs do not support automated data labeling.

choices.text: Enable automated data labeling in the built-in single-label image classification job.
choices.explanation: The model is updated using human labels, images that can be labeled with sufficient confidence are processed automatically, and the remaining candidates are sent for human review.

choices.text: Send all items to a private workforce and increase the number of workers.
choices.explanation: This may reduce the time required, but it does not reduce the number of items labeled by people.

learning.reason: Built-in active learning uses manually annotated validation data to determine the confidence threshold.
learning.concept: Ground Truth active learning

title: Retrieve historical features for training
prompt: At inference time, the latest features are retrieved by customer ID. For the next training run, you need to aggregate customer features with SQL for historical points in time across multiple months. When both stores are configured for the feature group, which approach should you choose?

choices.text: Read the latest value with GetRecord from the online store and replace its timestamp with the month used for training.
choices.explanation: Replacing historical values with the current value introduces information that did not exist at the training point in time.

choices.text: Pass the event time for the target month to GetRecord and retrieve the historical value for each customer.

choices.text: Create an interface VPC endpoint for the SageMaker endpoint and extract the training history through it.
choices.explanation: This configures network connectivity; it is not a way to query historical data in the offline store.

choices.text: Retrieve the history from the Feature Store offline store with Athena and filter it by timestamp.
choices.explanation: The offline store retains historical records in S3, which can be queried from Athena.

learning.concept: SageMaker Feature Store offline store

title: Passing Processing output to training input
prompt: A SageMaker Processing container creates features for training. You want to keep files from being published during processing and upload all output from the container to a specified S3 prefix when the job ends. Downstream processing uses the output only after confirming that the job succeeded. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Specify LocalPath and S3Uri for the S3 output of ProcessingOutput, and set S3UploadMode to EndOfJob.
choices.explanation: This associates the processing container's output directory with the destination and uploads the files when processing is complete.

choices.text: Use the same output configuration but set S3UploadMode to Continuous.
choices.explanation: This can upload files while the job is running, so it does not meet the requirement to make the files available only after processing is complete.

choices.text: Add the target S3 prefix to ProcessingInput.
choices.explanation: This adds a download source for input; it does not upload the container's artifacts.

choices.text: Rename the output directory inside the container when the job succeeds.
choices.explanation: Renaming a directory locally does not transfer it to the specified prefix without an S3 output configuration.

learning.reason: With S3UploadMode set to EndOfJob, output from the specified local path is sent to S3 when the job completes. Training begins only after the successful status is confirmed.
learning.concept: SageMaker Processing output

category: MLモデルの開発

title: Selecting a Classification Threshold Based on Missed-Fraud Costs
prompt: A fraud-detection model converts scores into binary predictions using a threshold. With a threshold of 0.5 on the validation data, many fraudulent cases are missed. Missing fraud costs more than investigating a false alarm, but there is also a daily limit on the number of investigations. Without retraining the model, what is the most appropriate way to select a new threshold?

choices.text: Choose the threshold that maximizes accuracy on the validation data.
choices.explanation: Overall accuracy gives equal weight to the two types of error. It does not directly reflect business costs or the investigation limit.

choices.text: Measure false negatives, false positives, and the number of cases sent for investigation at multiple thresholds, then choose the threshold with the lowest total error cost while remaining within the investigation limit.
choices.explanation: This reflects the different costs of missed fraud and unnecessary investigations while satisfying the operational capacity limit.

choices.text: Lower the threshold until recall is maximized, without checking the number of investigations.
choices.explanation: This can reduce missed fraud, but it may exceed the investigation limit and increase the cost of unnecessary investigations.

choices.text: Raise the threshold to reduce the number of cases sent for investigation as much as possible.
choices.explanation: Raising the threshold narrows the set of cases classified as positive. This approach does not evaluate both the cost of missed fraud and the investigation limit.

learning.reason: A classification-score threshold changes the trade-off between false positives and false negatives. Evaluate both costs and the operational capacity limit on validation data.
learning.concept: Classification threshold

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Stopping Training When XGBoost Validation Performance Worsens
prompt: You plan to train SageMaker built-in XGBoost for a maximum of 500 rounds. If the validation metric does not improve for 20 consecutive rounds, you want to stop the iterations at that point. Which setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Reduce the learning rate and train for 500 rounds without using a validation channel.
choices.explanation: The learning rate adjusts the update size. This does not configure a stopping condition based on the validation score.

choices.text: Set max_depth to 20 and num_round to 500.
choices.explanation: The maximum tree depth limits the complexity of each tree; it does not monitor the number of rounds without improvement.

choices.text: Specify a validation channel, set early_stopping_rounds to 20, and set the num_round upper limit to 500.
choices.explanation: If the validation score fails to improve for the specified number of rounds, training can stop without waiting for the num_round upper limit.

choices.text: Set only num_round to 20.
choices.explanation: This always ends training within 20 rounds, so training cannot continue even if the validation metric is still improving during that period.

learning.reason: With SageMaker XGBoost, early_stopping_rounds ends training when the validation metric has stopped improving for the specified number of rounds.
learning.concept: XGBoost early stopping

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Evaluating Regression with MAE in the Presence of Outliers
prompt: You are comparing models that predict delivery time in minutes. The error should be described as an average in minutes and evaluated with a penalty proportional to each individual error. Which metric should you use?

choices.text: Use RMSE.
choices.explanation: The result is in minutes, but because it uses squaring, it gives relatively greater weight to large errors.

choices.text: Use MSE.
choices.explanation: Because it averages squared errors, its unit is minutes squared, and the influence of large errors also increases.

choices.text: Use MAPE.
choices.explanation: It evaluates error as a percentage of the measured value, so the result is a percentage rather than an average error in minutes.

choices.text: Use MAE.
choices.explanation: It averages the absolute prediction errors. The result is in the same unit as the target, minutes, and each error contributes in proportion to its magnitude.

learning.reason: MAE averages absolute errors, so it reports the average error in the original unit. Unlike MSE and RMSE, which square errors, it weights individual errors according to their magnitude.
learning.concept: Regression MAE

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Controlling XGBoost Overfitting with Regularization
prompt: With SageMaker built-in XGBoost, you want to compare generalization performance by strengthening only the L2 regularization on leaf weights while keeping the tree structure and learning rate fixed. Which hyperparameter should you change?

choices.text: Increase lambda.
choices.explanation: lambda is the coefficient of the L2 regularization term for leaf weights.

choices.text: Increase alpha.
choices.explanation: alpha changes the L1 regularization term. It does not change the L2 regularization coefficient being compared.

choices.text: Increase gamma.
choices.explanation: gamma adjusts the minimum loss reduction required to split a tree and changes split decisions.

choices.text: Increase eta.
choices.explanation: eta adjusts the update step size for each iteration. It does not change the L2 regularization coefficient.

learning.reason: In XGBoost, lambda controls L2 regularization and alpha controls L1 regularization. When comparing models with the split criterion and learning rate fixed, change only lambda.
learning.concept: XGBoost regularization

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Searching Learning Rates on a Logarithmic Scale with HPO
prompt: The candidate learning rates range from 0.0001 to 1 across several orders of magnitude. You want to allocate enough search points to the smaller values. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Change the endpoint's minimum capacity.
choices.explanation: This is unrelated to Training HPO.

choices.text: Define the HPO continuous range with logarithmic scaling type.
choices.explanation: This searches values across different orders of magnitude on a logarithmic scale.

choices.text: Limit the candidates to 0 and 1.
choices.explanation: This does not search valid intermediate values.

choices.text: Make the model artifact name logarithmic.
choices.explanation: This does not change the search space.

learning.reason: logarithmic scaling type searches a continuous parameter on a logarithmic scale.
learning.concept: SageMaker HPO logarithmic range

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Selecting AutoML Candidates with an Objective Metric
prompt: For tabular classification with SageMaker Autopilot, you generated candidate models using F1, which is important to the business, as the objective metric. The reviewer wants to evaluate the objective metric of promising candidates while preserving the test data. Which procedure should be used?

choices.text: Rank candidates only by training time and adopt the shortest-running model.
choices.explanation: Computation time does not indicate the relative F1 values and cannot compare the specified objective metric.

choices.text: Compare the number of training instances assigned to each candidate instead of F1.
choices.explanation: The number of instances indicates compute capacity, not prediction quality on the validation data.

choices.text: Compare the candidates' validation results using the configured F1 validation scores. After selecting a candidate, evaluate it on the preserved test data.
choices.explanation: Selection is based on the validation metric, while the test data remains available for final evaluation.

choices.text: Ignore the validation results and measure every candidate on the preserved test data to select the best model.
choices.explanation: Using the test data for model selection prevents it from being preserved for an independent final evaluation.

learning.reason: Autopilot provides candidates' validation objective metrics. Selecting a model based on validation results and then evaluating it on independent data provides an assessment unaffected by the selection process.
learning.concept: SageMaker Autopilot candidates

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Detecting Outliers in Unlabeled Time Series
prompt: Factory sensors have no anomaly labels, and you want to detect measurements that deviate from the normal patterns in multidimensional data. Which choice does not create a supervised classifier?

choices.text: Use BlazingText supervised classification.
choices.explanation: It requires ground-truth labels.

choices.text: Use linear regression alone to produce categories.
choices.explanation: Linear regression is not intended for outlier detection.

choices.text: Configure only endpoint autoscaling.
choices.explanation: This does not train a model.

choices.text: Use SageMaker Random Cut Forest for anomaly detection.
choices.explanation: It can be used to score anomalies in unlabeled data.

learning.reason: Random Cut Forest can be used for unsupervised anomaly detection.
learning.concept: Random Cut Forest anomaly detection

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Evaluating Multiclass Classification with Minority Classes
prompt: In a multiclass classification problem, the major categories account for most of the data. You want to evaluate every category with equal weight without hiding performance degradation in minority classes. Which metric should you use?

choices.text: Use macro F1, which averages the F1 score for each class
choices.explanation: It treats every class equally without weighting by class frequency.

choices.text: Use overall accuracy only
choices.explanation: The result can be dominated by the majority classes.

choices.text: Use MSE
choices.explanation: This is an error metric for continuous-value regression.

choices.text: Use inference latency only
choices.explanation: It does not indicate classification quality.

learning.reason: A macro average aggregates class-level performance with equal weight for each class.
learning.concept: Macro F1

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Identifying System Bottlenecks in a Training Job
prompt: You are training with a compatible GPU instance and framework in an environment where SageMaker Profiler is available. You want to examine GPU idle time and the timing of processing on the CPU along the same timeline to identify bottlenecks in the training loop. What should you choose?

choices.text: Record only validation accuracy for each epoch during training.
choices.explanation: This measures changes in prediction quality but does not show where CPU or GPU processing is stalled.

choices.text: Enable SageMaker Profiler and inspect CPU and GPU activity traces for the training job.
choices.explanation: You can analyze the processing timeline and correlate GPU idle periods with the CPU processing performed during those periods.

choices.text: Set a one-minute GPU utilization alarm in CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: This provides aggregated utilization information but cannot correlate computation and CPU processing on the same fine-grained timeline.

choices.text: Compare the training-data distribution with the inference-input distribution using Model Monitor.
choices.explanation: This observes input drift and does not measure computation time during training.

learning.reason: In a compatible environment, SageMaker Profiler traces allow CPU and GPU computation to be correlated on a timeline.
learning.concept: SageMaker Profiler

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Choosing a Distributed Training Method Based on Model Size
prompt: You want to train a model that fits in a single GPU's memory on a large dataset in a short time. You also need to support a future, extremely large model that will not fit on a single GPU. Which options should you choose? Select two.

choices.text: Use endpoint autoscaling
choices.explanation: This does not partition a model for Training.

choices.text: For the first case, use data parallelism to replicate the model on each GPU and provide a different data shard to each GPU
choices.explanation: Data parallelism is appropriate when the model fits on each GPU.

choices.text: For the second case, use model parallelism to partition model layers or tensors across multiple GPUs
choices.explanation: This can partition a model that does not fit on one GPU.

choices.text: For the first case, provide the same data to every GPU
choices.explanation: This does not parallelize the training data.

choices.text: For the second case, reduce the number of GPUs to one
choices.explanation: This does not resolve the memory shortage.

learning.reason: Data parallelism and model parallelism are selected according to the data volume and the model's memory requirements.
learning.concept: Distributed training parallelism

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Learning from Related Store-Demand Histories with One Forecasting Model
prompt: You need to forecast daily demand for multiple stores. Some new stores have only short histories, but the stores share common day-of-week and seasonal patterns. Which approach can learn commonality from multiple demand series without maintaining a separate model for each store?

choices.text: Train an independent ARIMA model for each store.
choices.explanation: This can forecast individual demand, but it does not share learning across stores and requires separate model operations.

choices.text: Classify stores with K-means and use each store's cluster number as the daily demand.
choices.explanation: A cluster number represents a similar group of stores; it does not estimate future demand in a time series.

choices.text: Include each store's demand series as a separate record in the DeepAR training input and train one model.
choices.explanation: DeepAR can train a single global model from multiple related series and use their common patterns.

choices.text: Sum demand across all stores by day and return store-level demand directly from the aggregate series.
choices.explanation: Summing the data loses the ability to distinguish each store's observations, and the model output would represent aggregate demand.

learning.reason: DeepAR can train on multiple related time series simultaneously and use patterns shared across the series.
learning.concept: DeepAR with multiple related time series

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Updating an Existing Image Classification Model with Additional Data
prompt: A model trained with the SageMaker built-in Image Classification - MXNet algorithm exists, and additional images with labels from the same classification scheme are stored in Amazon S3. Which method creates a new model starting from the existing weights while reducing the time required to retrain from scratch?

choices.text: Specify the existing model artifact in the validation input channel.
choices.explanation: The validation channel receives validation data. It is not a channel for loading the weights of an existing model.

choices.text: Send the new images to Batch Transform and save the prediction file under the existing model's S3 key.
choices.explanation: Batch Transform does not update model weights, and a prediction file is not in the format of a trained model.

choices.text: Use CreateEndpointConfig to reference the existing model weights and provide the additional images during deployment.
choices.explanation: An endpoint configuration sets up model hosting. It does not run training to update weights with additional images.

choices.text: Pass the existing model artifact through the model input channel, specify the additional data, and run incremental training.
choices.explanation: Incremental training can continue training with the existing model weights as the initial state.

learning.reason: For supported built-in algorithms, the artifacts from the previous training run can be supplied through the model channel to perform incremental training.
learning.concept: Incremental training for image classification starting from existing weights

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Comparing Multiple Training Experiments on the Same Scale
prompt: Several engineers are experimenting with the same classification problem. For each training run, they want to associate the learning rate, validation accuracy at each epoch, and the corresponding trained model, then compare the runs later. Which method is most appropriate in SageMaker?

choices.text: Record runs in SageMaker MLflow, associate the learning rate as a parameter and validation accuracy as a step-based metric, and associate the model as an artifact.
choices.explanation: This allows run-level parameters, metric histories, and models to be compared in the same tracking system.

choices.text: Aggregate only the endpoint Invocations metric in CloudWatch and compare the training runs.
choices.explanation: Production inference invocation counts do not provide the training settings, validation accuracy, or model association.

choices.text: Overwrite the latest model at the same S3 key each time and compare file sizes.
choices.explanation: File size does not represent validation-accuracy history and does not record its association with the learning rate.

choices.text: Register only production-approved model names in Model Registry.
choices.explanation: Approved models can be identified, but per-trial parameters and accuracy trends are not recorded.

learning.reason: Record metrics, training conditions, and model artifacts in an MLflow run for comparison and reproducibility.
learning.concept: MLflow experiment tracking

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Notifying Downstream Processing When Long-Running Inference Completes
prompt: An image-analysis model takes several minutes to perform one inference, and the client cannot maintain the connection. You want SageMaker to store requests in Amazon S3 and notify downstream processing when they complete. Which configuration is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use only Batch Transform and wait for an individual completion notification.
choices.explanation: Batch Transform performs batch processing; it is not asynchronous endpoint notification for individual requests.

choices.text: Enable only CloudWatch Logs.
choices.explanation: This does not configure request queuing or output notifications for inference.

choices.text: Configure SageMaker Asynchronous Inference with an S3 output location and SNS notifications.
choices.explanation: Correct. Asynchronous inference queues requests and supports S3 output plus success and failure notifications.

choices.text: Continue making synchronous calls to a real-time endpoint.
choices.explanation: This does not fit the long-running request and inability to maintain the connection.

learning.reason: SageMaker Asynchronous Inference supports S3 output and SNS success and failure notifications.
learning.concept: Asynchronous endpoints and completion notifications for long-running ML inference

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Gradually Deploying a New Model to a Production Endpoint
prompt: You need to deploy an approved new model version to a SageMaker endpoint. You want to limit user impact, validate it with a small amount of traffic, and then proceed to full traffic. Which deployment method is appropriate?

choices.text: Delete the existing endpoint and create a new endpoint.
choices.explanation: This undermines staged validation and rapid rollback.

choices.text: Immediately send all traffic to the new model.
choices.explanation: This does not limit the impact.

choices.text: Delete the training data.
choices.explanation: This is not a deployment method.

choices.text: Configure canary traffic shifting with a blue/green deployment during an endpoint update.
choices.explanation: Correct. Traffic can be shifted gradually to the new environment, starting with a small amount.

learning.reason: SageMaker blue/green deployments provide canary or linear traffic shifting.
learning.concept: Canary deployment and gradual traffic migration for ML models

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Tracking the training lineage of deployment candidates
prompt: Among the registered models, you need to investigate which versions were built with training data from before a policy revision. The training-data version cannot be distinguished from the model approval status or the ARN of the approved release. How should you record the training-data version as a machine-readable key-value pair on newly registered models so that you can check it by version later?

choices.text: Record the training-data version ID in CustomerMetadataProperties for each Model Package Version.
choices.explanation: Metadata for each model version can retain a key and value representing its lineage.

choices.text: Record the latest training-data version in the description of the same Model Package Group.
choices.explanation: Updating the description would not allow you to distinguish the data version used by each historical package version.

choices.text: Set the training-data version ID in ModelApprovalStatus.
choices.explanation: Model approval status accepts defined values; it cannot record an arbitrary training-data version ID.

choices.text: Interpret the suffix of ModelPackageArn as the training-data version ID.
choices.explanation: The ARN identifies the model package. Model versions and training-data versions can change independently.

learning.reason: Record the training-data lineage in metadata for each model package version. Approval status and the model resource identifier represent different kinds of information.
learning.concept: Training-data lineage metadata for a Model Package Version

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Using the model version validated in staging in production
prompt: Several versions approved in SageMaker Model Registry are available. Another version might be approved between the completion of staging validation and the production deployment. What should be passed to the deployment pipeline to ensure that the validated version is reused?

choices.text: Reconstruct the model name from the staging endpoint name.
choices.explanation: An endpoint name alone does not pin a specific version of the model package.

choices.text: Record the ARN of the approved Model Package Version used in staging and pass it as the input to production.
choices.explanation: Pinning the versioned ARN allows the same model package to be specified even if another version is approved later.

choices.text: Specify only the Model Package Group and find the latest approved version when production starts.
choices.explanation: If another version is approved after staging, a different version could be selected.

choices.text: Select the file with the latest modification time from the shared S3 prefix for training artifacts.
choices.explanation: The modification time does not indicate that the file was validated in staging.

learning.reason: Passing the ARN of the model package version used in staging to production keeps the deployment target unchanged even if another version appears after validation.
learning.concept: Passing a model package version from staging to production

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Processing the first asynchronous inference request from zero instances
prompt: A SageMaker asynchronous inference endpoint scales down to zero instances overnight. The first request during the day remains in the queue, and processing does not begin until additional requests accumulate. Which change enables the endpoint to start with only a small number of requests while retaining the existing backlog target tracking and scale-down to zero?

choices.text: Start instances when instance CPU utilization exceeds 80%.
choices.explanation: With zero instances, there is no instance to process requests, so queue accumulation cannot be detected through CPU utilization.

choices.text: Only shorten the target-tracking scale-out cooldown period.
choices.explanation: This affects consecutive scaling actions after startup, but it does not configure one instance to start before the trigger condition is met.

choices.text: Create a CloudWatch alarm monitoring HasBacklogWithoutCapacity and use step scaling to increase capacity to at least one instance.
choices.explanation: This detects a backlog with no processing capacity and can start an instance before normal target tracking responds.

choices.text: Set the minimum number of instances to one at all times.
choices.explanation: This can process the first request, but it does not retain the required scale-down to zero.

learning.reason: In addition to normal backlog target tracking, use HasBacklogWithoutCapacity to detect unprocessed requests when capacity is zero and perform the initial scale-out.
learning.concept: Starting asynchronous inference from zero instances

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Selecting an inference model within a shared endpoint
prompt: You serve store-specific models through one SageMaker multi-model endpoint. The models are stored at store-specific relative paths under the S3 prefix specified in CreateModel. For the existing endpoint, how can you specify the target store's model for each invocation?

choices.text: Specify the model's relative path in TargetVariant of InvokeEndpoint.
choices.explanation: TargetVariant specifies a production variant; it does not select a model within that variant.

choices.text: Specify the full URI, including the S3 bucket, in TargetModel of InvokeEndpoint.
choices.explanation: TargetModel receives the relative path from the prefix specified in CreateModel.

choices.text: Pass the model's S3 key in InferenceId of InvokeEndpoint.
choices.explanation: InferenceId identifies an inference and is not used to select a model within a multi-model endpoint.

choices.text: Specify the model's relative path in TargetModel of InvokeEndpoint.
choices.explanation: SageMaker combines the base S3 prefix with TargetModel to identify the target artifact.

learning.reason: Even when invoking a shared endpoint, TargetModel selects the requested artifact for each invocation.
learning.concept: TargetModel for a multi-model endpoint

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Carry Customer IDs into Batch Inference Output
prompt: JSON Lines containing customer IDs are passed to a running SageMaker Batch Transform job. Only features should be passed to the model, while the output file should retain the customer IDs and predictions. Which two data-processing settings should be used?

choices.text: Use InputFilter to remove the customer ID from the model input.
choices.explanation: This identifies which attributes are passed to the inference container. The original input data remains available for the join operation.

choices.text: Set JoinSource to Input and use OutputFilter to retain the customer ID and prediction.
choices.explanation: This joins the original input record with the inference result and selects the fields to retain in the output.

choices.text: Set JoinSource to None and use OutputFilter to filter only the predictions returned by the model.
choices.explanation: Without a join, a customer ID that was not sent to the model cannot be restored in the prediction result.

choices.text: Set SplitType to Line to remove the customer ID and add it to the output.
choices.explanation: This specifies how the input is split. It does not remove input attributes or join them to the output.

choices.text: Use InputFilter to select only the customer ID and use OutputFilter to pass the remaining fields to the model.
choices.explanation: OutputFilter is applied when writing the result, so it cannot select the features passed to the model.

learning.reason: InputFilter narrows the input sent to the model. JoinSource and OutputFilter control joining the input with the predictions and selecting the fields retained in the result.
learning.concept: Batch Transform input filtering and result joining

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Adapt a Custom Inference Container to the SageMaker Serving Contract
prompt: An existing classifier is deployed in a custom container to a SageMaker real-time endpoint. The container can perform inference when requests are sent to /predict on port 5000, but it fails the SageMaker health check. Which change follows the standard hosting contract?

choices.text: Start the server on port 8080, return health status from /ping, and implement inference processing at /invocations.
choices.explanation: This accepts health checks and inference requests on the standard port and paths.

choices.text: Keep port 5000 and /predict, and add 8080 to the Image EXPOSE declaration.
choices.explanation: A declaration alone does not change the server's listening port or the request paths.

choices.text: Change the server to port 8080 but continue using /predict for the health check.
choices.explanation: Even with the correct listening port, this does not satisfy SageMaker's required /ping and /invocations contract.

choices.text: Reconfigure only the model's S3 authorization and keep the container's listening port and paths unchanged.
choices.explanation: Adjusting permission to load the model does not change the container's HTTP interface.

learning.reason: A custom hosting container must listen on port 8080 and provide both /ping and /invocations.
learning.concept: SageMaker real-time inference container serving contract

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Automatically Scale an Endpoint Based on Prediction Requests
prompt: For a real-time inference endpoint, latency worsens when the number of invocations per instance exceeds the target. Which scaling configuration is most appropriate?

choices.text: Change the workload to Batch Transform.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the real-time requirement.

choices.text: Configure target tracking with InvocationsPerInstance as the target metric.
choices.explanation: This is correct. Capacity can be adjusted according to the number of invocations per instance.

choices.text: Change only the model name.
choices.explanation: This does not adjust capacity.

choices.text: Delete the logs.
choices.explanation: This does not improve latency.

learning.reason: SageMaker target tracking can manage endpoint capacity using InvocationsPerInstance.
learning.concept: Load-following autoscaling for a real-time ML endpoint

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Pass Actual Preprocessing Output to Training in the Same Run
prompt: In SageMaker Pipelines, a Processing step writes features to an S3 URI that differs for each run. The Training step must receive the output from the same run and start after preprocessing completes, without locating the URI through a custom script. What should be configured?

choices.text: Have the Training step infer the previous day's date and read that date's prefix.
choices.explanation: This does not guarantee that the data came from the same pipeline run.

choices.text: Start Training at the same time as preprocessing and read the first data found in S3.
choices.explanation: This does not guarantee that preprocessing has completed or that the artifact corresponds to that run.

choices.text: Pass the Processing step's output S3 URI properties to the Training step's input.
choices.explanation: The properties are resolved at pipeline runtime, passing the output from the same run. The data dependency also determines the execution order.

choices.text: Configure only DependsOn and use a common fixed S3 path for the training input.
choices.explanation: This controls execution order but cannot receive the S3 URI that differs for each run.

learning.reason: Referencing the preceding step's output properties establishes both data transfer and the step dependency in the same pipeline definition.
learning.concept: SageMaker Pipelines step-output references and data dependencies

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Limit the Number of Concurrent Steps
prompt: Several independent feature computation steps run in SageMaker Pipelines. Each step is independent and must remain unchanged. Which approach limits the number of steps running simultaneously within the same pipeline execution to a maximum of two?

choices.text: Set ProcessingResources.InstanceCount to 2 for each step.
choices.explanation: This specifies the number of instances allocated to each individual Processing job; it does not control the number of concurrent steps in the pipeline.

choices.text: Change the output of each step to use the same S3 prefix.
choices.explanation: Changing the output destination does not tell the scheduler about dependencies or the desired parallelism.

choices.text: Use the same pipeline execution role for all steps.
choices.explanation: This aligns the permissions used to run the jobs, but steps using the same role can still run in parallel.

choices.text: Specify MaxParallelExecutionSteps=2 in ParallelismConfiguration.
choices.explanation: This sets the limit on concurrent steps within a pipeline execution while preserving the existing dependencies.

learning.reason: MaxParallelExecutionSteps controls how many independent steps can run concurrently in a single execution.
learning.concept: Parallelism within a SageMaker Pipelines execution

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Standardize Deployment While Continuing to Use the Existing Training Process
prompt: The team already performs model training and registration on its existing platform. It wants to use an AWS-provided SageMaker Projects template to provide a sample Git repository, CodePipeline, and deployment to staging and production SageMaker endpoints. Which option most directly meets the requirement?

choices.explanation: This provides the deployment scaffold needed to promote the model to staging and production without changing the existing training process.

choices.text: Rebuild the process from training onward with the Model building, training, and deployment template.
choices.explanation: This is intended to create an end-to-end training and deployment environment. The requirement does not include rebuilding the existing training process.

choices.text: Register a new container for a Processing job.
choices.explanation: This prepares an execution environment for data processing; it does not generate a CodePipeline deployment configuration.

choices.text: Share a training notebook in SageMaker Studio.
choices.explanation: This can be used to share experiment code, but it does not configure deployment to staging and production.

learning.reason: When selecting a Projects template, distinguish the existing training and registration process from the deployment scope being added.

title: Compare Inference Instances Empirically Under the Expected Traffic Pattern
prompt: Before deploying real-time inference, the team wants to compare candidate instances using the same model. Traffic increases sharply during the lunch break in production, so the team wants to specify the request-increase pattern and select a configuration that meets latency and throughput requirements. Which validation method is most appropriate?

choices.text: Choose instances in ascending order of the S3 size of the model artifacts.
choices.explanation: Artifact size alone cannot determine inference latency or throughput when traffic increases.

choices.text: Configure a custom load test in SageMaker Inference Recommender and specify the candidate endpoint configurations, traffic pattern, and stopping conditions.
choices.explanation: A load test with the specified conditions measures the candidate configurations and enables comparison of inference performance.

choices.text: Use SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning to minimize the validation error of the training job.
choices.explanation: This optimizes training hyperparameters; it does not compare endpoint responses under load.

choices.text: Create a data-quality baseline with SageMaker Model Monitor.
choices.explanation: This provides a baseline for comparing inference-input distributions; it does not load-test candidate instances.

learning.reason: Measuring candidate configurations with custom traffic conditions makes it possible to compare latency and throughput under the expected request pattern.

title: Wait for Training to Succeed Before Starting Evaluation
prompt: An AWS Step Functions Standard workflow registers a SageMaker training job. Evaluation starts immediately, before the model output is available in S3, and fails. Which approach allows evaluation to start only after training succeeds without adding custom polling?

choices.text: Insert a fixed Wait state and run evaluation after a set period.
choices.explanation: Training duration varies, and a fixed wait cannot confirm that training has completed successfully.

choices.text: Increase the evaluation Lambda timeout and invoke evaluation immediately after starting the training job.
choices.explanation: Extending the function timeout does not establish the ordering condition that the S3 artifacts are ready.

choices.text: Use arn:aws:states:::sagemaker:createTrainingJob.sync with the optimized SageMaker integration.
choices.explanation: The Run a Job integration pattern waits for the training job to complete, so the workflow proceeds only after it receives a successful result.

choices.text: Receive only the CreateTrainingJob start response and proceed immediately to evaluation.
choices.explanation: This confirms that the job was accepted, but it does not guarantee that training has completed.

learning.reason: When a Standard workflow must wait for a SageMaker job to complete, it can use the corresponding optimized integration with .sync.

title: Reviewing the network configuration at the time of a failure
prompt: A connection failure occurred at 3:00 p.m. on Tuesday for an inference API in a VPC, and an operator subsequently repaired the security group. choices.text: Open the resource timeline for the target security group in AWS Config and inspect the configuration item at the time of the failure.

choices.text: Check only the current security group in the VPC console.

choices.text: Use a normal CloudFormation change set to view the differences for the rule change planned for the next deployment.
choices.explanation: This is a diff for a future change and does not show the actual configuration at the time of the failure.

title: Improve a Glue job that spends too long before filtering input files
prompt: An events table for training has millions of catalog partitions. The Glue job reads only the S3 files for the target date, but it spends a long time listing partitions from the Data Catalog before Spark starts processing. What should be changed?

choices.text: Create a partition index on the target key and specify the date with catalogPartitionPredicate.
choices.explanation: The index filters candidates on the Data Catalog side and avoids retrieving the full list of partitions.

choices.text: Rewrite only the current push_down_predicate expression.
choices.explanation: This can filter before reading from S3, but the catalog partitions are listed before this expression is applied.

choices.text: Add a date filter in the Spark transformation step after reading the data.
choices.explanation: A filter in the transformation step does not reduce the amount of data read from the catalog upstream.
