title: Ingest change data in transaction order
prompt: You want to reproduce updates to different tables as the same order transaction and incrementally update machine learning features. With CDC from AWS DMS to Amazon S3, you must pass the transaction order across tables to downstream processing. Which settings should you choose?

choices.text: Do not use CDC; rerun a full load every day and process the files in filename order.
choices.explanation: This cannot reproduce individual changes that occurred between snapshots or the order of transactions.

choices.text: Only reduce CdcMaxBatchInterval.
choices.explanation: This adjusts the file buffering interval; it does not specify that the output transaction order should be preserved.

choices.text: For the S3 target, set PreserveTransactions to true and specify CdcPath.
choices.explanation: This outputs CDC files with transaction order preserved to the specified path.

choices.text: Output each table as an independent Parquet file and order changes by the S3 last-modified time.
choices.explanation: An object's last-modified time does not correspond to the order of individual transactions across tables.

learning.reason: For an S3 target, AWS DMS can combine PreserveTransactions with CdcPath to output CDC changes as CSV files in transaction order.
learning.concept: Preserving CDC transaction order with DMS

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Correct historical data without changing online inference values
prompt: SageMaker Feature Store has both its online and offline stores enabled. A batch process corrects historical errors for training, and it must not change records used for online inference regardless of the timestamp received by the batch. How should this be specified with PutRecord?

choices.text: Specify only OnlineStore in TargetStores.
choices.explanation: This writes to the online store and does not correct the training history.

choices.text: Omit TargetStores and assume that the input timestamp is sufficiently old.
choices.explanation: When both stores are enabled for the feature group, writes target both stores. This cannot be guaranteed based on the input timestamp.

choices.text: Read the online store after the correction and copy the current values to the offline store.
choices.explanation: This overwrites the training history with current values instead of correctly correcting historical values.

choices.text: Specify only OfflineStore in TargetStores.
choices.explanation: This limits the correction writes to the offline store.

learning.reason: PutRecord uses TargetStores to explicitly select the write destinations. Selecting only OfflineStore prevents records in the online store from being updated.
learning.concept: TargetStores for historical backfilling

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Resume a feature stream from its previous position
prompt: Events are ingested from Kinesis Data Streams by Glue streaming ETL. When the job is restarted within the stream's retention period, you want it to resume from the progress that has already been read. What should be maintained?

choices.text: Maintain the same S3 checkpoint path.
choices.explanation: Processing can resume from the checkpoint that stores the read position.

choices.text: Delete the checkpoint each time and enable the standard Glue job bookmark.
choices.explanation: Job bookmarks are not used for the streaming job's progress, and deleting the checkpoint prevents recovery from it.

choices.text: Always specify LATEST and do not use the previous checkpoint.
choices.explanation: Records that arrived while the job was stopped and are earlier than the latest position could be skipped.

choices.text: Always specify TRIM_HORIZON and recreate the checkpoint.
choices.explanation: This starts reading from older retained records and may cause already-read data to be processed again.

learning.reason: Glue streaming ETL restores the read progress for a restart from the checkpoint.
learning.concept: Read checkpoints in Glue Streaming

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Organizing JSON Records by Region During Delivery
prompt: A feature-generation team wants to store delivery events arriving as JSON under S3 prefixes based on the value of the region field. The team can create a new Firehose stream. Each record contains a single JSON object, and the team does not want to operate custom transformation code. Which method should they choose?

choices.text: Enable compression to S3 and include a Hadoop-style date in the key name.
choices.explanation: Compression and date-based naming do not route records according to the region field.

choices.text: Enable dynamic partitioning, extract region with inline jq, and set it as the S3 prefix.
choices.explanation: This can group and deliver records according to values contained in each record.

choices.text: Specify only the timestamp namespace in the S3 prefix.
choices.explanation: This organizes records by delivery time but cannot separate them by the region value in the record body.

choices.text: Set the region name in the Firehose error-output prefix.
choices.explanation: This configures an error destination; it does not determine the destination for successful records from values in the record body.

learning.reason: Firehose dynamic partitioning can extract a JSON key with an inline jq expression and use its value in an S3 prefix.
learning.concept: Firehose inline JSON extraction and dynamic partitioning

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Daily Extraction of Change Data for Training
prompt: Export the contents of a PITR-enabled DynamoDB table to Amazon S3. The initial full export has already been stored, and the subsequent exports must be divided into consecutive daily intervals. Which setting ensures that a change occurring exactly at a boundary is included in only one interval?

choices.text: Specify the next start time as one second before the previous end time.
choices.explanation: The periods covered by the incremental exports overlap.

choices.text: Create a GSI on the update date and manually exclude the final item each time.
choices.explanation: The boundary will not necessarily contain only one change, and this does not manage PITR incremental-export intervals, including deletions.

choices.text: Specify the end time of an incremental export as the start time of the next incremental export without changing it.
choices.explanation: The end time is excluded from the previous interval and included in the next interval.

choices.text: Specify the next start time as one second after the previous end time.
choices.explanation: A period near the boundary will be left out of the export coverage.

learning.reason: DynamoDB incremental exports include the start time but exclude the end time, so the end time of one adjacent interval can be the same as the start time of the next.
learning.concept: Half-open intervals in DynamoDB incremental exports

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Making Images Added to S3 Visible Through Lustre
prompt: Images are added to Amazon S3 overnight. A training job reads them through an associated FSx for Lustre file system. Which setting reflects files corresponding to new S3 objects in the file system without launching a data repository task every day?

choices.text: Enable only the New event for automatic export.
choices.explanation: This reflects new files on the Lustre side in S3; it does not import additions from S3.

choices.text: Increase only the file system's storage capacity.
choices.explanation: This increases available capacity but does not change the setting that reflects new S3 objects in the file system.

choices.text: Use an S3 lifecycle rule to transition new objects to infrequent access.
choices.explanation: This only changes the S3 storage class and does not import file metadata.

choices.text: In the data repository association, enable the New event for automatic import.
choices.explanation: This reflects file metadata for objects added to S3 on the Lustre side.

learning.reason: Configuring automatic import for the association updates file metadata on the Lustre side in response to object-created events in S3.
learning.concept: S3 integration and automatic import with FSx for Lustre

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Resolving Throttling Caused by a Skewed Write Key
prompt: Temperature data from devices is being written to Kinesis Data Streams. A store has many devices, and using only storeId as the partition key has concentrated that store's records. Ordering across the entire store is unnecessary, but measurements from the same device must be assigned to the same key. What should be changed?

choices.text: Use a value combining the store ID and device ID as the partition key.
choices.explanation: The same device receives the same key, while writes from many devices can be distributed across different hashes.

choices.text: Keep the same storeId and configure enhanced fan-out for the read consumer.
choices.explanation: This separates read throughput; it does not change the producer-side concentration of keys.

choices.text: Use a fixed string as the key for every store and put only the device ID in the record body.
choices.explanation: The device ID in the body is not used for shard selection, so the write concentration continues.

choices.text: Use a random value as the key for each record and put only the device ID in the record body.
choices.explanation: Writes are distributed, but this does not ensure that records from the same device are sent with the same key.

learning.reason: Kinesis Data Streams selects a shard by hashing the partition key. Separating keys by device helps distribute writes while preserving the same key for measurements from each device.
learning.concept: Eliminating hot partition keys in Kinesis

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Read events from all history with an updated consumer
prompt: A schema for learning events managed in Glue Schema Registry is being updated. The new consumer uses the latest schema and must also read events remaining in the data lake that were registered under every previous schema version. There is no requirement for an old consumer to read future new events. Which compatibility setting should be configured?

choices.text: Use NONE.
choices.explanation: Compatibility between schema versions is not checked.

choices.text: Use BACKWARD_ALL.
choices.explanation: Backward compatibility is checked against every previously registered version.

choices.text: Use BACKWARD because it is sufficient, without checking relationships with other previous versions.
choices.explanation: The check is limited to the immediately preceding version and does not verify compatibility with every previous version.

choices.text: Use FORWARD_ALL.
choices.explanation: The direction is reversed; this checks whether readers using previous versions can read newly written data.

learning.reason: BACKWARD_ALL checks that consumers using the latest definition can read data written with every previous version.
learning.concept: Full-history backward compatibility in Glue Schema Registry

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Redact personal information from inquiry text before training
prompt: English inquiry logs will be used to train a classification model. The input is a large volume of text in S3, and a separate file with email addresses and phone numbers redacted must be produced. Which architecture avoids increasing the number of users who can access the raw text and avoids building custom replacement logic?

choices.text: Use Compression and write the original inquiry files unchanged to the training S3 bucket.
choices.explanation: Compression changes the storage format, but the personal information remains after decompression.

choices.text: Exclude only inquiries containing email addresses and use the remaining text without modification.
choices.explanation: Inquiries containing phone numbers would remain, and the requirement to preserve the text with redactions would not be met.

choices.text: Run an asynchronous Comprehend PII detection job with ONLY_REDACTION and specify the target entity types.
choices.explanation: The service replaces the specified types with redactions or entity names and saves the results to the output location.

choices.text: Run the same job with ONLY_OFFSETS and use the results directly as training text.
choices.explanation: The job returns position information, so it does not produce the original text with personal information redacted.

learning.reason: Selecting Redactions for an asynchronous Comprehend PII job outputs text with the specified types redacted to S3.
learning.concept: PII output modes for training material

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Check for reference keys missing from the training data
prompt: Before creating features from purchase events, verify that each event's product_id exists in the reference product table. The same product may be purchased repeatedly, and the reference product table may contain products that have not been purchased. Which Glue Data Quality rule should be configured?

choices.text: Apply IsUnique to product_id in the purchase events.
choices.explanation: Repeated purchases of the same product would fail, and the rule does not check whether the key exists in the reference table.

choices.text: Apply IsComplete to product_id in the purchase events.
choices.explanation: This detects missing values, but not non-NULL values that do not exist in the reference table.

choices.text: Require the RowCount of the two datasets to be equal.
choices.explanation: The number of purchases and the number of products are independent; equal row counts do not guarantee that each key exists.

choices.text: Configure ReferentialIntegrity from purchase-event product_id to the reference product table's product_id, with a match rate of 1.
choices.explanation: This checks that every key in the event data exists in the referenced dataset.

learning.reason: A referential-integrity rule can check the proportion of keys in the input events that exist in the reference table.
learning.concept: Cross-dataset referential integrity in Glue DQDL

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Consolidate multiple annotations for the same image
prompt: As an existing customer, you perform standard single-label image classification in Ground Truth. The same image is presented to multiple workers, and even when their labels disagree, the training manifest must retain one consolidated label per image. Which feature performs this role?

choices.text: Use the annotation consolidation feature for the standard image classification task.
choices.explanation: It produces one consolidated label for each image from multiple responses to the same image.

choices.text: Use automated labeling and always accept the first worker's response.
choices.explanation: Automated labeling divides work between people and models; it does not define a consolidation rule that always selects the first response.

choices.text: Duplicate the same image URI in the input manifest once per worker and train on all entries as-is.
choices.explanation: The duplicate images and differing labels would enter training unchanged and would not be consolidated into one label.

choices.text: Assign different images to each worker and concatenate the labels in sequence.
choices.explanation: This does not allow multiple judgments for the same image to be compared.

learning.reason: For standard Ground Truth tasks, annotation consolidation combines multiple worker inputs for the same data object into one labeling result.
learning.concept: Ground Truth annotation consolidation

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Putting Late Measurements into Measurement-Time Windows
prompt: A five-minute feature is calculated with Managed Service for Apache Flink and passed to SageMaker. Each record contains the device measurement time, and records can arrive out of order by about 30 seconds. Window boundaries must be based on measurement time, and window progress must account for delays within the allowed range. Which configuration should be used?

choices.text: Replace the time of every record with its arrival time and store the measurement time only as a feature.
choices.explanation: The five-minute window boundaries would be based on arrival time, so the measurement-time requirement would not be met.

choices.text: Extract the measurement time and configure a watermark using 30 seconds of forBoundedOutOfOrderness.
choices.explanation: Records can be assigned to windows based on measurement time, while the watermark does not immediately advance to the maximum observed time.

choices.text: Create windows based on processing time and set the checkpoint interval to 30 seconds.
choices.explanation: Checkpoints are for state recovery; they do not define measurement-time window assignment or event-time progress.

choices.text: Use measurement time but choose a strategy that assumes timestamps always arrive in ascending order.
choices.explanation: Because out-of-order arrival is possible, late events may no longer be included in the appropriate measurement-time window.

learning.reason: A watermark that uses event time and allows out-of-order events controls when a window closes when arrival order differs from measurement time.
learning.concept: Flink event time and watermarks

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Processing Many Small JSON Files with Fewer Read Tasks
prompt: Even after restricting the input to daily S3 partitions, each training JSON file is small, and the startup time for Spark tasks that read them with a Glue DynamicFrame is dominant. You want to combine the read units without recreating the original files. Which method should you choose?

choices.text: Stop filtering the catalog by date and add other dates to the input.
choices.explanation: This increases the number of input files and does not solve the problem of having many small input units.

choices.text: Increase only the file size of the results written by Glue.
choices.explanation: The output file size does not reduce the number of tasks that must open the current small JSON files.

choices.text: Set groupFiles to inPartition for the S3 input and adjust groupSize as needed.
choices.explanation: The existing small files can be grouped and read within each S3 partition without modifying them.

choices.text: Apply repartition to the records after they have been read.
choices.explanation: This changes partitions for later processing, but the initial tasks that open the input files have already started.

learning.reason: Glue input grouping combines small files within an S3 partition and forms in-memory partitions for Spark tasks to process.
learning.concept: Glue groupFiles and groupSize

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Detecting Whole-Object Corruption During a Multipart Upload
prompt: A completed large training artifact is uploaded using multipart upload. You want to use the CRC for the entire file before upload as the validation basis and have S3 fail completion if the received data differs. Which method should be used?

choices.text: Attach the precomputed CRC to the uploaded object as user metadata.
choices.explanation: User metadata stores a value; it does not configure S3 to compare the CRC and reject completion.

choices.text: Assume that the completion ETag is the MD5 of the entire object and compare it with the local CRC.
choices.explanation: A multipart ETag cannot be treated as the MD5 of the entire object, and this does not provide a server-side CRC comparison.

choices.text: Validate only the checksum of the last part uploaded.
choices.explanation: This does not verify that the checksum of the entire object, including all earlier parts, matches.

choices.text: Specify the FULL_OBJECT checksum for the applicable algorithm and send the precomputed value in the completion request.
choices.explanation: S3 validates the checksum of the received whole object and fails with BadDigest if the value differs.

learning.reason: When a supported whole-object checksum is configured for a multipart upload, S3 compares it with the received object and rejects a mismatch.
learning.concept: Multipart full-object checksums

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Applying the Same Feature Flow to Monthly S3 Inputs
prompt: An existing SageMaker Data Wrangler flow manages type conversions and missing-value processing for sales data. Each time you process a new month's data, you want to reuse the same transformation definition and pass only the date of the S3 input path for that processing job. What should you configure?

choices.text: Parameterize the date portion of the flow's S3 input path and specify the target month in the job.
choices.explanation: The same flow definition can read different S3 objects for each month.

choices.text: Create separate copies of the flow with each month's S3 input location hard-coded.
choices.explanation: This requires duplicated flows, and the transformation content must be changed separately in each copy.

choices.text: Keep the input path fixed and change only the output location for each month.
choices.explanation: Changing the output location does not change the input files being read.

choices.text: Overwrite all months to the same S3 key and have the flow read the latest content.
choices.explanation: The input for the explicitly specified month cannot be selected per run, and the same definition cannot be safely run for multiple periods in parallel.

learning.reason: Parameterizing the date in the S3 input path lets each run select a different period while preserving the transformation definition.
learning.concept: Parameterizing an input path in Data Wrangler

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Evaluating the Difference in Observed Label Rates Before Training
prompt: In an environment where SageMaker Clarify is available, you review the labels of two groups before training. Group A has 60 positive labels out of 100 people, and group D has 80 positive labels out of 200 people. What value represents the difference in positive-label rates between the groups as DPL?

choices.explanation: This is the ratio of A's positive-label rate to D's, not the difference.
The difference between A's 60% positive-label rate and D's 40% rate is 20 percentage points.
This results from subtracting A from D, but the formula here subtracts D from A.
This is the simple difference in the numbers of positive labels, 60 and 80, and does not account for the different group sizes.

learning.reason: DPL calculates the observed positive-label rate for each group and subtracts D from A. Here, the calculation is 0.60−0.40.
learning.concept: Difference in observed positive-label rates

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Temporarily Loading Archived Training Data
prompt: To reproduce a previous training result, you need to read an original S3 Glacier Deep Archive object from an S3 training pipeline for only three days. The original data must remain in the same archive class even after a temporary copy is made. Which procedure is appropriate?

choices.text: Copy the object directly to S3 Standard with CopyObject, then start training.
choices.explanation: The Deep Archive object must be restored before it can be copied, and a permanent copy in the Standard class is not required.

choices.text: Add s3:GetObject to the training job's execution role.
choices.explanation: Read permission alone is insufficient; archived data must first undergo a restore operation.

choices.text: Use RestoreObject to set a three-day restore retention period, then retrieve the object after the restore is complete.
choices.explanation: The restored temporary copy can be retrieved during the specified period, while the S3 archive class itself remains unchanged.

choices.text: Run GetObject immediately after a HEAD request succeeds.
choices.explanation: Retrieving metadata does not mean that temporary restoration of the archived data has completed.

learning.reason: Deep Archive objects become temporarily readable after a restore request, while the original archived object retains its storage class.
learning.concept: Temporary restoration of archived training files

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Applying a Directional Constraint to a Risk Feature in XGBoost
prompt: In a loan-risk model, you must enforce a business constraint during training that the predicted risk must not decrease as the number of days delinquent increases. Which option should you use?

choices.text: Configure endpoint autoscaling.
choices.explanation: This does not constrain the model function.

choices.text: Set a positive monotonic constraint on the delinquency-days feature with XGBoost's monotone_constraints.
choices.explanation: This constrains the directional relationship between the feature and the prediction in the learned trees.

choices.text: Randomly reorder the predictions after inference.
choices.explanation: This does not impose a directional constraint during training.

choices.text: Make max_depth unlimited.
choices.explanation: This does not guarantee monotonicity.

learning.reason: XGBoost's monotone_constraints defines a directional constraint for each feature.
learning.concept: XGBoost monotone constraints

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Specifying the Business Problem Type for AutoML
prompt: You provide AutoML V2 with tabular data containing a binary label that indicates whether a purchase occurred. You want it to generate candidates using classification metrics without trying regression candidates. Which option should you use?

choices.text: Convert the input label to an integer and omit ProblemType.
choices.explanation: This delegates detection to Autopilot and does not fix the experiment to the specified problem type.

choices.text: Select a text-classification configuration in CreateAutoMLJobV2.
choices.explanation: The input contract is different. You need to specify a configuration for tabular feature columns and a binary label.

choices.text: Set BinaryClassification in CreateAutoMLJobV2's TabularJobConfig.ProblemType.
choices.explanation: For tabular data, this fixes the supervised problem type for candidate models to binary classification.

choices.text: Set Regression in TabularJobConfig.ProblemType.
choices.explanation: Even if the label is 0 or 1, a regression configuration does not specify exploration as a probabilistic binary-classification problem.

learning.reason: Autopilot V2 lets you specify binary classification and other problem types with ProblemType.
learning.concept: Autopilot V2 problem type

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Warm-start AMT from the same problem configuration
prompt: You want to reuse the previous AMT results with the same features, objective metric, and training data to shorten additional hyperparameter exploration. Which option should you use?

choices.text: Use a job with a different problem type as the parent.
choices.explanation: The exploration results cannot be safely reused.

choices.text: Use an endpoint configuration as the parent job.
choices.explanation: This is not the history of a tuning job.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail for warm start.
choices.explanation: This does not specify a parent AMT job.

choices.text: Use WarmStartConfig to specify the previous tuning job as the parent while maintaining the same problem configuration.
choices.explanation: AMT can warm-start from a compatible parent job.

learning.reason: WarmStartConfig reuses the results of a compatible tuning job.
learning.concept: SageMaker AMT warm start

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Verify the required model license before fine-tuning
prompt: You will fine-tune a foundation model suitable for your organization's use case in JumpStart in SageMaker Studio. The model requires explicit EULA acceptance before training. After your organization has completed its license review, which procedure should you follow in Studio?

choices.text: Submit the fine-tuning job, then review and accept the displayed model EULA.
choices.explanation: For models that require acceptance, Studio requests explicit acceptance of the displayed license before training starts.

choices.text: After training completes, tag the generated model's metadata as EULA accepted.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the EULA acceptance required before training starts, and a tag cannot replace acceptance in Studio.

choices.text: Expand the S3 permissions of the training execution role and run the job again.
choices.explanation: Data access permissions are separate from accepting the model license before training.

choices.text: Open the link in the model description and omit EULA acceptance in Studio.
choices.explanation: Reviewing the description alone does not complete the explicit acceptance required by the model.

learning.reason: For a JumpStart model that requires explicit EULA acceptance, review the use and terms after organizational approval and accept the EULA in Studio before training.
learning.concept: JumpStart license acceptance

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Discover topics in unlabeled documents
prompt: Customer free-text responses have no predefined categories. You want to extract frequently occurring latent topics and create a classification taxonomy later. Which option should you use?

choices.text: Use endpoint autoscaling.
choices.explanation: It does not train a topic model.

choices.text: Use SageMaker Neural Topic Model for unsupervised topic inference.
choices.explanation: It can infer latent topics in a document collection without supervision.

choices.text: Use BlazingText supervised.
choices.explanation: It requires ground-truth labels.

choices.text: Use linear regression.
choices.explanation: It is not used for document topic inference.

learning.reason: NTM provides unsupervised topic modeling.
learning.concept: SageMaker NTM

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Choose Linear Learner to meet a target recall during training
prompt: For a binary-classification Linear Learner model with validation data, you want to automatically select the candidate with the highest precision while targeting 80% recall. Which training-time evaluation setting should you use?

choices.text: Set binary_classifier_model_selection_criteria to accuracy.
choices.explanation: This compares the proportion of correct predictions among all predictions. It does not maximize precision subject to a target recall.

choices.text: Set binary_classifier_model_selection_criteria to f_beta without specifying a recall target.
choices.explanation: This compares the harmonic mean of precision and recall. It does not maximize precision under a specified recall constraint.

choices.text: Set binary_classifier_model_selection_criteria to precision_at_target_recall and set target_recall to 0.8.
choices.explanation: This supplies a recall target and compares candidate precision under that condition.

choices.text: Set binary_classifier_model_selection_criteria to recall_at_target_precision and set target_precision to 0.8.
choices.explanation: The 80% target becomes precision, and recall becomes the metric being maximized.

learning.reason: When selecting precision_at_target_recall, provide target_recall. With recall_at_target_precision, the target metric and the metric being maximized are reversed.
learning.concept: Linear Learner target precision and recall

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Evaluating probability predictions with log loss
prompt: In binary churn classification, the candidate models have nearly identical accuracy on the validation data, but you want to penalize candidates that assign high probabilities to incorrect predictions. Inference must also produce the probability of churn. How should you configure the XGBoost objective and validation metric?

choices.text: Use binary:logistic and compare only the error rate at a fixed threshold.
choices.explanation: The error rate alone does not distinguish how much probability was assigned within the same set of misclassifications.

choices.text: Use multi:softmax and compare only the accuracy of the classification labels.
choices.explanation: This compares class labels but does not evaluate how confidently the probabilities were assigned.

choices.text: Compare only the inference invocation time of the binary classification models.
choices.explanation: This measures operational performance, not the magnitude of errors in probability predictions.

choices.text: Use binary:logistic and compare logloss on the validation data.
choices.explanation: It outputs binary probabilities, and log loss increases when a prediction assigns a high probability to the wrong class.

learning.reason: binary:logistic produces binary-class probabilities, and log loss evaluates the magnitude of the probability assigned to an incorrect prediction.
learning.concept: XGBoost binary probability output and log loss

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Retesting a time series with rolling-origin backtesting
prompt: You will deploy a monthly demand forecast for the following month. You want to prevent future data from entering training and evaluate stability at multiple forecast origin points. Which approach should you use?

choices.text: Use rolling-origin backtesting: train on the data available up to each point and validate on the next period.
choices.explanation: It preserves time order and evaluates multiple forecast origin points.

choices.text: Randomly divide the entire period into k folds.
choices.explanation: Future information can enter the training data.

choices.text: Train only on the last month.
choices.explanation: This discards the available history.

choices.text: Reverse the data in date order.
choices.explanation: This does not reproduce the operational time series.

learning.reason: Time-series evaluation must not include data from after the forecast point in training.
learning.concept: Rolling-origin backtesting

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Exploring discrete optimizer candidates with HPO
prompt: You want to choose an optimizer from adam, sgd, and rmsprop rather than tune a learning rate. Which HPO configuration lists the candidates without interpolating them over a continuous range or logarithmic scale?

choices.text: Configure endpoint autoscaling.
choices.explanation: This does not change the HPO candidates.

choices.text: List the candidate strings in a categorical parameter range.
choices.explanation: This allows the discrete candidates to be explored individually.

choices.text: Set a continuous range to logarithmic.
choices.explanation: This is intended for continuous numeric ranges.

choices.text: Use optimizer as the artifact name.
choices.explanation: This does not define the search space.

learning.reason: A categorical range defines discrete hyperparameter candidates.
learning.concept: HPO categorical range

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Combining multiple tabular models into one candidate
prompt: For a tabular purchase prediction task, you want Autopilot to build an ensemble that stacks predictions from multiple algorithms. The team does not want to maintain custom training code or prediction-combination code. Which training mode should you explicitly select?

choices.text: Choose the time-series forecasting setting and ignore the tabular features.
choices.explanation: This setting handles date-based series and differs from combining multiple classifiers for a tabular purchase prediction task.

choices.text: Assume that Automatic mode always uses an ensemble regardless of the input size.
choices.explanation: Automatic mode selects an approach based on conditions, so it does not meet the requirement to explicitly specify an ensemble.

choices.text: Choose Ensembling mode.
choices.explanation: AutoGluon trains multiple base models and combines their predictions using stacking.

choices.text: Choose Hyperparameter Optimization mode and adopt only the top-ranked single model.
choices.explanation: It can find hyperparameters for individual models, but it does not meet the requirement to stack multiple models.

learning.reason: Autopilot's Ensembling mode generates a stacked candidate from multiple base models for tabular data.
learning.concept: Autopilot Ensembling mode

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Training Sparse Categorical Interactions with Factorization Machines
prompt: In click-through prediction for advertisements, one-hot features for user IDs and product IDs are extremely sparse, but their interactions are important. Which option should be used?

choices.text: Use PCA only
choices.explanation: PCA is not a click classifier.

choices.text: Use Random Cut Forest
choices.explanation: Random Cut Forest is intended for anomaly detection.

choices.text: Increase the number of endpoints
choices.explanation: This does not train feature interactions.

choices.text: Use SageMaker Factorization Machines
choices.explanation: It can efficiently learn feature interactions from sparse features.

learning.reason: Factorization Machines are suitable for learning interactions in high-dimensional sparse data.
learning.concept: Factorization Machines

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Selecting a Clarify SHAP Baseline from a Representative Customer Group
prompt: SageMaker Clarify can be used for existing customers. You want to explain a contract-renewal model by showing differences from representative customers with the same contract type. Select two preparations that align the subject of the analysis with the comparison baseline.

choices.text: Use the number of endpoints as the baseline
choices.explanation: The number of endpoints is not a comparison baseline for explanations.

choices.text: Specify a baseline dataset that represents the operational population
choices.explanation: This makes the SHAP comparison baseline representative of the real population.

choices.text: Use the same feature-column schema for the baseline as for the inference input
choices.explanation: This aligns the analysis subject with the comparison baseline.

choices.text: Unconditionally use only rows containing all zeros as the baseline every time
choices.explanation: Such rows may not represent a realistic customer baseline.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail logs as the baseline
choices.explanation: CloudTrail logs are not model feature data.

learning.reason: A Clarify SHAP baseline should use representative data with a schema aligned to the inference input.
learning.concept: SageMaker Clarify SHAP baseline

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Using an Upper Demand Quantile to Match Stockout Costs
prompt: For retail inventory planning, you obtain this week's demand forecast from DeepAR after training across stores. Because the cost of insufficient demand coverage is higher than the cost of excess inventory, you use the 90th percentile for each forecast day in replenishment calculations. What should you change in the request and response?

choices.text: Specify 0.9 for quantiles in the request configuration and retrieve the corresponding forecast series.
choices.explanation: The model's probabilistic forecast can return a series for the 90th percentile.

choices.text: Extract only the point forecast mean and multiply every forecast value by 0.9.
choices.explanation: Multiplying the mean by a constant does not produce the 90th percentile of the forecast distribution.

choices.text: Request the 0.1 quantile and use the response as is.
choices.explanation: This is the lower quantile, which is the opposite side from the requested 90th percentile.

choices.text: Change num_samples to 90 and output only the mean.
choices.explanation: Changing the number of samples does not specify the target quantile.

learning.reason: With DeepAR, specify quantiles in the configuration to retrieve quantile forecasts for each time point in the response.
learning.concept: DeepAR probabilistic quantile output

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Converting Inference Coordinates to the Same Format as Validation Labels
prompt: You are evaluating an object detection model with SageMaker Object Detection - MXNet. The predictions contain normalized left, top, right, and bottom coordinates, whereas the ground-truth labels are stored as pixel-based left, top, width, and height values within the image. How should you compare the predicted and ground-truth overlap in the same image coordinate system?

choices.text: Compare the label's left, width, top, and height values with the predictions after only reordering them.
choices.explanation: The difference between normalized and pixel units, as well as the difference between endpoint and dimension formats, remains.

choices.text: Multiply the predicted left and right by the image width and the predicted top and bottom by the image height to obtain endpoints, then calculate width and height from the differences.
choices.explanation: This converts normalized coordinates to pixels and transforms them into the same left, top, width, and height format as the labels.

choices.text: Multiply only the predicted right and bottom by the image dimensions and use them directly as width and height.
choices.explanation: This does not subtract the left and top endpoints and confuses positions with width and height.

choices.text: Multiply the confidence score in the prediction response by the image width and image height instead of using the image dimensions.
choices.explanation: Confidence is a prediction score, not a scale for converting coordinates to pixels.

learning.reason: Right and bottom are endpoint positions, while width and height are the differences between the two endpoints. Use the image dimensions to align coordinate units before comparison.
learning.concept: Normalized coordinates and pixel bounds in object detection

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Reduce Training Time Consumed by Tuning
prompt: There are many neural-network tuning candidates, and assigning the same maximum training resources to every candidate would leave insufficient computing time. Choose a strategy that compares evaluations during training, stops candidates with low potential, and redirects training resources to promising candidates. Which AMT setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Increase the number of combinations with a Grid search and make each trial return only its final value.
choices.explanation: Without intermediate results, it is not possible to decide which candidates are promising and redirect resources to them.

choices.text: Stop tuning and only increase the number of instances in the prediction endpoint.
choices.explanation: This increases inference capacity but does not allocate computing resources for developing model candidates.

choices.text: Choose Hyperband and configure jobs to report intermediate objective metrics.
choices.explanation: Candidates can be compared using intermediate metrics, and the decision to continue training can be based on their performance.

choices.text: Use a random search and assign the same maximum number of epochs to every candidate.
choices.explanation: Candidates can be selected randomly, but running every candidate through the maximum number of epochs does not allow time to be allocated based on intermediate performance.

learning.reason: Hyperband uses intermediate evaluations to stop poorly performing candidates early and adjust resource allocation across the search.
learning.concept: Candidate allocation with SageMaker AMT Hyperband

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Adjust the Number of Samples in the k-NN Training Index
prompt: With SageMaker built-in k-NN, you want to keep the existing number of neighbors used for prediction unchanged. At the same time, you want to include more training examples in the index built from a subset of the original data and evaluate the effect on validation accuracy and size. Which parameter should you change?

choices.text: Increase only k.
choices.explanation: This changes the number of neighbors used for prediction; it does not change the number of samples used as input to the training index.

choices.text: Switch predictor_type from classifier to regressor.
choices.explanation: This changes the type of prediction problem and is unrelated to increasing the sample count.

choices.text: Lower dimension_reduction_target.
choices.explanation: This changes the feature dimension of each sample. It does not specify the number of samples passed to the index.

choices.text: Increase sample_size.
choices.explanation: This increases the number of training samples used for the index while leaving k at its current value for prediction.

learning.reason: k is the number of neighbors consulted during prediction. sample_size specifies the number of training data points sampled before the index is created.
learning.concept: The number of neighbors and index sampling in k-NN

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Place Custom Training Container Files in the Appropriate Locations
prompt: You are creating training code in a custom SageMaker container. Match each local path managed by the platform with its purpose. Use each candidate exactly once.

choices.text: /opt/ml/model
choices.explanation: This path stores the final model that is passed to hosting after training finishes.

choices.text: /opt/ml/input/data/train
choices.explanation: This path provides access to the data in the input channel named train.

choices.text: /opt/ml/output/data
choices.explanation: This path can contain outputs such as diagnostic reports, separately from the final model.

choices.text: /opt/ml/checkpoints
choices.explanation: For a job configured with S3 checkpoints, this path synchronizes the state needed to resume training.

learning.reason: Training inputs, the final model, diagnostic artifacts, and resume checkpoints are handled in separate paths according to the configuration.
learning.concept: The path contract inside a SageMaker training container

prompts.text: Read the train input channel delivered from S3.
Save the resume state configured for S3 synchronization.
Save the final model that will be passed to inference.
Output training diagnostic reports separately from the final model.

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Override an Environment Value at Runtime
prompt: You want to use the same SageMaker Pipeline while changing only the output S3 URI at runtime between development and production. Which method is appropriate?

choices.text: Manually edit the Pipeline definition every time.
choices.explanation: This sacrifices reusability.

choices.text: Retrain the model.
choices.explanation: This does not change the output URI.

choices.text: Delete the logs.
choices.explanation: This does not configure an environment value.

choices.text: Define a Pipeline parameter and override its value with StartPipelineExecution.
choices.explanation: Correct. Parameters can be specified at runtime.

learning.reason: Pipeline parameters allow values to be supplied at runtime.
learning.concept: Overriding Pipeline environment parameters at runtime

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Cache and Reuse the Same Preprocessing
prompt: A Pipeline is run repeatedly with the same inputs and settings. You want to reuse the Processing results for a limited period and rerun the step after the period expires. Which setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Enable step cache and set an ExpireAfter TTL.
choices.explanation: Correct. You can configure the cache expiration period.

choices.text: Delete S3.
choices.explanation: The results cannot be reused.

choices.text: Stop logging.
choices.explanation: This does not reuse the step results.

choices.text: Change the model name.
choices.explanation: This does not configure a TTL.

learning.reason: SageMaker Pipelines provides step cache and ExpireAfter.
learning.concept: Managing the TTL for Pipeline step cache

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Reduce Initial Latency for a Serverless Endpoint
prompt: Only the first request in the morning is slow on a SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint. Which setting provides initialized capacity at a predictable start time?

choices.text: Change the temperature.
choices.explanation: This is unrelated to endpoint initialization.

choices.text: Configure Provisioned Concurrency.
choices.explanation: Correct. This reserves initialized concurrent capacity.

choices.text: Delete the logs.
choices.explanation: This does not reduce initial latency.

choices.text: Move the workload to Batch Transform.
choices.explanation: This does not suit real-time requests.

learning.reason: Serverless Inference supports configuring Provisioned Concurrency.
learning.concept: Mitigating cold starts for a serverless endpoint

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Run Preprocessing and Inference Sequentially
prompt: You want to run a classification model after normalizing text on a real-time endpoint. Which configuration passes the intermediate data without sending it to a separate endpoint?

choices.text: Invoke two models simultaneously.
choices.explanation: This does not guarantee that the input has been normalized first.

choices.text: Delete the logs.
choices.explanation: This does not configure sequential processing.

choices.text: Define the preprocessing and inference containers in order in a SageMaker Inference Pipeline.
choices.explanation: Correct. The output of one container can be passed sequentially to the next container.

choices.text: Send the intermediate data to CloudTrail.
choices.explanation: This is not an inference pipeline.

learning.reason: An Inference Pipeline runs multiple containers sequentially.
learning.concept: Sequencing preprocessing and model inference for real-time inference

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Explicitly Reference an Endpoint Configuration with IaC
prompt: You are creating a SageMaker endpoint with CloudFormation. Separate from approval of the registered model, you want to explicitly specify which EndpointConfig to use so that the deployment is reproducible. Which resource reference is appropriate?

choices.text: Specify only the model name for the endpoint.
choices.explanation: This does not specify the endpoint configuration.

choices.text: Reference CloudTrail logs.
choices.explanation: This is not an IaC configuration.

choices.text: Overwrite the artifacts.
choices.explanation: This reduces configuration reproducibility.

choices.text: Reference the EndpointConfig in EndpointConfigName of AWS::SageMaker::Endpoint.

learning.concept: Referencing an endpoint configuration with CloudFormation

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション

title: Start a Pipeline on a Schedule
prompt: Start a SageMaker Pipeline with StartPipelineExecution at a fixed time every Monday. Which configuration does so without changing the configuration of an always-running server whenever the date changes and without adding intermediary code?

choices.text: Use an EventBridge Scheduler SageMaker StartPipelineExecution target and grant the execution role permission to start the target pipeline.
choices.explanation: The managed schedule calls the API at the specified time, and the execution role authorizes starting the target pipeline.

choices.text: Modify the SageMaker TrainingStep to run once a week without configuring how to start the pipeline.
choices.explanation: A step runs within a pipeline execution. An execution that has not been started cannot be created by that step.

choices.text: Configure a training-completed EventBridge event as the start trigger.
choices.explanation: This condition runs when training is complete; it does not start a new execution at a weekly scheduled time.

choices.text: Describe the weekly start in the S3 data-retention period.
choices.explanation: S3 lifecycle rules configure actions such as object transitions. They do not start a SageMaker Pipeline at a specified time.

learning.reason: SageMaker Pipelines can be started by EventBridge.
learning.concept: Scheduled ML Pipeline orchestration with EventBridge

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Send Inference Requests to a Specified Variant
prompt: You want to integration-test only a specific production variant of the same endpoint. Which specification is appropriate?

choices.text: Delete S3.
choices.explanation: This does not select an inference destination.

choices.text: Specify TargetVariant in InvokeEndpoint.
choices.explanation: Correct. This selects a specific variant.

choices.text: Change only the model name.
choices.explanation: This does not select a variant.

choices.text: Delete the logs.
choices.explanation: This does not change traffic distribution.

learning.reason: TargetVariant specifies the production variant to invoke.
learning.concept: Explicit testing of an endpoint variant

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Rerun Only the Required Pipeline Steps After a Failure
prompt: In a SageMaker Pipeline, you want to use processed data from the previous successful execution and reevaluate later steps after changing the training configuration. How can you receive the outputs from a specified previous execution without running the earlier steps?

choices.text: Remove the earlier steps from the pipeline definition and leave the training input empty.
choices.explanation: This avoids rerunning the earlier steps, but it cannot reuse the previously processed data.

choices.text: Only increase the automatic retry count for failures.
choices.explanation: This does not create a configuration that specifies outputs from a previous pipeline execution and runs only the later steps with new settings.

choices.text: For Selective Execution, specify the source Pipeline execution and the later steps to rerun.
choices.explanation: Outputs from the source execution for steps that are not selected can be reused, and only the selected steps can be executed.

choices.text: Run a new full execution and only extend the step-cache TTL without specifying a source execution.
choices.explanation: This can reuse past artifacts when they match the cache key. It does not explicitly specify a source execution and selected steps.

learning.reason: Selective Execution can rerun a selected portion of a Pipeline execution.
learning.concept: Partial reruns of an ML Pipeline

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Balance Concurrent Requests and the Payload Limit in Batch Transform
prompt: In SageMaker Batch Transform, one record can be up to 20 MB and cannot be split. You must explicitly specify both MaxPayloadInMB and MaxConcurrentTransforms and increase the number of parallel requests on one instance. Which combination can process the largest record while meeting the service limit?

choices.text: Set MaxPayloadInMB to 20 and MaxConcurrentTransforms to 6.
choices.explanation: A 20-MB record fits, but the product is 120 MB, which exceeds the limit.

choices.text: Set MaxPayloadInMB to 15 and MaxConcurrentTransforms to 6.
choices.explanation: The product is 90 MB, but a 20-MB record does not fit within the payload setting for one request.

choices.text: Set MaxPayloadInMB to 50 and MaxConcurrentTransforms to 3.
choices.explanation: The record fits, but the product is 150 MB, which exceeds the limit.

choices.text: Set MaxPayloadInMB to 20 and MaxConcurrentTransforms to 5.
choices.explanation: A 20-MB record fits, and the product of the setting values is 100 MB, which does not exceed the limit.

learning.reason: MaxPayloadInMB must accommodate the largest input record, and its product with MaxConcurrentTransforms must be 100 MB or less.
learning.concept: SageMaker Batch Transform concurrency and payload limits

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Increasing the Copy Count of an Inference Component
prompt: An endpoint has separate Inference Components for two models, and only one model is experiencing an increasing processing backlog. Capacity is available, and you must add execution copies only for the target model without changing the copy count of the other model. Which API setting should you use?

choices.text: Specify the target InferenceComponentName and increase DesiredRuntimeConfig.CopyCount in UpdateInferenceComponentRuntimeConfig.
choices.explanation: The requested copy count can be applied to only one component.

choices.text: Lower the maximum shared token count for both models on the endpoint.
choices.explanation: This might change the amount of request processing, but it does not add execution copies for a specific model.

choices.text: Only specify the TargetVariant on the caller side without changing the copy state.
choices.explanation: This selects the invocation target; it does not change the copy count of any component.

choices.text: Rewrite the displayed DesiredCopyCount value in the DescribeInferenceComponent response.
choices.explanation: Changing a displayed state does not send a request to the service to update the copy count.

learning.reason: UpdateInferenceComponentRuntimeConfig sets the execution copy count for the target component through DesiredRuntimeConfig.CopyCount.
learning.concept: Adjusting inference capacity at the component level

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Retrying a Training Step Only for Transient Internal Errors
prompt: A Training step in SageMaker Pipelines is designed to process the same input again. You want to retry up to three times with increasing intervals only when a transient SageMaker internal error occurs, while failing immediately for a data validation error in the training program. What should you configure?

choices.text: Extend the SageMaker training timeout and continue waiting for the job that produced an internal error.
choices.explanation: Increasing the execution time limit does not restart a failed step.

choices.text: Configure the Training step's RetryPolicy for SageMaker.JOB_INTERNAL_ERROR, including the retry count, interval, and backoff.
choices.explanation: The step is retried automatically for the specified internal error and does not retry beyond the configured count.

choices.text: Enable caching for the preprocessing step.
choices.explanation: Caching reuses preprocessing artifacts; it does not classify and retry internal errors in the Training step.

choices.text: Always rerun the entire pipeline on a time-based schedule.
choices.explanation: This does not distinguish internal errors from data validation errors or control the steps in the current execution.

learning.reason: A RetryPolicy limited to the relevant exception type on the Training step distinguishes retries for internal errors from failures in the training program.
learning.concept: Retrying Training steps in SageMaker Pipelines

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Reducing Environment Preparation Time for Sequential Similar Training Jobs
prompt: Training jobs with the same instance type and count and compatible configurations run sequentially a few minutes apart. You want to keep the training work for every trial while reducing only the preparation of a new environment each time. Managed Warm Pools are available in the account. Which method should you choose?

choices.text: Keep the training output in S3 and skip subsequent jobs.
choices.explanation: Artifacts can be reused, but this does not meet the requirement to run the training for subsequent trials.

choices.text: Switch each job to a different network configuration and let it select matching resources.
choices.explanation: The later job would no longer match the configuration of the earlier job and could not use the retained compute resources.

choices.text: Set KeepAlivePeriodInSeconds in the preceding job's ResourceConfig, then start a later job with a matching configuration within that period.
choices.explanation: The retained compute resources are reused by the later job, while the later job's training still runs.

choices.text: Enable Provisioned Concurrency for the inference endpoint.
choices.explanation: This reduces preparation for inference requests; it does not reuse a training environment.

learning.reason: Managed Warm Pools reuse the preceding job's execution resources when a later training job with a matching configuration starts within the retention period.
learning.concept: Managed Warm Pools between sequential training jobs

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Displaying Partial Results Before the Final Response
prompt: The model container for a SageMaker real-time endpoint generates partial results during processing and supports response streaming. The client must display each partial result as it arrives, before the final response is complete. Which invocation method should you choose?

choices.text: Use InvokeEndpoint and split the string on the display side after receiving the response.

choices.text: Use InvokeEndpointAsync and read the result from S3 after the job completes.
choices.explanation: The request can be processed asynchronously, but fragments of the inference result are not received sequentially in the same invocation.

choices.text: Periodically resend the same request to InvokeEndpoint and use the first response returned.
choices.explanation: This runs duplicate inferences and does not receive intermediate results within one invocation.

choices.text: Invoke the endpoint with InvokeEndpointWithResponseStream and process each received PayloadPart in order.
choices.explanation: The client reads the stream generated by the model and can display portions of the result as they arrive.

learning.reason: For a streaming-capable model, use InvokeEndpointWithResponseStream and process the payload in each received event as it arrives.
learning.concept: Response streaming from a real-time endpoint

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Create Neo artifacts for the target hosting instance
prompt: Using SageMaker Neo, compile a trained model for a new hosting instance. The input artifact is in S3. Arrange the steps for deploying the compiled artifact to a new inference endpoint in dependency order.

choices.text: Run a compilation job for the selected target using the original model as input, and wait for it to succeed.
choices.explanation: After it succeeds, an artifact for the new hosting instance is created.

choices.text: Deploy a model that references the compiled artifact to an endpoint on the selected instance.
choices.explanation: Deploy it after the compiled artifact becomes available.

choices.text: Confirm the supported framework and hosting instance, and determine the compilation target.
choices.explanation: Determining the target first ensures that compilation uses the same target as the deployment destination.

learning.reason: Compile with Neo for the same target as the deployment destination, then specify the resulting artifact for hosting on that instance.
learning.concept: Neo target matching and hosting

category: MLソリューションのモニタリング、保守、セキュリティ
examDomain: MLソリューションのモニタリング、保守、セキュリティ
title: Detect anomalies in inference load that varies by day of the week

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation
choices.explanation: Audit-log integrity does not detect seasonal anomalies in a metric.

choices.text: Retrain the model
choices.explanation: This does not configure invocation-volume monitoring.

choices.text: Configure a CloudWatch Anomaly Detection band for the metric
choices.explanation: Anomaly Detection can learn historical seasonal patterns in a metric and detect deviations from the expected range.

choices.text: Set the same static threshold for every day of the week
choices.explanation: This does not reflect different normal levels by day of the week, increasing false positives or missed anomalies.

learning.reason: CloudWatch Anomaly Detection provides a dynamic expected range based on the normal patterns in a time series.

categoryLabel: Monitoring, maintaining, and securing ML solutions
examDomainLabel: Monitoring, maintaining, and securing ML solutions

category: MLソリューションのモニタリング、保守、セキュリティ
examDomain: MLソリューションのモニタリング、保守、セキュリティ
title: Monitor an increase in invalid inference inputs
prompt: A SageMaker real-time endpoint's inference container is implemented to return a 4xx response when the request payload does not conform to the required JSON format. Which metric monitors the number of invocations for which the model returned such input errors during a given period?

choices.text: Monitor Invocation5XXErrors
choices.explanation: 5xx responses indicate a failure on the model or SageMaker side and differ from input-validation errors.

choices.text: Monitor ModelLatency
choices.explanation: Inference processing time does not indicate whether the request format is valid.

choices.text: Monitor the number of ECR images
choices.explanation: The number of images in a repository is unrelated to invocation input errors.

title: Reflecting Changes for the Same Customer in Individual Training Events
prompt: The same customer record is updated repeatedly within a short period. Feature generation must start processing within a few minutes, associate the before-and-after item images for each change, and record changes for the same customer in change order. How should the data be retrieved from DynamoDB?

choices.text: Scan the table every minute and calculate the difference from the previous result.
choices.explanation: If multiple changes occur between scans, the intermediate changes cannot be identified.

choices.text: Enable DynamoDB Streams with NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES and consume the stream.
choices.explanation: This provides the before-and-after state for each change, and events for the same item appear in change order.

choices.text: Use DynamoDB Streams with KEYS_ONLY and reread the current item when processing each event.
choices.explanation: The current value may include subsequent changes, so the before-and-after state at the time of each event cannot be obtained.

choices.text: Use only a daily incremental export and assume that every change during the period will appear.
choices.explanation: An incremental export retrieves the state of items that changed during a specified interval; it is not a method for processing each update image sequentially within a few minutes.

learning.reason: DynamoDB Streams records item changes. With NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES, the contents before and after an update are available, and changes to the same item retain their order.
