examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Registering a Delimited S3 Format Correctly in the Glue Catalog
prompt: Manufacturing equipment data is stored in S3. Columns are separated by semicolons, and every file has a header. Without rewriting the files, the organization wants a Glue crawler to catalog them with the correct columns for downstream feature generation. Which configuration should be selected?

choices.text: Create a custom CSV classifier specifying a semicolon delimiter and that a header is present, then associate it with the target crawler.
choices.explanation: The classifier can be given the assumptions about the target files and use them to infer the schema.

choices.text: Prefer the built-in Parquet classifier and change only the file extension to .parquet.
choices.explanation: The files remain delimited text files, so this does not provide Parquet types or metadata.

choices.text: Enable Glue job bookmarks and assume that the column delimiter will be communicated to the crawler.
choices.explanation: Bookmarks track input already read by a job; they do not change the classifier's file-format settings.

choices.text: Record the delimiter in S3 object tags and assume that this alone changes which columns the crawler reads.
choices.explanation: Storing a value in a tag does not make the crawler use that delimiter.

learning.reason: A Glue custom CSV classifier can explicitly define the delimiter and header conditions, and the crawler can use that classifier.
learning.concept: Custom CSV classifiers for Glue crawlers

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Converting Incoming JSON to a Columnar Format During Delivery
prompt: Event records arrive in Firehose as structured JSON. The training side reads only Parquet from Amazon S3. The existing Glue Data Catalog contains a table schema that matches the input, and you do not want to manage a Lambda function or ETL job for the conversion. Which configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Choose Parquet as the output format for S3 Inventory.
choices.explanation: The object listing becomes Parquet, but the file format of each received event is not converted.

choices.text: Enable format conversion for the S3 destination, and configure a JSON deserializer, the corresponding Glue table, and a Parquet serializer.
choices.explanation: This interprets the JSON according to the schema and converts it to Parquet before writing it to S3.

choices.text: Set Firehose compression to GZIP and add .parquet to the output name.
choices.explanation: Compression leaves the record structure as JSON; it does not create a columnar file.

choices.text: Use dynamic partitioning only to add the event type to the S3 prefix.
choices.explanation: This changes the destination layout, but the record files themselves do not become Parquet.

learning.reason: Firehose record format conversion combines JSON reading, a Glue Data Catalog schema, and serialization to Parquet during delivery.
learning.concept: Converting JSON to Parquet in Firehose

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Determining the Online Expiration Time for Late-Arriving Data
prompt: A value observed at 10:00 was registered in an online Feature Store at 10:40. The record's EventTime was set to the observation time, and the TTL was set to one hour. What is the reference time at which this value expires from the online store?

choices.explanation: This adds the TTL to the registration time, rather than calculating it using EventTime.
This adds two hours to EventTime at 10:00, exceeding the configured TTL by one hour.
This adds one hour to the 10:00 EventTime.
This is the registration time, and the record's configured validity period has not yet elapsed.

learning.reason: TTL is based on the record's EventTime. Even if the event arrives or is registered late, the reference time does not shift to the registration time.
learning.concept: Event-time-based TTL in Feature Store

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Selecting a Validation Sample That Includes Small Categories
prompt: You are preprocessing data in SageMaker Data Wrangler, with different numbers of records for each delivery region. To inspect the transformation results locally, you want to select a small number of rows while approximately preserving the regional composition of the original data and avoiding bias within each region. Which sampling method should you use?

choices.text: Retrieve only the specified number of rows from the beginning of the file.
choices.explanation: If the input is ordered by region, this biases the sample toward the rows from the first region.

choices.text: Sample from the entire dataset with the same probability regardless of region, assuming that smaller regions are always included.
choices.explanation: With a small sample, simple random sampling can omit rare strata.

choices.text: Increase every region to the same number of records and use the entire result as the validation data.
choices.explanation: This changes the original regional composition and does not meet the requirement to limit the sample to a small number of rows.

choices.text: Perform stratified random sampling using the region column.
choices.explanation: This selects samples from each stratum while preserving the composition across regions.

learning.reason: Stratified sampling defines strata using values such as region and can sample so that the distribution of the original strata is represented.
learning.concept: Stratified sampling and validation subsets

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Creating the Previous Value Without Mixing Equipment Histories
prompt: You have evenly spaced measurement data for each equipment ID, with multiple pieces of equipment mixed in the same file. You want to create an input column containing the previous measurement for the same equipment that was already available at prediction time. Which transformation should you use in Data Wrangler?

choices.text: Split the time series by equipment ID and create a one-step lag of the measurement values in time order.
choices.explanation: This uses a past value from the specified series, without crossing equipment boundaries or using the next measurement.

choices.text: Combine all equipment and sort by time, then use the immediately preceding row.
choices.explanation: If consecutive rows belong to different equipment, a value from another piece of equipment is introduced.

choices.text: Split by equipment ID, but use the value one row after the current row.
choices.explanation: This depends on a future measurement that may not yet be known at prediction time.

choices.text: Copy the maximum value from the entire period for each equipment to every row.
choices.explanation: The maximum over the entire period is not the previous value and may depend on a future observation.

learning.reason: Applying lag features to a time-ordered series adds a past value from the same series to the current row.
learning.concept: Equipment-specific time-series lag features

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Recover Without Resending Successful Kinesis Records
prompt: A producer sends 100 records to Kinesis PutRecords. The HTTP response is successful, but only the result corresponding to one input reports temporary throttling. How should the producer recover the unaccepted records without resending records that are confirmed successful?

choices.text: Compress the record results and update only metrics without checking for failures.
choices.explanation: The monitoring values can be updated, but the inputs that were not accepted are not resent.

choices.text: Map each result's ErrorCode to its input and resend only the failed records with backoff.
choices.explanation: This identifies the outcome of each record and avoids unnecessarily resending records that succeeded this time.

choices.text: Treat all 100 records as successful because the response was an HTTP success.
choices.explanation: Individual input results can include failures, causing unaccepted events to be lost.

choices.text: Send all 100 records again with the same keys.
choices.explanation: Records that previously succeeded would also be sent again as new records.

learning.reason: PutRecords returns a result for each record in the same order as the inputs. The indexes of failed records can be used to resend only the unaccepted records.
learning.concept: Partial failure and resend granularity in PutRecords

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Expose a Dedicated Training-Material Location to Existing SFTP Users
prompt: External contractors using an existing AWS Transfer Family deployment should see only their own material-upload location as the SFTP root. All contractors use different prefixes in the same S3 bucket, and the bucket name must not be exposed to the SFTP client. Which two settings should be selected?

choices.text: Set the home directory to LOGICAL and map the root to each contractor's S3 prefix.
choices.explanation: The client sees a logical root that resolves to the path assigned to that user.

choices.text: Restrict the S3 permissions used by Transfer Family for each contractor's connection to the assigned upload location.
choices.explanation: In addition to the mapping, this limits actual S3 operations to the contractor's permitted scope.

choices.text: Set the home directory to PATH and configure the bucket root for everyone.
choices.explanation: This exposes the physical S3 path and does not provide a user-specific logical root.

choices.text: Use S3 events to identify the contractor and move the file after upload.
choices.explanation: This does not configure the initial SFTP root or the boundary at upload time.

choices.text: Give everyone unrestricted S3 access through a shared role and retain only transfer-operation logs.
choices.explanation: Logs support after-the-fact review but do not enforce the required permission boundary.

learning.reason: Transfer Family assigns the logical path that is displayed, while the actual permissions to S3 must also be restricted to each contractor's upload location.
learning.concept: Transfer Family logical roots and S3 permissions

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Rename Columns Without Rewriting Parquet
prompt: Athena reads Parquet files containing machine-learning features. The table is unpartitioned, and all files have the same column order and data types. The logical table column names must change without changing their positions or rewriting the existing files. Which setting is required?

choices.text: Keep the same SerDe configuration, move the column to the beginning, and then rename it.
choices.explanation: Changing the column position violates the condition that it be read from its original position, and it does not resolve the name mapping.

choices.text: Change the key names of the S3 objects.
choices.explanation: An S3 key name is not a Parquet internal column name or a catalog schema name.

choices.text: Use a table with parquet.column.index.access set to true and change the logical name without changing the column position.
choices.explanation: Because the column position rather than the physical file column name is used, the logical name can change without rewriting the files.

choices.text: Keep Parquet's default name-based access and change only the column name in the catalog.
choices.explanation: The new name would no longer correspond to the physical column name in the existing files.

learning.reason: Athena uses column names for Parquet by default. When the column order is guaranteed to be the same, index-based access allows the files to be read independently of the logical names.
learning.concept: Parquet name-based access and index-based access

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Compare a Sharp Daily Data Drop with the Recent Trend
prompt: A Glue ETL job ingests training data every day. Because the absolute count changes seasonally, the quality gate should fail when the count is at or below 80% of the average RowCount from the most recent seven runs. Which DQDL rule should be used?

choices.text: RowCount > last() * 0.8
choices.explanation: This uses only the immediately preceding run and does not use the seven-run average.

choices.text: RowCount > 7 * 0.8
choices.explanation: The threshold is fixed and does not adapt to the historical row-count trend.

choices.text: Set IsComplete only on the training-label column.
choices.explanation: This checks for missing values but does not compare for a sharp decrease in input count.

choices.text: RowCount > avg(last(7)) * 0.8
choices.explanation: This uses the average count from the most recent seven runs as the threshold baseline.

learning.reason: In Glue ETL dynamic DQDL rules, last retrieves previous values of the same metric and avg creates a recent baseline.
learning.concept: Dynamic DQDL rules for row counts

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Separating Unconvertible Events for Investigation in S3
prompt: Firehose converts JSON to Parquet and delivers it to S3. You want to separate records that fail conversion from the prefix for valid Parquet files and analyze them from locations organized by failure type. Which setting should you use?

choices.text: Include the firehose:error-output-type expression in ErrorOutputPrefix to store failed results by type.
choices.explanation: The conversion error type is reflected in the S3 key, distinguishing failed outputs from the normal delivery destination.

choices.text: Only append a date-and-time expression to the Prefix for successful records.
choices.explanation: This organizes records by arrival time but does not configure an output destination for records that fail conversion.

choices.text: Disable Parquet grouping and convert failed records to normal Parquet.
choices.explanation: The input schema requirements for conversion do not change, and this does not separate records for error investigation.

choices.text: Add invalid records one at a time to a Glue table and leave the Firehose configuration unchanged.
choices.explanation: This does not configure failure output for auditing and instead changes the schema intended for valid data.

learning.reason: Use the S3 error output prefix to separate records by error type, including conversion errors, based on the value of error-output-type.
learning.concept: Firehose error output prefixes for failed records

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Locking the Specific Version of Evidence Used for Training
prompt: Auditable training data is stored in versioned S3. You must set a seven-year retention period for the target object version and prevent administrators, including the root user, from shortening that period. Which retention setting should you use?

choices.text: Configure deletion after seven years with Lifecycle.
choices.explanation: Lifecycle defines an action after the specified period but does not prevent individual deletion before then.

choices.text: Set the retention period for the target version in Object Lock Compliance mode.
choices.explanation: This sets a retention period on the object version and prevents even administrators from shortening it while protection is active.

choices.text: Use Governance mode and assume that administrators with bypass permissions cannot shorten the period.
choices.explanation: A principal with bypass permissions and an appropriate request can override a Governance retention setting.

choices.text: Configure only a Legal Hold and assume that administrators with permission to release it cannot shorten the period.
choices.explanation: A Legal Hold has no fixed retention period and can be released by a principal with the required permissions.

learning.reason: Object Lock Compliance mode prevents shortening the retention period of a protected version and prevents deletion or overwrite during the protection period.
learning.concept: S3 Object Lock Compliance mode retention

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Using Product-Specific Sentiment as Features from the Same Review
prompt: You are processing English product reviews for training. A single review can contain both evaluations, such as “the camera is good, but the battery is disappointing,” and you need to structure whether the writer is positive or negative about the camera and battery separately. Which analysis should you select in Amazon Comprehend?

choices.text: Use entity detection to extract the mentioned target names and use only their presence or absence for evaluation.
choices.explanation: This can extract the targets but does not provide positive or negative sentiment for each target.

choices.text: Use key phrase detection to extract phrases and treat a frequently mentioned target as positive.
choices.explanation: Frequency does not measure sentiment direction, so a frequently criticized target would receive the same classification.

choices.text: Apply Targeted sentiment to the English reviews and use the sentiment for each mention of each entity.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes the evaluations of different targets contained in the same review.

choices.text: Use standard sentiment analysis to label the entire review and assign the same value to both targets.
choices.explanation: Overall review sentiment cannot distinguish opposite evaluations of the individual targets.

learning.reason: Targeted sentiment identifies sentiment toward mentions of detected entities instead of estimating a single sentiment for the entire document.
learning.concept: Extracting entity-linked sentiment with Comprehend Targeted sentiment

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Passing Categorical Column Positions to CatBoost
prompt: The first column of the training CSV is the target variable, and you want to pass the third and fifth columns to SageMaker CatBoost as categorical features. The CSV has no header, and you can place the CSV and a configuration file under the training prefix. Select two appropriate settings.

choices.text: Add a header row indicating the types of the categorical columns to the beginning of each CSV.
choices.explanation: SageMaker CatBoost training CSV files have no header; categorical positions are specified in a separate configuration file.

choices.text: Place the configuration file only in the validation channel and point the training channel to individual CSV files.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the contract requiring the configuration to be specified under the same prefix as the training-channel input.

choices.text: In categorical_index.json under the training prefix, set cat_index_list to [2,4].
choices.explanation: Because indexing starts at zero, the third and fifth columns have indices 2 and 4.

choices.text: For the training channel, specify the S3 prefix containing the CSV and configuration file rather than the key of an individual CSV.
choices.explanation: CatBoost can detect the categorical-column configuration located with the data.

choices.text: Set cat_index_list to [3,5].
choices.explanation: These are one-based positions and do not match the required zero-based column indices.

learning.reason: Specify zero-based column positions in categorical_index.json. Index 0 is reserved for the first target-variable column, and the training channel references a prefix rather than a single file.
learning.concept: SageMaker CatBoost categorical column indices

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Choose an exploration strategy that uses past evaluations with few trials
prompt: Each Train trial takes a long time, and only a small number of trials can be run with AMT. Operationally, only one trial can run at a time, and you want to use the evaluation of a completed candidate when selecting the next candidate. No other tuning jobs from the past exist. Which exploration strategy should you choose?

choices.text: Choose Bayesian and set the maximum number of concurrent trials to 1.
choices.explanation: The results of trials that finish sequentially can be incorporated into the next candidate.

choices.text: Choose Random and set the maximum number of concurrent trials to 1, expecting past evaluations to guide the next random candidate.
choices.explanation: Reducing the number of concurrent trials does not cause Random to use each trial's result when selecting the next candidate.

choices.text: Choose Grid and process candidates sequentially from the predefined grid.
choices.explanation: This approach predetermines the combinations and does not propose the next point based on the accuracy of completed candidates.

choices.text: Use Warm Start and import results from a parent job even though no usable parent job exists.
choices.explanation: Because there is no other tuning job from which to start, results from a parent job cannot be imported.

learning.reason: Bayesian exploration selects the next candidate from the evaluation results of completed trials. This differs from a situation in which many trials are run in parallel because the computational budget constraints are different.
learning.concept: Sequential feedback in Bayesian exploration

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Train on image defects at the pixel level
prompt: You need to isolate defect regions in inspection photographs. Rather than only determining whether an image contains a defect or locating it with a bounding box, you want to estimate whether each pixel belongs to a defect or a normal area. Which ground-truth data should you prepare for supervised learning?

choices.text: Randomly overlay several images and label the resulting image as normal.
choices.explanation: This loses the teacher information for the defect class and its corresponding region.

choices.text: Create a PNG mask corresponding to each training image, with each pixel value representing the class ID for that location.
choices.explanation: Pixel-level ground-truth data enables the model to learn the classification boundaries at the pixel level.

choices.text: Assign one label per image indicating whether it contains a defect.
choices.explanation: This is ground-truth data for image-level classification and does not provide the defect's location or boundary.

choices.text: For each defect, provide only the left coordinate, top coordinate, width, and height of its bounding rectangle.
choices.explanation: This represents an approximate location, but does not identify which pixels inside the rectangle are defects.

learning.reason: Semantic segmentation uses a mask that assigns a class to each pixel at the same location as the training image.
learning.concept: Pixel masks for semantic segmentation

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Compare translation candidates using BLEU on the full validation set
prompt: You are training a Sequence-to-Sequence translation model in SageMaker. Validation checkpoints are compared using BLEU from actually decoding the validation sentences, not only token predictions during training. Choose two settings that use the entire validation set for each evaluation.

choices.text: Specify bleu for optimized_metric.
choices.explanation: This uses BLEU as the comparison metric during validation.

choices.text: Specify -1 for bleu_sample_size.
choices.explanation: This value uses all instances in the validation set.

choices.text: Set optimized_metric to perplexity and do not use validation BLEU for selection.
choices.explanation: The selection metric becomes the uncertainty of the language model's predictions, so decoded BLEU is not used for comparison.

choices.text: Change bleu_sample_size to 1.
choices.explanation: This specifies decoding only one item per evaluation and does not use the entire validation set.

choices.text: Only maximize max_seq_len_target and leave BLEU measurement at its default setting.
choices.explanation: Changing the output sequence length constraint does not specify the evaluation metric or the number of items decoded.

learning.reason: Setting optimized_metric to bleu and bleu_sample_size to -1 enables comparison using decoded results from the entire validation set.
learning.concept: The Seq2Seq BLEU metric and validation scope

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Use a known promotion schedule as a feature for DeepAR forecasting
prompt: You have trained DeepAR using whether a promotion is active as dynamic_feat. The demand history covers 60 days, the forecast period is 7 days, and the promotion schedule for the next 7 days is known. At inference time, how many values should you provide for the promotion feature?

choices.text: Provide only the seven future promotion-feature values and omit the historical values.
choices.explanation: Each dynamic feature also requires historical values covering the same period as the target history.

choices.text: Treat unobserved demand as actual demand and make target contain 67 values.
choices.explanation: Future promotions are known features; future demand does not need to be filled in as if it had already been observed.

choices.text: Concatenate the previous 60 days and the scheduled 7 days for the promotion feature, and provide 67 values.
choices.explanation: This satisfies the combined length of the target history and the forecast period.

choices.text: Provide only the 60 values corresponding to the historical period for the promotion feature.
choices.explanation: The feature values for the forecast interval would be missing, so the input contract of the trained model would not be satisfied.

learning.reason: DeepAR dynamic_feat covers the combined length of the historical target and the forecast interval; values for the forecast interval can be known exogenous variables.
learning.concept: The inference-time length of DeepAR dynamic_feat

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Interpreting the Nearest Cluster and Distance from Its Center
prompt: Normalized device features were input into SageMaker k-means. The operations dashboard displays which trained cluster is the closest and the degree of distance from its center. How should the response be interpreted?

choices.text: Display distance_to_cluster directly as a class-membership probability from 0 to 1.
choices.explanation: The distance from the cluster center represents a distance, not a probability, and it can exceed 1.

choices.text: Use closest_cluster as a continuous value representing the magnitude of a prediction error.
choices.explanation: The cluster number is an identifier; its numeric magnitude does not represent distance.

choices.text: Use distance_to_cluster to determine whether a true label matched.
choices.explanation: This is an unsupervised response and does not return the correct label for a target class.

choices.text: Use closest_cluster as the cluster identifier and distance_to_cluster as the distance to that cluster's center.
choices.explanation: The two response fields can be used to display the nearest group and its distance separately.

learning.reason: k-means returns the identifier of the nearest cluster and the distance to its center. The distance is not a class probability; it represents a positional relationship in the same feature space.
learning.concept: k-means cluster identifiers and distance

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Viewing How the Model's Average Response Changes at Different Feature Values
prompt: In an environment where SageMaker Clarify is available, you want to examine how the model responds to different shipping-cost levels. You want the predicted response for each shipping-cost value when the other inputs are averaged over the dataset distribution, rather than a contribution ranking for an individual order. Which analysis should you choose?

choices.text: Create a Partial Dependence Plot for shipping cost.
choices.explanation: This examines the model's response averaged over the other inputs as the shipping-cost value changes.

choices.text: Calculate the SHAP values for one order and treat them as the average response across the full shipping-cost range.
choices.explanation: These are contributions for an individual prediction, not responses averaged over the other inputs at separate feature values.

choices.text: Use Model Monitor only to examine drift in the input distribution for shipping cost.
choices.explanation: This can show whether the data distribution changed, but it does not show the model's average response at a specified level.

choices.text: Calculate only the median shipping cost in the dataset.
choices.explanation: This summarizes the input distribution but does not evaluate the model output.

learning.reason: A Partial Dependence Plot displays the average predicted response while varying the feature of interest and marginalizing over the other input features.
learning.concept: SageMaker Clarify Partial Dependence Plots

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Changing the Collective-Communication Backend in Existing PyTorch DDP
prompt: You will run a PyTorch DistributedDataParallel training script with a compatible SageMaker training image and GPU environment. You want to preserve the design that replicates the model on each GPU and use the SageMaker SMDDP library for collective communication. Choose two required changes.

choices.text: Specify smddp as the backend in torch.distributed.init_process_group.
choices.explanation: The process group will use the specified collective-communication implementation.

choices.text: Leave the backend unchanged and split only the model layers across different GPUs.
choices.explanation: This changes the computation approach to model parallelism, but it does not select a communication backend for DDP.

choices.text: Rename the directory used to save the final model to smddp.
choices.explanation: The output path is unrelated to registering the communication library or configuring the process group.

choices.text: Assume that no application-side backend specification is needed if the instance type supports GPUs.
choices.explanation: Choosing suitable hardware alone does not switch the PyTorch communication backend used by the existing code.

choices.text: Import smdistributed.dataparallel.torch.torch_smddp and register the backend.
choices.explanation: Importing the compatible library makes smddp available for selection in PyTorch.

learning.reason: Importing the SageMaker SMDDP client registers the smddp backend with PyTorch. Select it when initializing the process group.
learning.concept: Registering and initializing the SMDDP backend for PyTorch DDP

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Giving Rare Positive Examples More Weight in the Loss Calculation
prompt: In SageMaker Linear Learner, you are predicting machine failures and failure labels are very rare. Without duplicating training rows, you want misclassifying a failure to have a greater effect on the loss during training. Which binary-classification setting should you change?

choices.text: Change predictor_type to regressor.
choices.explanation: Changing the problem type does not provide a way to weight positive examples in the loss.

choices.text: Set positive_example_weight_mult to a value greater than 1.
choices.explanation: This gives positive examples greater weight in the training loss.

choices.text: Leave training and evaluation unchanged and lower only the threshold after deployment.
choices.explanation: This changes how many cases are classified as positive, but it does not change loss weights during training.

choices.text: Increase bias_wd_mult to apply stronger regularization only to the intercept.
choices.explanation: This controls regularization for the intercept and does not selectively increase the loss term for positive examples.

learning.reason: positive_example_weight_mult adjusts the weight of positive examples. It acts during training, unlike the decision threshold applied after training.
learning.concept: Linear Learner positive-example weighting

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Passing Per-Job Training Settings to a Custom Training Container
prompt: A training team specifies learning_rate and epochs for every CreateTrainingJob while using the same Docker image. The custom container reads the settings through SageMaker's standard file contract, so the image does not need to be rebuilt. Which method should be used?

choices.text: Read the job-specified learning rate from /opt/ml/model.
choices.explanation: This is the location for writing the final model, not for receiving the job's runtime settings.

choices.text: Fix both values when building the image and change to a different image for each job.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement to use runtime values with the same image.

choices.text: Specify the values in the job's HyperParameters and have the container read /opt/ml/input/config/hyperparameters.json.
choices.explanation: This keeps the same image and retrieves the per-run training values from the standard path.

choices.text: Read only /opt/ml/input/config/resourceconfig.json and assume that epochs is configured there.
choices.explanation: resourceconfig.json contains information about execution resources such as the hosts.

learning.reason: Hyperparameters passed through CreateTrainingJob can be read from hyperparameters.json in the training container's input configuration.
learning.concept: Configuration files for a custom SageMaker training container

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Explaining Why a Regression Model Performed Worse Than the Mean Prediction
prompt: A regression model has an R² of −0.3 on validation data. The variance of the observed values in the validation data is not zero. How should this result be explained in a model review?

choices.text: The mean of the predicted values was necessarily −0.3.
choices.explanation: R² does not report the value or unit of the mean prediction.

choices.text: It means that the model was wrong on 30% of the validation examples.
choices.explanation: R² is not a classification error rate. It evaluates the squared error of regression predictions against a baseline.

choices.text: The correlation coefficient between the true and predicted values is necessarily −0.3.
choices.explanation: R² compares residual error with a baseline error, so its value does not directly determine the correlation coefficient.

choices.text: The model's squared error is greater than that of a baseline that always predicts the observed mean of the validation data.
choices.explanation: The comparison for R² = 0 is a constant prediction of the mean. A negative value means that the residual sum of squares exceeds that baseline.

learning.reason: When the variance is nonzero, a negative R² means that the model's squared error was greater than that of a constant prediction based on the observed mean of the validation data.
learning.concept: Negative R² and the mean-value baseline

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Training on Multiple Labels That Can Apply Simultaneously to One Image
prompt: An equipment-maintenance photo can show rust and cracking at the same time. The presence or absence of each condition in each image is estimated with SageMaker Image Classification - MXNet. Which method represents each positive condition in the data without treating the conditions as mutually exclusive?

choices.text: Choose multilabel image classification and provide a multi-hot label with both elements corresponding to rust and cracking set to 1.
choices.explanation: This represents the presence of multiple conditions in one image as separate elements.

choices.text: Use single-label classification and keep only the first condition found when both appear in the image.
choices.explanation: The excluded condition is lost from the training label, so the model cannot learn each condition when they occur together.

choices.text: Use the average of the label numbers for rust and cracking as the regression target.
choices.explanation: This cannot represent the presence or absence of each condition independently.

choices.text: Provide only one normal or abnormal label for each image.
choices.explanation: This can represent whether an anomaly exists, but it cannot distinguish the two conditions.

learning.reason: A multilabel image-classification setup can use a multi-hot label when multiple conditions are positive in the same image.
learning.concept: Multi-hot labels in image classification

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Tracing the Data Used by a Deployed Model
prompt: After testing multiple model versions, a team needs to determine which data artifact produced the model currently used by a SageMaker endpoint. The training-name convention changed during the process, but the lineage relationships from that time were recorded. Which investigation should be performed?

choices.text: Infer which data artifact was used for training from the request count in CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: Inference-volume metrics do not include relationships to the training input.

choices.text: Start from the endpoint context, run an upstream lineage query, and inspect the related Dataset Artifact.
choices.explanation: This traces the training input through the recorded relationships without relying on naming conventions.

choices.text: Start from the endpoint and follow only downstream entities, then infer the training data from where the predictions were used.
choices.explanation: The training input is upstream of the deployment, so it cannot be traced by following only downstream entities.

choices.text: Assume that the latest S3 dataset was always used and adopt its key.
choices.explanation: The latest dataset and the input used by the deployed model may be different.

learning.reason: Following recorded lineage relationships upstream from a deployed context identifies the related model and training-input entities.
learning.concept: Upstream queries in SageMaker lineage

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Generating embeddings for out-of-vocabulary terms
prompt: An industrial equipment name is converted into an embedding using SageMaker BlazingText Word2Vec. During operation, a name that was not in the training vocabulary may appear, and you want to compute its vector using character subwords learned during training. Which training setting should you choose?

choices.text: Increase the word-frequency threshold and assume that unknown words will be added to the vocabulary.
choices.explanation: Increasing the frequency threshold removes low-frequency words; it does not add unknown words to the vocabulary after training.

choices.text: Switch from embeddings to supervised document classification.
choices.explanation: This predicts document classes and does not meet the requirement to generate a vector for an unknown individual word.

choices.text: Enable subwords in the applicable Word2Vec mode and train the model.
choices.explanation: The model can use character n-gram vectors, allowing it to represent an unknown word from known subwords.

choices.text: Do not use subwords during training and make the same string longer during inference.
choices.explanation: Because the model did not learn character n-gram embeddings, it cannot use them to construct an unknown word.

learning.reason: BlazingText trained with subwords enabled can generate a vector for a word outside the vocabulary by combining representations of its character n-grams.
learning.concept: BlazingText subword embeddings

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Reducing the dimensionality of wide, sparse features
prompt: You provide sparse training data with many features to SageMaker PCA. You want to avoid explicitly constructing the full covariance matrix and obtain the leading principal components, even if they are approximate. Which setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Run PCA in regular mode and assume that returning only the leading components avoids constructing the original covariance matrix.
choices.explanation: Limiting the number of output components does not change the fact that regular mode computes the covariance matrix.

choices.text: Replace each feature with the mean of its column.
choices.explanation: This removes the feature variance and eliminates the basis for computing principal components.

choices.text: Sort the training columns by name and use only the first columns.
choices.explanation: Column order does not reflect the data's variance structure and is not an approximation of the principal components.

choices.text: Set PCA's algorithm_mode to randomized.
choices.explanation: This selects an approximate computation for the leading principal components of high-dimensional data.

learning.reason: Regular mode computes the covariance matrix. Randomized mode uses an approximation and can make computing the leading components more efficient for high-dimensional data.
learning.concept: Randomized PCA for high-dimensional data

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Learning the relationship between search terms and documents in pairs
prompt: For an internal search system, you want to vectorize a short search term and a long document using separate processing. For training, you have pairs of search terms and documents, along with labels indicating whether each pair is related. Which architecture processes the two inputs with independent encoders and predicts the relationship between the pair?

choices.text: Pass the search term and document as a pair to Object2Vec, and train their respective encoders and comparator.
choices.explanation: Object2Vec can represent two inputs with different lengths or characteristics separately and output the strength of their relationship.

choices.text: Pass only the search terms to BlazingText word-embedding training and do not use the pair-relevance labels.
choices.explanation: This may produce word representations, but it does not learn the relationship between search-term and document pairs from those labels.

choices.text: Concatenate all inputs and treat them as one document, assuming that the two inputs are processed independently.
choices.explanation: This does not satisfy the requirement to process each input type independently.

choices.text: Cluster the documents with K-means and discard the search-term/document relevance labels.
choices.explanation: This is unsupervised grouping and does not train a comparator using the provided pair-relevance information.

learning.reason: Object2Vec passes two inputs to separate encoders and compares the resulting embeddings to learn the relationship between the pair.
learning.concept: Object2Vec dual inputs and comparator

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Distinguishing state, action, and reward in inventory-policy simulation
prompt: You simulate daily inventory replenishment on SageMaker. The learning agent receives observations, the agent chooses an order, and the simulator returns an evaluation based on costs after the action is executed. Match each item to its role in reinforcement learning.

choices.text: State
choices.explanation: This is information about the environment observed when the agent chooses an action.

choices.text: Action
choices.explanation: This is the decision selected by the agent based on its observation and passed to the environment.

choices.text: Reward
choices.explanation: This is a scalar evaluation of the result of an action, used to optimize the policy going forward.

learning.reason: The agent observes the state and chooses an action. The environment returns the next state and reward as the result of the action.
learning.concept: State, action, and reward in reinforcement learning

prompts.text: The inventory level and quantity awaiting replenishment on the decision date are passed to the agent.
The agent determines today's order quantity.
The environment adds the storage and stockout costs and returns the negative of that total.

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Change only capacity while preserving existing traffic weights during a model update
prompt: A running SageMaker endpoint sends traffic to variants A and B at a 70-to-30 ratio. You want to keep the variant names, update the model, and adopt only the instance counts from a new EndpointConfig. Which two UpdateEndpoint settings preserve the existing weights?

choices.text: Set RetainAllVariantProperties to false.
choices.explanation: This applies the configuration values without preserving the existing weights.

choices.text: Set TargetVariant on the client that makes the invocation, without changing the UpdateEndpoint settings.
choices.explanation: This sends client requests to a particular variant; it does not determine which values are retained during an update.

choices.text: Set RetainAllVariantProperties to true.
choices.explanation: This preserves properties such as the weights of the variants currently in service.

choices.text: Specify only DesiredInstanceCount in ExcludeRetainedVariantProperties.
choices.explanation: This excludes only the instance count from retention, so the instance count from the new configuration is used.

choices.text: Specify only DesiredWeight in ExcludeRetainedVariantProperties.
choices.explanation: The weights would be overwritten by the new configuration, which is the opposite of the requirement.

learning.reason: UpdateEndpoint can retain the properties of existing variants while excluding only DesiredInstanceCount from retention. This preserves the weights and uses the instance counts in the new configuration.
learning.concept: Inheriting variant properties during an endpoint update

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Set separate limits for queue time and processing time in asynchronous inference
prompt: In SageMaker asynchronous inference, requests that have not started running within 15 minutes of acceptance must expire. Requests that have started running may have up to 30 minutes of processing time. Which InvokeEndpointAsync settings meet these requirements?

choices.text: Set RequestTTLSeconds to 900 and InvocationTimeoutSeconds to 1800.
choices.explanation: These settings apply the required limits to queue time before execution starts and processing time after execution starts, respectively.

choices.text: Set RequestTTLSeconds to 1800 and InvocationTimeoutSeconds to 900.
choices.explanation: This reverses the limits for queue time and processing time.

choices.text: Set only RequestTTLSeconds to 2700.
choices.explanation: This allows a longer queue time and does not specify the separate 30-minute execution limit.

choices.text: Set the communication timeout for the client's submission API to 15 minutes.
choices.explanation: This controls only the submission request's communication timeout; it does not change the queue or processing deadlines for an accepted asynchronous request.

learning.reason: RequestTTLSeconds controls how long a request can wait in the queue, whereas InvocationTimeoutSeconds controls processing time after execution begins.
learning.concept: Queue time and execution time for asynchronous inference requests

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Wait for the initial load of a multi-model endpoint and retry
prompt: You send the first request to an infrequently accessed model on a SageMaker multi-model endpoint, and the response is ModelNotReadyException. The specified model key is correct, and model loading has started. How can you use the model without redeploying it?

choices.text: Remove the target name, make a prediction with a different model, and return that result as the output of the same model.
choices.explanation: This returns output from a model other than the one required.

choices.text: Retry the invocation of the same model with a limit and backoff configured.
choices.explanation: This retries a transient error a finite number of times while waiting for the model to become available.

choices.text: Immediately send the same request as a large number of parallel requests to force the load.
choices.explanation: Loading has already started, and repeated requests are likely to fail in the same state while adding unnecessary load.

choices.text: Duplicate the model under another key and recreate the endpoint every time.
choices.explanation: This adds deployment work when it is sufficient to wait for the normal initial load to complete.

learning.reason: Even if the initial model load does not finish within the invocation time, the service continues loading the model in the background. The caller can retry while accounting for the loading time.
learning.concept: ModelNotReadyException for a multi-model endpoint

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Pass a large model artifact to hosting without compression
prompt: You are deploying a large model to a supported SageMaker real-time configuration. The artifact consists of multiple files under one S3 prefix, and you want to avoid the time required for the default compression and extraction. Which two CreateModel settings should you choose?

choices.text: Set S3DataType to S3Prefix and specify the prefix containing all the files.
choices.explanation: This treats multiple artifacts under an S3 prefix as the input.

choices.text: Set CompressionType to None.
choices.explanation: This avoids treating the input as a compressed archive that must be extracted during deployment.

choices.text: Put the prefix in ModelDataUrl and have it treated as an alternative to a compressed tar archive.
choices.explanation: The legacy ModelDataUrl archive contract cannot specify multiple uncompressed files for loading.

choices.text: Set S3DataType to S3Object and specify only the first parameter file.
choices.explanation: The remaining files would not be passed to the model.

choices.text: Set CompressionType to Gzip while passing each file under the prefix uncompressed.
choices.explanation: The actual file format would not match the compression format declared to the service.

learning.reason: Using ModelDataSource with an uncompressed S3 prefix allows the model files under that prefix to be used without combining them into a compressed archive.
learning.concept: Using ModelDataSource with uncompressed S3 model files

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Reflecting External Approval Completion in the Pipeline’s Next Step
prompt: After a SageMaker Pipeline generates a model card, you want it to wait until an existing separate system approves it. The approval process is asynchronous and time-consuming. The pipeline must continue the same execution without repeatedly polling the waiting process. Arrange the steps in dependency order.

choices.text: The external system returns the finalized result together with the token by calling SendPipelineExecutionStepSuccess or Failure.
choices.explanation: The token allows the external result to be reported to the waiting step.

choices.text: The pipeline’s Callback step sends a message containing the token to the specified SQS queue.
choices.explanation: The pipeline execution tells the external system what it must wait for.

choices.text: The external system receives the message and retains the token until the approval result is determined.
choices.explanation: The received token must be associated with the result so it can be returned to the same waiting step.

learning.reason: A Callback step sends a message containing a token to SQS and waits until the external process returns a result using that token.
learning.concept: External-process callbacks in SageMaker Pipelines

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Updating Without Simultaneously Provisioning the Entire Old and New Fleets
prompt: You are updating a standard SageMaker real-time endpoint using the same variant name. Because you cannot provision the full old and new capacities at the same time, you want to replace the model in portions of the fleet. Each new batch should be observed for a period before the old capacity is released. Which deployment strategy should you choose?

choices.text: Delete all instances at once and recreate them with the same endpoint name.
choices.explanation: This does not replace the capacity in batches while keeping the service running.

choices.text: Change only the variant weights without updating the instances or model.
choices.explanation: This changes request distribution but does not meet the requirement to replace the model incrementally.

choices.text: Use Rolling deployment and specify an acceptable MaximumBatchSize.
choices.explanation: It replaces the fleet in batches without creating the entire new fleet first.

choices.text: Choose a Blue/green Canary deployment and provision the entire new fleet before sending a portion of the traffic to it.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to limit the capacity provisioned initially. The portion being controlled is traffic.

learning.reason: With Rolling deployment, new capacity is added and switched over in the specified batch sizes, and the old capacity can be released after the observation period.
learning.concept: Rolling deployment that adds capacity in batches

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Choosing Low-Latency Inference with GPU and VPC Connectivity
prompt: You are deploying a custom GPU inference model. It must respond quickly to synchronous requests from a machine-inspection device, and the inference container must also access data in an internal VPC. Users may send requests throughout the day, and the container can remain running. Which hosting option meets these requirements?

choices.text: Configure Provisioned Concurrency for Serverless Inference and enable GPU and VPC connectivity.
choices.explanation: Although this option reduces initial latency, it does not add GPU or VPC connectivity that the service does not support.

choices.text: Use Asynchronous Inference and make the client wait for the result to be written to S3.
choices.explanation: Even if the configuration can use a GPU, it processes results through a queue and S3 instead of providing the requested synchronous response.

choices.text: Use Batch Transform to collect one hour of requests before processing them.
choices.explanation: This does not provide a quick response to each synchronous request as it arrives.

choices.text: Use a real-time endpoint with a supported GPU instance type and configure the internal VPC connection in the model’s VpcConfig.
choices.explanation: A running GPU instance can provide synchronous responses, and a VPC route can be configured for the model container.

learning.reason: Serverless Inference has limitations for GPUs and VPC connectivity. A real-time endpoint using a supported GPU instance can combine synchronous inference with the model’s VpcConfig.
learning.concept: SageMaker real-time and Serverless feature requirements

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Returning Explanations Only for Review Requests
prompt: You have an existing SageMaker real-time endpoint configured for online explanations with Clarify as an existing customer. Explanations are disabled for normal predictions. You want explanations returned only for some requests from an approved review client, without changing the shared configuration. Which approach should you choose?

choices.text: Specify EnableExplanations only in the review client’s InvokeEndpoint request and set the condition to true.
choices.explanation: Explanation generation can be overridden for each invocation.

choices.text: Set the explanation setting in CreateEndpointConfig permanently to true and update the endpoint.
choices.explanation: This configuration change would also affect normal requests that do not need explanations.

choices.text: Assume that specifying the review client’s TargetVariant will always return an explanation.
choices.explanation: Selecting a variant is not the parameter that enables explanation generation.

choices.text: Aggregate feature attributions in a monitoring schedule and return them as the explanation for the immediately preceding request.
choices.explanation: Aggregated monitoring results are not explanations for an individual synchronous request.

learning.reason: For an endpoint configured for explanations, EnableExplanations passed to InvokeEndpoint can determine explanation generation at the request level.
learning.concept: Per-request online explanation overrides

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Reserve a GPU for an Inference Container in ECS
prompt: An ECS cluster uses EC2 container instances equipped with GPUs. You must specify the hardware requirements in the task definition and reserve one physical GPU for a single inference container. Which setting should you choose?

choices.text: Add only a memory limit to the task and consider the GPU allocation complete.
choices.explanation: Memory and GPU requirements are independent; a memory setting does not reserve a GPU.

choices.text: Set an item in the inference container's resourceRequirements with type set to GPU and value set to 1.
choices.explanation: ECS considers the container's GPU requirements during placement and reserves the specified capacity.

choices.text: Increase the task's CPU value by 1024 only.
choices.explanation: This adjusts vCPU capacity; it does not place or reserve a GPU.

choices.text: Set only the GPU_COUNT environment variable to 1.
choices.explanation: The value is passed to the container application, but it does not tell ECS that a GPU must be reserved.

learning.reason: ECS uses the container definition's GPU resourceRequirements to reserve GPU capacity on supported container instances.
learning.concept: GPU resource requirements in an ECS task definition

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Reuse the Same Model Load for Lambda Inference Invocations
prompt: A small CPU-only model is used for inference in Lambda. The model version is fixed and shared by all requests, but latency has increased because the same file is fetched from S3 and loaded every time. Assuming the model works correctly in new execution environments, which change reuses an existing environment?

choices.text: Remove the retrieval process for new environments on the assumption that /tmp saved during the first invocation is accessible from every execution environment.
choices.explanation: /tmp is isolated per execution environment, so another environment cannot access that cache.

choices.text: Require the client to include the model file in the request body every time.
choices.explanation: This transfers and loads the model on every request and does not reduce latency as request volume increases.

choices.text: Initialize the model outside the handler and, when appropriate, cache the version-pinned file in /tmp.
choices.explanation: The same execution environment avoids repeating the retrieval and load, while a new environment can initialize normally.

choices.text: Delete the model from /tmp at the end of every handler invocation and download it again for the next request.
choices.explanation: The model is retrieved every time even when the execution environment is reused, so load time is not reduced.

learning.reason: Initialized objects and static files in /tmp can be reused while a Lambda execution environment is reused. A new environment retrieves the model again during initialization.
learning.concept: Static model caching in the Lambda execution environment

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Review Changes to the Training Environment Before Execution
prompt: CloudFormation manages an inference endpoint and related persistent resources. The next template contains configuration changes, and you want to determine in advance whether the current resources will be replaced during the update. Which method lets you investigate without starting the production update?

choices.text: Run UpdateStack and investigate the replaced resources if the operation fails.
choices.explanation: The update process has already started, so this does not meet the requirement for advance review.

choices.text: Run only Drift Detection on the deployed stack.
choices.explanation: This detects differences from the current template; it does not determine whether a future template will cause replacement.

choices.text: Compare only the template descriptions.
choices.explanation: This does not provide information about which resources will need replacement during the actual update.

choices.text: Create a Change Set with the new template and review the resources marked for Replacement or deletion.
choices.explanation: A Change Set displays the proposed changes before execution, allowing you to decide whether to apply them.

learning.reason: A Change Set lets you review possible resource additions, updates, deletions, and replacements before execution. The stack is not updated until the Change Set is executed.
learning.concept: Checking replacements with a CloudFormation Change Set

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Allow the Deployment Account to Access a Model Group
prompt: A model version in the SageMaker Model Registry of a research account will be deployed in an independent production account. The deployment IAM role already has the required permissions, and its access to ECR, S3, and KMS has been verified. However, the production account cannot access the shared model group. Which setting is required in the sharing account?

choices.text: Set a resource policy on the model group with PutModelPackageGroupPolicy to allow the production account the required access.
choices.explanation: Together with IAM permissions in the production account, this allows another account to operate on the shared model group.

choices.text: Change the registered model's approval status to Approved and thereby enable sharing with other accounts.
choices.explanation: The approval status represents the model lifecycle; it does not authorize cross-account resource access.

choices.text: Append the production account ID to the ECR image tag.
choices.explanation: This changes only the image identifier and does not configure Model Registry permissions.

choices.text: Add the production account name to the model group's description.
choices.explanation: A description does not change access control for sharing.

learning.reason: Cross-account sharing of a model version requires a resource policy on the model group in the sharing account. This authorization is separate from access to the artifacts.
learning.concept: Cross-account sharing of a Model Registry model group

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Reviewing the timeout before model retrieval completes
prompt: A SageMaker model is being updated. The health check after container startup is normal, but retrieving a large model artifact from S3 exceeds the default time and the update fails before the container starts. S3 access and capacity have been verified, and the goal is to wait for the download to complete within the permitted time. Which setting should be reviewed?

choices.text: Disable the endpoint's ModelLatency alarm.
choices.explanation: Changing an inference-performance alarm does not change the time limit for retrieving an artifact during deployment.

choices.text: Review ProductionVariant's ModelDataDownloadTimeoutInSeconds.
choices.explanation: This changes the amount of time allowed for retrieving the model artifact.

choices.text: Increase only ContainerStartupHealthCheckTimeoutInSeconds.
choices.explanation: This extends the time allowed for the container health check to succeed. It does not resolve the earlier model-retrieval failure.

choices.text: Increase the client communication timeout for InvokeEndpoint.
choices.explanation: Artifact retrieval during deployment is independent of the communication timeout for an inference request.

learning.reason: ProductionVariant has separate timeouts for downloading the model artifact and for the health check after the container starts.
learning.concept: SageMaker model-retrieval and container-startup timeouts

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Storing large parallel scoring results outside the workflow output limit
prompt: A Step Functions Distributed Map performs a large number of scoring operations. Each child workflow can return a small result, but aggregating all results would exceed the state output limit. The results must be retained elsewhere so that a downstream batch process can use all of them. Which setting should be configured?

choices.text: Truncate the output below the limit and treat it as though all items were passed downstream.
choices.explanation: The remaining results would be lost, so this would not satisfy the requirement to use all results.

choices.text: Increase only the workflow timeout.
choices.explanation: This increases the available processing time but does not change the state-data size limit.

choices.text: Use the Distributed Map's ResultWriter to specify an S3 output location, and have the downstream process read the results from there.
choices.explanation: All results can be stored in S3 without returning them as the state's response.

choices.text: Set MaxConcurrency to 1 so that the aggregated size is always smaller.
choices.explanation: This changes the number of child executions running concurrently but not the total amount of results eventually aggregated.

learning.reason: The Distributed Map ResultWriter writes child-execution results to S3, eliminating the need to pack all results into a single state output.
learning.concept: Distributed Map S3 result output

category: MLソリューションのモニタリング、保守、セキュリティ
examDomain: MLソリューションのモニタリング、保守、セキュリティ
title: Calculating the overall error rate for two variants with different traffic volumes
prompt: Variant A of the same SageMaker endpoint had 10 errors out of 1,000 requests, while variant B had 5 errors out of 10 requests. In CloudWatch, you need to produce a time series showing the error ratio across all invocations rather than separately for each variant. Which aggregation method should you use?

choices.text: Add the error counts for both variants over the same period and divide by the total number of invocations during that period.
choices.explanation: Divide the 15 errors by all 1,010 requests to calculate the overall request-level rate.

choices.text: Calculate the average of the error rates for the two variants.
choices.explanation: Because the two variants do not receive the same amount of traffic, this does not equal the rate calculated using all requests as the denominator.

choices.text: Display only the error rate for the variant with the higher number of errors.
choices.explanation: This excludes the errors and request volume for the other variant.

choices.text: Divide the total number of errors by the number of variants.
choices.explanation: This produces the number of errors per variant, not the proportion of requests that resulted in errors.

learning.reason: The denominator for the overall rate is the total number of requests across both variants. A simple average of the individual rates overweights the lower-traffic variant.
learning.concept: Request-volume-weighted error rates using CloudWatch metric math

title: Detecting intermittent degradation while excluding a temporary spike
prompt: Inference processing latency is observed at one-minute intervals. A notification is required when at least 3 of the most recent 5 points exceed a threshold, regardless of whether the points are consecutive. A five-minute average must not be used; the value for each minute must be evaluated. Which CloudWatch configuration meets these requirements?

choices.text: Set Period to 1 minute, Evaluation Periods to 3, and Datapoints to Alarm to 3.
choices.explanation: The evaluation range is reduced to 3 points, so it cannot detect 3 points scattered across a 5-point range.

choices.text: Set Period to 1 minute, Evaluation Periods to 5, and Datapoints to Alarm to 3.
choices.explanation: This meets the condition when any 3 of the 5 points exceed the threshold, regardless of consecutiveness.

choices.text: Set Period to 5 minutes, Evaluation Periods to 1, and Datapoints to Alarm to 1.
choices.explanation: This evaluates one aggregated point instead of counting multiple one-minute values individually.

choices.text: Set Period to 1 minute, Evaluation Periods to 5, and Datapoints to Alarm to 5.
choices.explanation: This requires every point to exceed the threshold and would not detect cases with only 3 exceeding points.

learning.reason: CloudWatch M out of N evaluation lets you specify the N points to evaluate and the M points that must exceed the threshold independently.
learning.concept: CloudWatch 3 out of 5 evaluation

title: Investigate 5-minute p95 from existing inference logs
prompt: Structured inference container logs contain durationMs for each request. You need to look back in time and compare the p95 for every 5-minute interval to identify periods when latency worsened. Do not publish additional metrics, and use only CloudWatch Logs Insights. Which query should you run?

choices.text: stats pct(durationMs, 95)
choices.explanation: This obtains the overall p95, but it cannot compare separate 5-minute intervals.

choices.text: stats count(durationMs) by bin(5m)
choices.explanation: This counts the data points in each interval but does not provide latency percentiles.

choices.text: stats pct(durationMs, 95) by bin(5m)
choices.explanation: This divides the data into 5-minute intervals and calculates the 95th percentile for each interval.

choices.text: stats avg(durationMs) by bin(5m)
choices.explanation: This calculates the average for each interval but does not obtain the p95 that separates lower and upper observations.

learning.reason: With Logs Insights stats, you can specify time intervals with bin and aggregate percentiles for each interval with pct.
learning.concept: Time windows and percentiles in CloudWatch Logs Insights

choices.text: Monitor the SageMaker Invocations metric against a fixed threshold.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail to audit only the API whose endpoint configuration was changed.

choices.text: Monitor only the modification time of the S3 object containing the trained model.
choices.explanation: A file update is separate from whether the running API returns the expected response.

choices.text: Periodically run a Synthetics Canary that sends test input and validates the response.
choices.explanation: This can inspect the same client path even when there are no actual users.

learning.reason: A CloudWatch Synthetics script can call the API at regular intervals without waiting for real traffic and inspect the returned result.

title: Reduce calls from S3 to KMS while continuing to use SSE-KMS
prompt: SSE-KMS is required for a general-purpose S3 bucket that receives a large number of learning files. The KMS key policy does not assume an encryption context restricted to the object ARN. You want to reduce KMS requests while keeping the encryption method for newly added files. What should you enable?

choices.text: Disable S3 Versioning.
choices.explanation: Changing version management does not reduce the number of requests used for SSE-KMS on new objects.

choices.text: Run GetObject multiple times in succession for the same object.
choices.explanation: This only increases retrievals and does not configure S3 to reduce encryption-time requests to KMS.

choices.text: Keep SSE-KMS and enable S3 Bucket Keys for new objects.
choices.explanation: This preserves the encryption method while reducing requests from S3 to KMS.

choices.text: Switch to SSE-S3 and stop using SSE-KMS.
choices.explanation: This changes KMS calls, but it does not meet the requirement that SSE-KMS be used.

learning.reason: S3 Bucket Keys use a bucket-level key for SSE-KMS and reduce the volume of requests from S3 to KMS.
learning.concept: Reducing requests with SSE-KMS and S3 Bucket Keys

title: Separate custom-container credentials from the image
prompt: A SageMaker inference container connects to an approved database. The connection information changes, so you want a configuration that does not require rebuilding the image when the password changes and does not expose the value in the training team's logs. The container can connect to Secrets Manager. Which two settings should you choose?

choices.text: Store the database value in Secrets Manager and configure only the Secret identifier in the container.
choices.explanation: This keeps the password out of the image configuration and lets the application retrieve the value when needed.

choices.text: Allow only secretsmanager:GetSecretValue for the relevant Secret in the execution role.
choices.explanation: This limits retrieval to the required Secret and does not allow reading other credentials.

choices.text: Put the plaintext password in Dockerfile ENV and consider it sufficient because ECR is private.
choices.explanation: Anyone who can read the image can be exposed to the value, and changing the value would also require rebuilding the image.

choices.text: Write the password to the container startup logs so operations staff can distribute it from there.
choices.explanation: This exposes the retrieved secret in logs.

choices.text: Allow all training users to read every Secret.
choices.explanation: This expands access to credentials that are not required for execution.

learning.reason: Manage connection information as a Secret and have the application read it at runtime. Limit permissions to the required execution role and Secret.

title: Restrict training jobs in member accounts to approved Regions
prompt: Human administrators manage SageMaker training across multiple member accounts. You must prevent CreateTrainingJob from being sent to Regions outside the approved set and maintain the restriction even if an IAM administrator in an account adds permissions. choices.text: In an SCP for the target OU, deny sagemaker:CreateTrainingJob when aws:RequestedRegion is outside the approved list.
choices.explanation: This enforces the approved-Region condition as a permissions boundary for the affected member accounts.

choices.text: Notify every account of the recommended Regions through an environment variable.

choices.text: Record only training in approved Regions with CloudTrail and allow requests that are not recorded.

choices.text: Add an Allow in IAM for only the approved Regions and leave each administrator's existing permissions unchanged.
choices.explanation: Other permissions could still allow operations outside those Regions, so this would not create an organization-wide upper limit.

learning.reason: An explicit Deny in a policy attached to an OU cannot be overridden by an IAM Allow in an affected member account.

title: Restricting Each Training Job’s Data Scope with a Shared Execution Role
prompt: A team wants to keep one execution role for SageMaker training while separating S3 input prefixes by tenant. The team wants each job to access only that tenant’s data by using the session tag tenant-id from an approved caller. Which two configurations are required?

choices.text: Include the tenant name as part of TrainingJobName and leave the S3 configuration unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing only the displayed job name does not change S3 permissions.

choices.text: Temporarily copy all data to each training job, and then have the training code delete unnecessary files.
choices.explanation: The job can read data from other tenants before the files are deleted, so this does not provide access-control isolation.

choices.text: Enable session-tag chaining and allow the required sts:AssumeRole and sts:TagSession actions for approved principals in the trust policy.
choices.explanation: This allows the approved tenant tag to be passed to the temporary session used by the training job.

choices.text: Limit S3 object permissions to the prefixes corresponding to aws:PrincipalTag/tenant-id.
choices.explanation: Even with a shared role, the tag associated with the job session can determine its access scope.

choices.text: Allow the shared role to read all S3 prefixes and separate tenants only in the application interface.
choices.explanation: This provides no authorization boundary, so the training code can retrieve data from other tenants.

learning.reason: Configure SageMaker jobs to pass session tags, and use PrincipalTag in the role’s S3 permissions to select the applicable prefix. Control the issuance and modification of tags through the trust policy.

choices.text: Select a supported successor image, run comparative training and evaluation tests, and deploy it afterward.

choices.text: Keep the old image and assume that AWS will overwrite its contents with fixes.
choices.explanation: New fixes are not provided for a version whose support has ended.

choices.text: Treat the libraries as updated simply by copying the old image to the organization’s ECR.
choices.explanation: Copying the image does not change the versions or vulnerabilities of the dependencies it contains.

choices.text: As the organization administrator, create an organization trail and deliver management events to the audit S3 bucket.

choices.text: Create a standard multi-Region trail only in the audit account.
choices.explanation: This supports multiple Regions, but management operations from accounts other than the account that created the trail are not collected across the organization.

learning.reason: A CloudTrail organization trail can deploy management-event collection across the organization’s member accounts. Members can view an organization trail but cannot change or delete it.

title: Determining the Validity Period of a Presigned Training-File URL
prompt: To inspect samples of training data, a team created a presigned S3 URL that expires two hours after it is issued. The signature uses an STS session that expires 30 minutes after issuance. What happens when the first download request is made with the URL 45 minutes after it was issued?

choices.text: It succeeds because the validity period is determined only by the URL’s two-hour expiration.
choices.explanation: This ignores the expiration of the temporary credentials.

choices.text: The same URL can be used automatically with a new signature if a new STS session is available.
choices.explanation: To authorize access with a new session, the signature included in the URL must also be generated again.

choices.text: It succeeds because the object’s existence was verified when the URL was issued.
choices.explanation: Object existence and signature validity at the time of the access request are independent.

choices.text: It fails because the session used to create the signature has already expired, even though the URL specifies two hours.
choices.explanation: The effective expiration cannot exceed the validity period of the credentials used to create the signature.

learning.reason: A URL signed with temporary credentials becomes unusable when the signing credentials expire, even if that occurs before the expiration specified for the URL.
learning.concept: Presigned S3 URLs and the shorter validity period of STS sessions
