title: Hide personal information during normal viewing and reveal it only for approved investigations
prompt: Inference diagnostic logs are sent to CloudWatch Logs. You want to mask supported personal information contained in logs ingested from now on during normal viewing, while allowing only an exception-approved investigation role to display the original values. Select two combinations.

choices.text: Configure a data protection policy with the relevant data identifiers on the log group and use it to mask the data.

choices.text: Allow only the investigation role to use logs:Unmask for the target log group.
choices.explanation: The mask remains in place for normal roles, while the investigation role can view the original values when necessary.

choices.text: Delete the entire log group and treat the deletion as masking.
choices.explanation: This also removes diagnostic information needed by normal users and prevents the investigation role from viewing the original values.

choices.text: Allow all operations staff to use logs:Unmask and instruct them not to use it routinely.
choices.explanation: The permission is not restricted to the approved investigation role.

prompt: Data for model regression tests is stored in EFS and protected with AWS Backup. Without switching the original EFS, you want to attempt a restore each month from selected recovery points and clean up the restored resources after testing. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Inspect EFS CloudWatch metrics and infer whether past recovery points can be loaded.
choices.explanation: Current usage and I/O alone cannot show whether a backup from that point in time can be restored.

learning.reason: An AWS Backup restore testing plan restores selected protected resources on a schedule, records the results, and cleans up the resources used for restoration after testing.

title: Distinguish the number of distinct values in an ID column from the number of nonduplicated values
prompt: A profile for training material created with Glue DataBrew contains both numeric and string columns. For a customer ID column whose values are A, B, A, and C, you want to report separately that there are 3 distinct values and 2 values that occur only once. Which statistics should you use?

choices.text: distinctValuesCount is 2 and uniqueValuesCount is 3.
choices.explanation: The meanings of the two aggregations are reversed.

choices.text: Both distinctValuesCount and uniqueValuesCount are 4.
choices.explanation: The total of four rows includes the repeated A. Neither value-based statistic equals the row count.

choices.text: uniqueValuesCount is 1.
choices.explanation: Only A appears more than once, but the statistic needed counts values that appear exactly once.

choices.text: distinctValuesCount is 3 and uniqueValuesCount is 2.
choices.explanation: A, B, and C are three distinct values, and B and C are the two values that occur only once.

learning.reason: distinctValuesCount calculates the number of distinct values that occur, while uniqueValuesCount counts values that occur exactly once.

title: Display a shared training table in Athena in the recipient account
prompt: The data provider has completed sharing a table with another account through Lake Formation, and the recipient has accepted the required invitations. An analyst in the recipient account has read permission on the shared table, but cannot select the shared table from the recipient's local database in Athena. How can the table be displayed without copying the data?

choices.text: Create a resource link in the recipient's database that points to the shared table, and grant the analyst permission to view the link.
choices.explanation: The shared table can be displayed in Athena in the recipient account as a catalog item that can be referenced.

choices.text: Delete the original table and replace it in the recipient account with a table having the same name.
choices.explanation: This breaks the reference to the sharing account and also disrupts the existing data provider.

choices.text: Change the Athena query result bucket to an S3 location owned by the sharing account.
choices.explanation: The query result location does not change how the shared table is displayed in the catalog.

choices.text: Create only the same column definition in the recipient account without configuring the shared resource or its S3 location.
choices.explanation: A definition alone cannot connect to the shared resource.

learning.reason: Create a link to the shared resource in the recipient's Data Catalog. Athena can reference the sharing account through this local resource link.

title: Join Reference Data for Training with SQL Without Replication
prompt: To evaluate features, you want to temporarily join historical events in S3 with current product attributes in PostgreSQL using SQL for read-only access. You do not need a scheduled copy of the product table, and you want to use the existing Athena query environment. Which approach should you choose?

choices.explanation: Although possible, this does not meet the requirement to avoid regularly copying the product attributes.

choices.text: Configure the appropriate data source connector for PostgreSQL and perform a read-only join from Athena with the S3 data.
choices.explanation: This lets you query the external data in place and run SQL without creating a scheduled copy in advance.

choices.text: Set the Athena results bucket to the RDS host name.
choices.explanation: A result-storage setting cannot read the input PostgreSQL tables.

choices.text: Add only the PostgreSQL column definitions to an S3 table and infer the nonexistent product data.
choices.explanation: A schema alone cannot retrieve data from the external source.

title: Keep Only the First Completed Training Manifest
prompt: Two retries concurrently upload a completed training manifest to the same Amazon S3 key. You need only the first write to succeed and must prevent a later write from overwriting it. How can you achieve this without using a separate locking service?

choices.text: Enable object versioning only.
choices.explanation: Versioning preserves the history, but subsequent writes to the same key still succeed.

choices.text: Send an email notification with SES and decide later to accept only the first execution.
choices.explanation: A notification cannot make the write conditional and does not prevent a later overwrite.

choices.text: Specify If-None-Match: * in both PutObject requests.
choices.explanation: S3 evaluates the condition that prevents overwriting an existing key.

choices.text: Check for absence with HeadObject and then issue an unconditional PutObject.
choices.explanation: Both concurrent checks could report that the object is absent, allowing a later PutObject to overwrite the object.

learning.reason: A write that specifies * for If-None-Match fails when a current object exists at the same key. The existence check and write are performed as one conditional request.
learning.concept: Conditional PutObject for controlling the first S3 write

title: Prevent a Late, Older S3 Event from Reverting the Training Index
prompt: You update an index of training materials from S3 event notifications. Creation and deletion notifications for the same key may arrive out of order. What should you compare to ignore an event that is older than the processed notification already stored?

choices.text: Always accept the notification with the later queue-arrival time.
choices.explanation: The arrival order does not necessarily match the order in which events actually occurred in S3.

choices.text: Compare the sequencer values as a single sequence number shared across the entire stream, including notifications for different keys.
choices.explanation: A sequencer does not establish ordering between different object keys.

choices.text: Compare object keys lexicographically to determine the order of events for each key.
choices.explanation: A key name does not indicate which change to the same object occurred first.

choices.text: Compare the stored sequencer for the same key with the sequencer in the new notification and ignore the older one.
choices.explanation: The relative ordering of notifications for the same key can be used to avoid reverting the index based on arrival order.

learning.reason: The sequencer included in creation and deletion events can be used to compare ordering for the same key. When the values have different lengths, pad the shorter value on the left with zeros before comparing them.
learning.concept: Object-level ordering with the S3 event sequencer

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Apply Updated Features and New Customer Rows at Once
prompt: You are loading customer features into an Iceberg table with Athena engine 3. The input batch contains one unique latest row for each customer ID. Existing customers must be updated, and new customers must be added. Which method applies both changes in a single transaction?

choices.text: Use MERGE INTO with customer ID as the matching condition, setting MATCHED to UPDATE and NOT MATCHED to INSERT.
choices.explanation: This processes existing and new customers in one statement.

choices.text: Use INSERT INTO for all rows and add existing customers again with the same keys.
choices.explanation: Because existing rows are not replaced, the old and new rows for the same customer may both remain.

choices.text: Use only UPDATE and do not create an initial row for new customers in the input.
choices.explanation: UPDATE does not insert a row that does not exist.

choices.text: Register a new Parquet file as a regular external table without updating the original Iceberg table.
choices.explanation: This does not apply the new and updated rows to the target Iceberg table.

learning.reason: MERGE INTO selects an update when the key matches and an insert when it does not, applying multiple operations in one transaction.
learning.concept: Updating features with Athena Iceberg MERGE INTO

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Retrieve only the required features for multiple records from the online store
prompt: As preprocessing for low-latency inference, you need to retrieve multiple customer IDs at once from the same feature group in an online Feature Store. You need only two features—age group and usage count—and do not need any other values in the response. Which API configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Scan the entire offline history of the group each time and extract the two requested fields in the application.
choices.explanation: This does not use online retrieval for low-latency workloads and also reads unnecessary history.

choices.text: Pass the feature group and the list of target IDs to BatchGetRecord, and set FeatureNames to only the two features.
choices.explanation: This requests the records in a batch while limiting the response to the specified features.

choices.text: Run PutRecord for each customer ID and use the write response as the feature values.
choices.explanation: PutRecord is a write operation; it does not retrieve the current record values.

choices.text: Call DescribeFeatureGroup once and read the feature values for all customers.
choices.explanation: This can retrieve the group definition, but it does not return feature data for each identifier.

learning.reason: BatchGetRecord retrieves records by specifying a feature group and multiple identifiers, while FeatureNames specifies which features to return.
learning.concept: Retrieving multiple IDs and selecting features in Feature Store

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Improve read performance for feature extraction without increasing EBS volume size
prompt: A training-data extraction process running on EC2 reads intermediate data on an EBS gp3 volume sequentially in large units. Measurements show that the current throughput setting is the limit, while the volume capacity and IOPS have headroom. The instance-side bandwidth also has headroom, and the setting can be adjusted within the gp3 supported range. What should you change?

choices.text: Increase only the IOPS and leave the throughput setting unchanged.
choices.explanation: This does not change the bandwidth limit measured as the current bottleneck.

choices.text: Change the volume tag to indicate higher performance.
choices.explanation: A tag is an operational classification and does not change the read-bandwidth setting.

choices.text: Increase the configured gp3 throughput without changing the volume size.
choices.explanation: This directly relaxes the read-bandwidth constraint identified by the measurements.

choices.text: Increase only the capacity and expect the configured throughput to increase automatically.
choices.explanation: For gp3, increasing capacity does not automatically increase the specified throughput value.

learning.reason: With gp3, capacity and performance are configured independently. When sequential reads reach the throughput limit, increase throughput while keeping capacity unchanged.
learning.concept: Independent capacity and throughput settings for gp3

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Pin the published version of a preprocessing recipe
prompt: While investigating a training-job failure, you need to transform the same input again with AWS Glue DataBrew. The training data was created with published version 3.0 of a preprocessing recipe, and another team has since published version 4.0. How should you configure the recipe job so that you can continue reproducing the original training data?

choices.text: Use the latest published version and include 3.0 in the output filename.
choices.explanation: The output filename does not pin the transformation steps. Using the latest published version applies the 4.0 steps.

choices.text: Switch to the work-in-progress version and make the project’s editing permissions read-only.
choices.explanation: The work-in-progress version is not necessarily identical to the published version used at that time, and restricting editing permissions does not restore the historical steps.

choices.text: Pin only the S3 version of the input and allow the recipe version used by the job to follow updates.
choices.explanation: Pinning the input preserves only the data content; updating the recipe can still change the transformation result.

choices.text: Specify the recipe name and published version 3.0.
choices.explanation: The job can continue using the specified published version even after later versions are released.

learning.reason: Reproducibility requires pinning both the input data and the preprocessing steps so changes to each can be isolated. A DataBrew recipe job can select a published version.
learning.concept: Specifying an approved version in a DataBrew recipe job

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Extract training data without adding load to the running database
prompt: An ML team wants to use product data from the time of last night’s automatic Amazon RDS DB snapshot in Parquet format in Amazon S3. Which method avoids querying the running database and does not add a DB instance solely for extraction?

choices.text: Start an RDS export to S3 for the automatic DB snapshot.
choices.explanation: RDS can use an automatic snapshot as the input and write Parquet to S3 in the background.

choices.text: Use AWS DMS full load with the running RDS database as the source and configure the S3 target output as Parquet.
choices.explanation: Although Parquet output is possible, this reads the running database rather than the database state represented by the specified snapshot.

choices.text: Restore the existing DB snapshot to another RDS instance and read it through a Glue JDBC connection.
choices.explanation: This restores the snapshot state but adds a DB instance solely for extraction.

choices.text: Copy the DB snapshot to another Region and read the copy from Athena as an external table.
choices.explanation: Copying a snapshot does not create Parquet data in S3, so Athena cannot access it this way.

learning.reason: RDS can extract data directly from a DB snapshot and write it to S3 in Parquet format, without querying the running database or restoring the snapshot to a DB instance.
learning.concept: Exporting an RDS DB snapshot to Parquet for analysis

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Consolidating Continuously Growing Small Files in an Iceberg Table
prompt: A streaming process is appending Parquet files to an Apache Iceberg table in the Glue Data Catalog. Numerous small files have slowed feature queries from Athena and EMR. You must continuously consolidate the existing table's data files without changing the write frequency. Which setting should you choose?

choices.text: Enable orphan file deletion for the table.
choices.explanation: Orphan file deletion targets files that are no longer referenced by the table; it does not merge small files that are currently referenced.

choices.text: Enable Glue Data Catalog managed compaction for the table.
choices.explanation: When the target partitions meet the conditions, managed compaction consolidates the small Parquet files.

choices.text: Only reduce the number of snapshots retained for the table.
choices.explanation: Reducing old snapshots does not merge the small files referenced by the current snapshot.

choices.text: Extend the query-result reuse period in the Athena workgroup.
choices.explanation: This only affects reuse of available results; it does not change reads from EMR or the number of small files in the source table.

learning.reason: Iceberg compaction consolidates the data files themselves, reducing the file-processing overhead for multiple read engines.
learning.concept: Continuous compaction of Iceberg Parquet files with the Glue Data Catalog

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Validating the Percentage of String Features That Can Be Converted to Integers
prompt: The `device_count` column from an external CSV is read as a string by AWS Glue. Before passing it to downstream feature processing, you want AWS Glue Data Quality to verify that more than 99% of the values can be converted to integers in Spark without changing the column. Which rule should you choose?

choices.text: `Uniqueness "device_count" >= 0.99`
choices.explanation: This checks the proportion of unique values. It does not determine whether values can be converted to integers, and valid duplicate values can cause the check to fail.

choices.text: Combine `ColumnExists "device_count"` with a table-column-count check.
choices.explanation: Column presence and column count cannot determine whether each row can be converted to an integer or whether the required proportion satisfies the condition.

choices.text: `ColumnDataType "device_count" = "INTEGER" with threshold >= 0.99`
choices.explanation: This evaluates the proportion of values that can be cast to integers against the specified threshold. It does not change the original column representation.

choices.text: `Completeness "device_count" >= 0.99`
choices.explanation: This can validate the proportion of nonmissing values, but strings that cannot be converted to integers are still treated as nonmissing.

learning.reason: DQDL ColumnDataType evaluates whether values can be cast to the specified type; it does not merely compare the data type recorded in the catalog.
learning.concept: Using ColumnDataType in Glue Data Quality to measure type-conversion feasibility

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Reducing Read Latency for Online Features That Do Not Need Historical Storage
prompt: A real-time fraud-detection model reads the latest state of a device from SageMaker Feature Store with low latency. The recent event types referenced by the model should be stored as a single list-type feature rather than split across columns. The training history is already stored by a separate pipeline. Which configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Create only an offline store and choose Iceberg.
choices.explanation: This configuration is intended for historical analysis and does not provide the real-time online retrieval API.

choices.text: Create a Standard online store and an offline store together, and shorten the TTL.
choices.explanation: TTL controls how long records remain valid; it does not add list-type support to the Standard tier.

choices.text: Set the storage type to InMemory and require automatic replication from the same feature group to an offline store.
choices.explanation: Replication from an InMemory feature group to an offline store is not supported. The existing separate pipeline can be used for the training history.

choices.text: Create a new online-only feature group and set the storage type to InMemory.
choices.explanation: InMemory supports list-type online features. The training history can remain in the existing separate pipeline.

learning.reason: The InMemory tier for online inference supports collection types such as lists with low-latency retrieval. Because replication to an offline store is not supported, historical data should remain in the existing separate path.
learning.concept: Collection types in the SageMaker Feature Store InMemory online store

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Expanding Logs While Retaining the Log Group and Log Stream
prompt: Two types of CloudWatch Logs log groups are sent through subscription filters to the same Amazon Data Firehose stream. When creating training features in S3, you need to partition the data by log group and log stream. How should you configure Firehose to expand the gzip data and retain the original CloudWatch Logs envelope in S3?

choices.text: Enable CloudWatch Logs decompression and disable message extraction.
choices.explanation: This expands the gzip data while retaining the surrounding fields that include the log group and log stream.

choices.text: Enable both CloudWatch Logs decompression and message extraction.
choices.explanation: Only the contents of the message field are delivered, so the envelope metadata required for this use case is removed.

choices.text: Disable CloudWatch Logs decompression in Firehose and only disable output compression for the S3 destination.
choices.explanation: Changing whether additional compression is applied during delivery does not expand the gzip payload received from CloudWatch Logs.

choices.text: Enable message extraction and recover the original log stream from the file name of the delivered S3 object.
choices.explanation: Even when one delivery stream handles multiple inputs, the standard output name does not preserve the mapping to the original log stream that was lost.

learning.reason: Firehose CloudWatch Logs decompression and message extraction are separate settings. When message extraction is enabled, fields such as the log group are removed.
learning.concept: Expanding CloudWatch Logs and retaining metadata with Firehose

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Adding Existing Training Data to S3 Replication
prompt: A rule was configured to replicate new objects so that training data in S3 could be moved to another Region. Versioning is enabled on both buckets, and replication of new files is succeeding. How can the S3 Standard objects that existed before the rule was configured also be sent according to the same rule without rewriting them?

choices.text: Export the object list to S3 Inventory and continue generating only the inventory.
choices.explanation: S3 Inventory creates a list. A job that uses the list or another input must also run to perform replication.

choices.text: Include the existing objects in scope in a manifest and run S3 Batch Replication.
choices.explanation: This starts on-demand replication of existing in-scope objects to the same destination used by the live configuration.

choices.text: Resave the live replication rule and wait until the target prefix matches.
choices.explanation: Live replication does not go back and replicate existing objects that are within the rule's scope.

choices.text: Enable S3 Replication Time Control and apply a replication deadline to all existing objects.
choices.explanation: RTC manages the timing of eligible live replication; it does not select past objects for on-demand replication.

learning.reason: Existing objects that were not included in live replication can be processed by an on-demand batch job that uses the replication configuration.
learning.concept: Completing replication of data created before the replication configuration with S3 Batch Replication

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Crawling Only New Date-Based Partitions
prompt: Training data is written to S3 every day under `day=YYYY-MM-DD/`, and a Glue crawler makes it available to Athena. Past folders are never updated or deleted, and the schema is fixed. While retaining the initial full crawl and the daily schedule, which setting should be selected to read only the date folders added afterward?

choices.text: Specify only the latest day in the `WHERE` clause of the Athena query.
choices.explanation: This limits what the query reads, but it does not affect the separately running Glue crawler.

choices.text: Continue full recrawls and limit the number of files examined in each leaf folder to one.
choices.explanation: Even if fewer files are read in each folder, existing date folders remain in the scan scope.

choices.text: Select `CRAWL_NEW_FOLDERS_ONLY` in the incremental crawl recrawl settings.
choices.explanation: The initial crawl covers the entire dataset, and subsequent crawls register compatible partitions in newly added folders.

choices.text: Continue full recrawls and configure schema-change behavior to log only.
choices.explanation: This setting prevents changes from being applied to the table; it does not suppress rescanning of existing folders.

learning.reason: The initial crawl recognizes the existing schema and partitions, while the new-folders-only setting reduces daily rescanning when existing folders do not need to be updated or deleted.
learning.concept: Incremental crawling of only new S3 folders with a Glue crawler

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Retaining Labeled Records When Reference Data Is Missing
prompt: In SageMaker Data Wrangler, regional statistics are added to member history that contains churn labels. The member history is on the left and the regional statistics are on the right, joined by a region ID. Some members have no matching region, but their rows must be retained. The regional statistics contain one row per region ID, and missing values will be filled in later. Which join should be used?

choices.text: Use an inner join.
choices.explanation: Because it retains only rows with matching region IDs, it would discard labeled members whose regional statistics are not registered.

choices.text: Use a left anti join.
choices.explanation: This extracts only unmatched members, so it discards members that match the regional statistics.

choices.text: Use a full outer join and send all rows directly to training.
choices.explanation: Rows for regions with no corresponding member may also be added, creating extra rows beyond the exact retention of the original labeled population.

choices.text: Use a left outer join.
choices.explanation: All labeled rows on the left are retained, and the regional-statistics columns are NULL when there is no match on the right.

learning.reason: A left outer join keeps labeled rows even when reference columns are missing, allowing those rows to be handled in a later step.
learning.concept: Using a Data Wrangler left outer join to retain the labeled population

category: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
examDomain: 機械学習のためのデータ準備
title: Reading Streaming JSON with Fixed Column Types
prompt: An AWS Glue streaming job reads JSON from Kinesis Data Streams. The initial microbatch contains no decimal measurements, so the type of `reading` changes depending on the sample. The type agreed with the sender is `DOUBLE`. How should the connection options be configured to fix the column type at parsing time for this input, which is not registered in the Data Catalog?

choices.text: Set `inferSchema` to `false` and specify input DDL in `schema` that includes `reading DOUBLE`.
choices.explanation: The explicitly specified schema is used to parse the input, so the type of `reading` is not determined by the values observed in a batch.

choices.text: Set `inferSchema` to `false` and provide only the stream ARN without specifying a schema.
choices.explanation: This configuration provides no input schema to replace inference and therefore does not meet the parsing requirement.

choices.text: Fix the checkpoint and leave `inferSchema` set to `true`.
choices.explanation: A checkpoint is used for read recovery; it is not the setting that explicitly declares the agreed column type for the connection.

choices.text: Lengthen the microbatch window and leave `inferSchema` set to `true`.
choices.explanation: A longer batch may still contain only integer representations, so it cannot guarantee the `DOUBLE` input contract.

learning.reason: Instead of reading JSON streaming input through schema inference, explicitly declaring the data contract stabilizes column types at parsing time.
learning.concept: Distinguishing Glue streaming schema inference from explicitly specified input DDL

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Create AutoML candidates using only approved algorithms
prompt: For regulated tabular data, you are comparing classifiers by using SageMaker Autopilot's `CreateAutoMLJobV2`. The job is already configured in ENSEMBLING mode, and only the reviewed XGBoost and CatBoost algorithms may be trained and included as candidates. Which setting imposes this restriction?

choices.text: Set `TabularJobConfig.ProblemType` to `BinaryClassification` to match the requirements.
choices.explanation: This setting specifies the type of problem to solve; it does not restrict the candidate algorithms.

choices.text: Pass a configuration to `TabularJobConfig.CandidateGenerationConfig.AlgorithmsConfig` in which `AutoMLAlgorithms` is `xgboost` and `catboost`.
choices.explanation: This generates candidates using only the specified algorithms from the available set.

choices.text: Set `Mode` to `ENSEMBLING` and add a threshold for the metric to pass to the objective metric.
choices.explanation: The mode and objective metric are not an algorithm allowlist and do not prevent other default candidates from being trained.

choices.text: After the job completes, register only candidates containing XGBoost and CatBoost in the model registry.
choices.explanation: This can narrow the deployment candidates, but training for algorithms outside the review scope has already occurred.

learning.reason: The AutoML training mode determines the set of available algorithms. An allowlist in the candidate-generation configuration selects which algorithms from that set are actually trained.
learning.concept: AlgorithmsConfig for Autopilot V2 tabular jobs

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Determine an alert threshold from Random Cut Forest scores
prompt: You are monitoring sensors from two factories with separate models in SageMaker Random Cut Forest. You have normal-period data for both factories, but the score distributions returned by the two models differ. How should you set the thresholds to begin operation while keeping each factory's normal-period alert rate at approximately 0.5%?

choices.text: Pool the normal scores from both factories and apply the 99.5th percentile estimated from the combined data to both factories.
choices.explanation: This may adjust the overall alert rate, but it does not guarantee comparable rates for factories with different distributions.

choices.text: For each model, generate an alert when the score is below the 0.5th percentile of its normal scores.
choices.explanation: This accounts for each distribution, but higher scores indicate greater anomaly severity.

choices.text: Evaluate each model on an unused normal period and use approximately the 99.5th percentile of its scores as the initial threshold.
choices.explanation: This targets only high scores for alerts and calibrates the alert rate for each factory using its observed normal-score distribution.

choices.text: Generate an alert for either model whenever its score exceeds 0.995.
choices.explanation: This treats the RCF score as an anomaly probability from 0 to 1, which does not necessarily correspond to the upper 0.5% of normal scores.

learning.reason: RCF outputs anomaly scores in which higher values indicate greater anomaly severity; they are not calibrated anomaly probabilities. The upper quantile of normal scores provides an initial threshold for the target false-alert rate without assuming a particular distribution.
learning.concept: RCF anomaly-score direction and per-model operational thresholds

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Choose a k-NN configuration that compares embeddings by cosine similarity
prompt: You are classifying documents with the built-in k-NN algorithm in SageMaker. Embedding magnitudes vary with document length, and you want to compare directions using cosine similarity. The embeddings must be provided without transformation, and the comparison set is small enough that comparing every candidate is sufficient. Which configuration meets the requirements?

choices.text: Specify `index_type=faiss.IVFPQ` and `index_metric=COSINE`.
choices.explanation: This k-NN container does not support the IVFPQ and COSINE combination.

choices.text: Specify `index_type=faiss.Flat` and `index_metric=INNER_PRODUCT`.
choices.explanation: The inner product of unnormalized vectors is also affected by magnitude, so it does not provide the required cosine similarity.

choices.text: Specify `index_type=faiss.Flat` and `index_metric=L2`.
choices.explanation: Euclidean distance does not compare only the directions of vectors with different magnitudes.

choices.text: Specify `index_type=faiss.Flat` and `index_metric=COSINE`.
choices.explanation: The Flat index uses cosine similarity, so the vector lengths do not need to be equalized in preprocessing.

learning.reason: Distance and similarity are configured with `index_metric`, and the available metrics are constrained by the selected FAISS index.
learning.concept: COSINE compatibility with FAISS indexes in SageMaker k-NN

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Stop training and notify an operator when an anomaly is detected
prompt: A configured Debugger rule for a long-running SageMaker training job correctly detects a condition in which training is not progressing. The required execution permissions and the SNS email subscription are already configured. When this condition is detected, how can you automatically stop training and send an email without creating an additional Lambda function?

choices.text: Configure an `ActionList` in the rule's `actions` that combines `StopTraining()` and `Email(...)`.
choices.explanation: When the rule detects the issue, both stopping and notification can be performed through built-in actions.

choices.text: Configure only `Email(...)` for the rule and wait for training to stop through the rule's `IssuesFound`.
choices.explanation: The email action provides notification only; the rule's detection state does not stop the training job.

choices.text: Shorten the maximum runtime and notify SNS when the job fails.
choices.explanation: This stops the job based on elapsed time rather than at the time of detection and does not allow a healthy long-running job to continue.

choices.text: Configure only `StopTraining()` for the rule and output the profiler report to S3.
choices.explanation: The job can be stopped and the report can be saved, but no email is sent to the operator when the rule detects the issue.

learning.reason: Debugger lets you associate multiple actions with the result of a built-in rule. Notification and job termination are separate actions, and both can be executed by the same rule.
learning.concept: ActionList, StopTraining, and Email for Debugger rules

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Selecting a model by object-detection performance on validation images
prompt: A warehouse-image object-detection solution uses SageMaker built-in Object Detection. With AMT, you want to optimize the standard metric produced by the container that reflects class and location matches and summarizes multi-class detection performance on validation images. Which objective metric should you use?

choices.text: Minimize the mean absolute difference between the number of predicted boxes and the number of ground-truth boxes for each validation image.
choices.explanation: Matching the counts does not ensure that the classes or locations match. This is also different from the container's standard validation mAP.

choices.text: Maximize `validation:mAP`.
choices.explanation: This is the container's standard metric for summarizing validation-set performance by evaluating detection results for each class based on precision and recall.

choices.text: Fix one confidence threshold during validation and maximize only the precision of the detection results.
choices.explanation: Precision at one fixed threshold does not account for missed detections or behavior at other thresholds, and it is not the container's standard objective metric.

choices.text: Maximize `train:accuracy`.
choices.explanation: Accuracy on the training set does not evaluate the performance of predicted boxes and classes on validation images, nor is it this container's standard objective metric.

learning.reason: The built-in object-detection container reports mAP for the validation set. Object detection evaluates not only whether the class is correct but also whether the detection box sufficiently overlaps the corresponding ground-truth box.
learning.concept: Using validation:mAP with SageMaker built-in Object Detection and AMT

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Reproducing the hyperparameter candidates tested by random search
prompt: You are evaluating a different container image with SageMaker AMT random search. You use the same data, search ranges, and number of trials, and want the randomly selected hyperparameter candidates to match those from a previous comparison experiment. The randomness used by AMT and the randomness used for training by the container are independent. What should you configure on the AMT side?

choices.text: Set only `MaxParallelTrainingJobs` to 1 so that the same number of jobs as before run sequentially.
choices.explanation: Changing the degree of parallelism does not configure the random candidate selection to be the same as in the previous search.

choices.text: Set the best-scoring hyperparameters from the previous run as fixed values for every child job.
choices.explanation: This can retrain one previous candidate, but it does not reproduce the set of candidates compared during the previous random search.

choices.text: Set `HyperParameterTuningJobConfig.RandomSeed` to the same value used previously.
choices.explanation: With the search conditions aligned, this improves reproducibility of the randomly selected hyperparameter configurations.

choices.text: Specify the same random seed as before only in the training script inside the container.
choices.explanation: This can control randomness during model training, but it does not affect AMT's independent random selection of candidates.

learning.reason: A fixed AMT seed can reproduce the configurations proposed by the search. It must be managed separately from the seed used by the training code and from conditions that make the container's computations identical.
learning.concept: Comparing random searches with SageMaker AMT RandomSeed

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Evaluating the false-blocking rate for legitimate transactions
prompt: In a payment-model evaluation, fraud is defined as the positive class. Predictions on the validation data produced TP=90, FN=10, FP=45, and TN=855. A reviewer wants to determine the proportion of transactions that were actually legitimate but incorrectly blocked. Which value should be reported?

choices.text: Approximately 33%. Divide the 45 incorrectly blocked transactions by the 135 transactions that were blocked.
choices.explanation: This is the proportion of blocked transactions that were incorrect, not a value whose denominator is the population of legitimate transactions.

choices.text: 4.5%. Divide the 45 false positives by all 1,000 validation samples.
choices.explanation: This is the proportion of false positives among all validation samples and does not condition the denominator on legitimate transactions.

choices.text: 10%. Divide the 10 missed fraud cases by the 100 transactions that were actually fraudulent.
choices.explanation: This is the missed-fraud rate, which is different from the false-blocking rate for legitimate transactions.

choices.text: 5%. Divide the 45 false positives by the 900 transactions that were actually legitimate.
choices.explanation: Among legitimate transactions, the proportion predicted as positive is `FP / (FP + TN)`.

learning.reason: The false-positive rate is the proportion of the true negative class that is classified as positive, and it is the complement of specificity. The denominator must therefore contain only transactions that were actually legitimate.
learning.concept: Calculating the false-positive rate and distinguishing it from precision and recall

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Separating compute time and the total deadline for Spot training
prompt: You use SageMaker Managed Spot Training. The training container can already resume from checkpoints synchronized with S3. You want to limit training execution time to 90 minutes and set a 3-hour job window that includes capacity waiting and waiting for recovery after interruptions. After enabling `EnableManagedSpotTraining`, select two values to configure.

choices.text: Set `CheckpointConfig.LocalPath` to 5,400.
choices.explanation: This is a local checkpoint path, not a setting that controls execution time.

choices.text: Set `MaxRuntimeInSeconds` to 5,400.
choices.explanation: This specifies the 90-minute maximum training execution time in seconds.

choices.text: Set `MaxWaitTimeInSeconds` to 10,800.
choices.explanation: This sets the total job limit, including Spot-capacity waiting, to 3 hours.

choices.text: Set `MaxWaitTimeInSeconds` to 5,400.
choices.explanation: Using the same value as the execution limit would not provide a 3-hour window that includes capacity waiting and similar delays.

choices.text: Set `MaxRuntimeInSeconds` to 10,800.
choices.explanation: This would allow training itself to run for more than 90 minutes and would not satisfy the compute-time limit.

learning.reason: Managed Spot Training uses separate fields for the maximum training execution time and the total job limit, which includes waiting for an instance.
learning.concept: Combining MaxRuntimeInSeconds and MaxWaitTimeInSeconds for Managed Spot Training

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Learning Per-Account IPv4 Usage Patterns
prompt: An e-commerce service records the logged-in account ID and the source IPv4 address. There is little data confirmed to be fraudulent. The service must detect when an account logs in from a network that differs from its usual networks, but it must not treat the use as anomalous when the same IP address is a usual source address for another account. What training should be performed in SageMaker?

choices.text: Provide account ID and IPv4 pairs to IP Insights for unsupervised training.
choices.explanation: This learns normal pairings and produces a score based on the combination of the IPv4 address and the account.

choices.text: Train a Random Cut Forest using only the total number of logins for each IPv4 address as a feature.
choices.explanation: This can detect IPv4 addresses that are uncommon overall, but the account using the IPv4 address is not part of the training input.

choices.text: Aggregate the number of login times for each account and forecast the aggregate values with DeepAR.
choices.explanation: This can forecast changes in frequency, but it does not learn the combination of an account and an IP address.

choices.text: Aggregate IPv4 occurrence frequency across all accounts and create rules for each source IP address.
choices.explanation: Because the rules depend only on the IP address, they cannot evaluate the same IPv4 address differently for different accounts.

learning.reason: IP Insights uses unsupervised learning to learn usage patterns for entity-and-IPv4 pairs. Unlike frequency analysis based only on IP addresses, it can evaluate how anomalous an address is for a particular entity.
learning.concept: Entity-and-IPv4 pair input for IP Insights

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Updating Weights Beyond the Classification Layer with Transfer Learning
prompt: To classify infrared images, a team uses a pretrained model for visible-light images with SageMaker Image Classification - TensorFlow. In an experiment that updated only the classification layer, performance did not improve on the validation data. The team wants to run a comparison experiment that also adapts the backbone to infrared images. Which setting should be changed while retaining the pretrained weights as the initial values?

choices.text: Leave `train_only_top_layer` set to `True` and change only the input image size.
choices.explanation: Changing the input resolution does not change the setting that controls whether the backbone is trained.

choices.text: Set `train_only_top_layer` to `False` and fine-tune the entire network.
choices.explanation: Training starts from the pretrained weights, and the weights in the pretrained portion can be updated along with the classification layer.

choices.text: Leave `train_only_top_layer` set to `True` and increase the learning rate for the classification layer.
choices.explanation: This changes the update magnitude, but the backbone remains frozen.

choices.text: Do not load the pretrained weights; randomly initialize all layers and train the network.
choices.explanation: Although all layers can be updated, this does not satisfy the requirement to use the pretrained weights as the initial values.

learning.reason: Transfer learning can either use the pretrained portion without updating it or fine-tune the entire network starting from those weights.
learning.concept: Disabling train_only_top_layer in Image Classification - TensorFlow

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Assigning Different Processing to CPU and GPU Instance Groups
prompt: GPU instances were waiting because preprocessing was CPU-intensive, so a training job in SageMaker was configured with a CPU group and a GPU group. However, the current entry point runs the same processing on every host, and CPU hosts also begin distributed-training initialization. How should the roles be separated within the same job?

choices.text: Change each S3 input channel to `ShardedByS3Key`.
choices.explanation: This changes how input data is distributed, but it does not change the processing invoked on each host.

choices.text: Place the CPU and GPU instances in one distributed process group and start the GPU training process on every host.
choices.explanation: This leaves the problem of training initialization on CPU hosts and does not separate preprocessing from training.

choices.text: At startup, obtain the instance group of the current host, then start preprocessing in the CPU group and distributed training in the GPU group.
choices.explanation: The execution path is selected by group, so CPU hosts do not incorrectly join GPU distributed training.

choices.text: Rename the instance groups to `preprocess` and `train`, then run the same script unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing group names alone does not select different entry-point functions.

learning.reason: Creating instance groups alone does not assign processing to them. The training script must obtain the current host's group and select the appropriate execution path.
learning.concept: Role assignment with the SageMaker Training Toolkit in heterogeneous clusters

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Comparing Predictions for Similar Applicants Across Attribute Groups
prompt: An existing SageMaker Clarify environment is used to evaluate a review model. The overall predicted approval rates are similar across groups, but applicants with similar income and repayment histories can receive different approval predictions when they belong to different groups. Which post-training bias metric should be selected to compare each applicant in group d with a nearby applicant in group a and investigate the direction of differing predictions?

choices.text: Difference in Positive Proportions in Predicted Labels (DPPL)
choices.explanation: This calculates the difference in predicted approval rates between groups; it does not match applicants with nearby counterparts.

choices.text: Accuracy Difference (AD)
choices.explanation: This compares the agreement between predictions and true labels across groups. It is not a metric for comparing predictions for similar applicants.

choices.text: Disparate Impact (DI)
choices.explanation: This calculates the ratio of positive prediction rates for groups. It does not select observations in another group that are similar to each applicant.

choices.text: Counterfactual Fliptest (FT)
choices.explanation: This compares each applicant's prediction in group d with the prediction for a similar applicant in group a and counts unfavorable and favorable outcome differences by direction.

learning.reason: Counterfactual Fliptest compares each observation in group d with a nearby observation in group a. Because it handles prediction disagreements by direction, it can examine differences in treatment between similar applicants even when overall approval rates are similar.
learning.concept: Neighborhood-based comparison with Clarify Counterfactual Fliptest

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Changing the FSDP Shard Configuration When Resuming Training
prompt: A model is being trained with PyTorch FSDP in the SageMaker model parallelism library. In the next run, both the number of replicas and the number of model shards will change. The training must resume from the intermediate state, including the optimizer, without gathering the entire model into one process when saving. A shared file system is available. What should be saved?

choices.text: Save sharded checkpoints for the model and optimizer on the shared file system.
choices.explanation: The state for each rank is saved and can be loaded according to the changed device configuration during restoration.

choices.text: Use local checkpoints with `SM_LOCAL_STATE_DICT` and change the number of model shards.
choices.explanation: The local format can support a change in the number of model replicas, but the number of model shards must match when restoring.

choices.text: Gather all model weights into one rank and export only the weights for inference.
choices.explanation: This does not meet the requirement to avoid gathering the model, and weights alone cannot carry over the optimizer's intermediate state.

choices.text: Save only the training loss and the last processed step number to the shared file system.
choices.explanation: This preserves execution-position information but cannot restore the model and optimizer states.

learning.reason: SMP sharded checkpoints can be repartitioned when the device configuration changes so that training can resume. SMP's fast local checkpoints require the number of model shards to match.
learning.concept: Saving reshardable FSDP checkpoints with SageMaker SMP

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Sending Training Inputs in the Correct Order from an Augmented Manifest
prompt: Each line of an augmented manifest in S3 contains `source-ref`, `class-id`, and audit metadata. A custom SageMaker training container reads the inputs in the order of image data first and class ID second. Without changing the manifest or parser, which channel configuration passes no audit data?

choices.text: Use Pipe mode with `S3DataType=ManifestFile` and pass the class ID in the order of the JSON keys in the file.
choices.explanation: A standard manifest does not provide the attribute-selection mechanism for an augmented manifest. The order of the keys cannot be used to specify the order passed to the parser.

choices.text: Use Pipe mode and `S3DataType=AugmentedManifestFile`, with `AttributeNames` set to `['source-ref', 'class-id']`.
choices.explanation: This selects only the image reference and class ID and passes the image first, as expected by the container.

choices.text: Use Pipe mode and `S3DataType=AugmentedManifestFile`, with `AttributeNames` set to `['class-id', 'source-ref']`.
choices.explanation: The required attributes are present, but the class ID is passed first, so the input order is incorrect.

choices.text: Use File mode while keeping `S3DataType=AugmentedManifestFile` and specifying both attributes.
choices.explanation: File mode is not supported for a channel that uses an augmented manifest.

learning.reason: A training channel that uses an augmented manifest must use Pipe mode. The items sent and their order are determined by the order in `AttributeNames`, not by the order of JSON keys.
learning.concept: Ordering `AttributeNames` with AugmentedManifestFile and Pipe mode

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Removing Results Available Only During Training from the Features
prompt: A delivery delay is predicted at the time of shipment. A SageMaker validation shows high accuracy, but in the deployment environment, `days_to_delivery` and `first_delivery_attempt_outcome` in the history table are unavailable. The remaining data contains the shipment time and the destination region known at that time. Before recalibrating the existing model's output in production, what should be rebuilt?

choices.text: Keep the two fields from historical training and fill their production missing values with the median and mode from the training data.
choices.explanation: The result information was available during training but is not available during inference, so constant imputation does not make the training and production conditions match.

choices.text: Randomly repartition the history to smooth shipment-time bias, while retaining the two fields.
choices.explanation: Changing the split method does not remove post-prediction information from the features in each row.

choices.text: Create only features available at the shipment time for each shipment, and rerun training and validation. Use the confirmed delay as the ground-truth label.
choices.explanation: This excludes information that becomes available after shipment and evaluates the model using the same inputs available during deployment.

choices.text: Remove the two fields only from the validation data and use the current model without retraining.
choices.explanation: The model used the two fields during training, so the input contract and evaluation conditions do not match.

learning.reason: Align the time at which each feature becomes available across training, evaluation, and inference. Including fields determined after the outcome is known introduces information into evaluation that is unavailable in production.
learning.concept: Preventing data leakage from features occurring after the prediction time

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Calibrating Confidence While Preserving Classification Rankings
prompt: An image classifier performs well enough based on class rankings, but images with predicted probabilities near 0.90 have an observed accuracy of about 0.70. The probabilities will be used to prioritize reviews, so confidence must be calibrated without changing the model weights or class rankings. An independent labeled calibration set, separate from training and final testing, is available. Which method should be selected?

choices.text: Keep the current raw probabilities and change only the threshold used to select items for review.
choices.explanation: This can change the number of reviews but does not calibrate the confidence represented by the probabilities.

choices.text: Update the weights for each class in the classification layer using the final test set, and report calibration accuracy on that same set.
choices.explanation: The model weights and rankings may change, and adjustment and final evaluation are not independent.

choices.text: Remove all classes below the second class in the prediction vector and replace the top-class probability with 1 for every prediction.
choices.explanation: Although the ranking can be preserved, this does not resolve overconfidence and eliminates the confidence differences needed to distinguish correct from incorrect predictions.

choices.text: Estimate one positive temperature on the calibration set for the fixed model's logits and apply it before softmax.
choices.explanation: This adjusts probabilities while preserving class rankings and model weights, and the calibration result can be evaluated on an independent test set.

learning.reason: Dividing all class logits by the same positive temperature before calculating softmax adjusts probability concentration while preserving class rankings. Estimate the temperature on the calibration set and reserve the final test set for evaluation.
learning.concept: Post-hoc calibration of classification probabilities with temperature scaling

category: MLモデルの開発
examDomain: MLモデルの開発
title: Aligning Neural Topic Model Input Dimensions with the Vocabulary
prompt: A SageMaker Neural Topic Model is being trained. When product reviews are represented using a shared vocabulary of 12,000 words, each review has at most 80 nonzero elements. The business team wants to organize the reviews into 24 topics. When using the vocabulary indices directly, which training settings should be used?

choices.text: Set `feature_dim=12000` and `num_topics=24`.
choices.explanation: The input dimension represents the entire vocabulary index, and the number of topics to train matches the requirement.

choices.text: Set `feature_dim=80` and `num_topics=24`.
choices.explanation: Eighty is the maximum number of words used in one document; it cannot represent the feature indices for all 12,000 words.

choices.text: Set `feature_dim=24` and `num_topics=80`.
choices.explanation: This confuses both the feature dimension and the number of topics with quantities that have different meanings.

choices.text: Set `feature_dim=12000` and `num_topics=80`.
choices.explanation: The vocabulary dimension is correct, but the business requirement specifies 24 topics.

learning.reason: Even when a sparse input has only a small number of nonzero elements per document, the feature dimension is the size of the entire vocabulary. The number of topics to extract is specified by a separate hyperparameter.
learning.concept: Separating `feature_dim` and `num_topics` in SageMaker NTM

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Processing a Large CSV Without Expanding It into the State Machine Input
prompt: A CSV containing several million rows is stored in S3, and Lambda calls a model for each row. At the start of the Step Functions execution, only the bucket name and key can be passed, and the entire CSV cannot be placed in the state payload. Which configuration should be used to process each CSV row in parallel child executions?

choices.text: Convert the CSV to a JSON array in a preceding step and pass the entire array to an Inline Map's `ItemsPath`.
choices.explanation: The array passed to the parent state would exceed the payload limit.

choices.text: Pass the CSV's S3 URI as a string to the Distributed Map's `ItemsPath`.
choices.explanation: `ItemsPath` selects items that already exist in the state input; it does not retrieve a CSV from a URI and expand it into rows.

choices.text: Specify the input CSV path in the Distributed Map's `ResultWriter`.
choices.explanation: `ResultWriter` configures where child execution results are written; it does not configure dataset reading.

choices.text: Specify the S3 CSV and input format in the Distributed Map's `ItemReader`.
choices.explanation: This reads each row from the CSV in S3 and passes it to child executions without placing a huge row array in the parent execution input.

learning.reason: The Distributed Map `ItemReader` can read an S3 CSV directly as a dataset. Only a reference to the target file needs to be included in the execution input, and the rows can be distributed to child executions.
learning.concept: Specifying an S3 CSV directly with `ItemReader` in a Distributed Map

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Passing Only Approved Model Versions to Automated Deployment
prompt: Model packages are registered in the SageMaker Model Registry with `PendingManualApproval`. Only approved versions in the target model group should be deployed. The deployment process removes duplicates by package ARN. Without polling periodically, how should the ARN of an approved version be passed to the process?

choices.text: Subscribe in EventBridge to `SageMaker Model Package State Change` events for the target group and pass packages with `ModelApprovalStatus=Approved` to the deployment process.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes completion of package creation from human deployment approval and deploys the version associated with the relevant event.

choices.text: Subscribe only to state changes with `ModelPackageStatus=Completed` and deploy completed versions.
choices.explanation: This indicates that package creation is complete; it does not indicate that human approval for deployment is complete.

choices.text: Deploy immediately after `CreateModelPackage` succeeds in the target group and monitor rejection events afterward.
choices.explanation: Because the approval state is pending at creation time, deployment would begin before review.

choices.text: Subscribe to events indicating that the deployment target's SageMaker endpoint has reached `InService`.
choices.explanation: This reports the result of a deployment that has already occurred and cannot determine approval of a registry version.

learning.reason: A Model Package State Change event includes information identifying the approval state and package. Restrict the event pattern to approved packages in the target group and use that version as the deployment input.
learning.concept: Filtering SageMaker model package state changes by approval status with EventBridge

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Reconsidering Caching for Inference with Little Model Reuse
prompt: A CPU-based SageMaker multi-model endpoint serves many small models. In this batch, each request calls a different model, so the same model is rarely accessed again. Load testing shows frequent model-cache evictions and low throughput. While keeping the multi-model configuration, which change should be tried?

choices.text: Place all models in a single serial inference pipeline.
choices.explanation: An inference pipeline makes containers process requests sequentially; it does not dynamically select the one model needed for each request.

choices.text: Set `ModelCacheSetting` to `Disabled` in the model container configuration and measure again with the same request distribution.
choices.explanation: Disabling a cache that is unlikely to be reused can reduce cache churn and may improve the parallelism of model loading.

choices.text: Keep caching enabled and send repeated requests to the same models in advance.
choices.explanation: Warming specific models does not help much when the production batch subsequently selects different models.

choices.text: Replace every request's `TargetModel` so that it returns only one model.
choices.explanation: This may change the cache-hit rate, but it violates the requirement to perform inference with the specified models.

learning.reason: A multi-model endpoint cache avoids loading models that are accessed repeatedly. When access is mostly one-time, disabling the cache can reduce processing associated with evictions in some workloads.
learning.concept: `MultiModelConfig.ModelCacheSetting` for multi-model endpoints

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Secure inference capacity ahead of predictable peak hours
prompt: A SageMaker real-time endpoint adjusts its instance count using target tracking. Traffic surges at 9:00 AM on business days, and scaling out after the load increases is too late. You want to keep normal capacity low outside business hours while continuing target tracking based on demand after the additional capacity is provisioned. Which setting should you add?

choices.text: Only shorten the cooldown periods for target tracking.
choices.explanation: This can affect response speed, but it does not provision the required capacity in advance of a known start time.

choices.text: Remove the existing tracking policy and set the endpoint to a fixed instance count required during business hours.
choices.explanation: Keeping a high capacity at all times prevents low capacity outside business hours and eliminates tracking-based adjustment.

choices.text: Use a scheduled action before business begins to increase the variant's minimum instance count, and another scheduled action after business hours to restore the normal minimum instance count.
choices.explanation: This provisions the required initial capacity in advance, after which the existing target-tracking policy continues to operate within the specified range.

choices.text: Use a scheduled action before business begins to increase only the maximum instance count, without changing the minimum instance count.
choices.explanation: Increasing the upper limit does not cause a preemptive scale-out if the current capacity is already within that range.

learning.reason: When an increase in load is predictable, scheduled scaling can raise the lower bound of the capacity for the scalable target in advance. Restoring the normal lower bound after the peak allows the existing target-tracking policy to continue adjusting capacity within that range.
learning.concept: Increasing and decreasing the minimum capacity of a SageMaker production variant with Application Auto Scaling schedules

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Update the inference Lambda execution image using the same ECR tag
prompt: A Lambda function that performs preprocessing and inference for a small model runs with the `scoring:release` image in Amazon ECR. You pushed a new image with the same tag, but an unqualified function invocation still uses the old model. How can you apply the new image to the latest code of this function?

choices.text: Verify that the tag in ECR points to a new digest, then wait for the Lambda execution environment to update naturally.
choices.explanation: The function configuration still references the old digest, so recreating the execution environment does not automatically change the referenced image.

choices.text: Only publish an additional Lambda version from the existing function code.
choices.explanation: The new version would freeze the current function code. The function code must first be updated to use the new image.

choices.text: Update the Lambda timeout and memory to launch a new execution environment.
choices.explanation: Changing the configuration does not update the code by resolving the function's image URI again.

choices.text: Run Lambda `UpdateFunctionCode` with an `ImageUri` that points to the new image.
choices.explanation: Even when the same tag string is specified, the new digest at the time of the code update can be associated with the function.

learning.reason: Lambda resolves an image tag to a digest when the image is deployed. Moving the tag in ECR alone does not switch the image referenced by the function.
learning.concept: The boundary between updating an ECR tag and Lambda UpdateFunctionCode

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Remove the old inference Pod only after the load balancer can receive traffic
prompt: An inference API Pod on EKS is being updated with a rolling deployment. The deployment uses the AWS Load Balancer Controller and an ALB with IP targets. The readiness probe inside the Pod succeeds first, but the old Pod is terminated before the new Pod becomes a healthy target in the ALB, causing temporary inference failures. What should you configure to keep the old Pod until the new Pod is ready to receive traffic both inside the container and through the ALB?

choices.text: Enable the AWS Load Balancer Controller Pod Readiness Gate and include ALB target health in the Pod's readiness conditions.
choices.explanation: Even when the container itself is ready, the Pod does not become ready until the new Pod is registered as healthy in the ALB.

choices.text: Run the container liveness probe at short intervals.
choices.explanation: This checks whether the process is running more frequently, but it does not include the ALB target registration state in the Pod's readiness conditions.

choices.text: Increase the number of successful readiness-probe checks and switch over after allowing the same fixed waiting time in every environment.
choices.explanation: This can provide a fixed grace period, but it cannot directly make completion of healthy ALB registration the condition for readiness.

choices.text: Change the ALB health check to a path that succeeds before the application loads the model.
choices.explanation: This only makes the ALB declare success earlier; it does not ensure that inference is actually possible or synchronize the Kubernetes and ALB states.

learning.reason: Load balancer target registration and application readiness are separate states. The AWS Load Balancer Controller Pod Readiness Gate can delay the Pod's overall readiness until the target becomes healthy.
learning.concept: Enabling the Pod Readiness Gate for EKS ALB IP targets

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Branch model registration based on the evaluation result from each execution
prompt: A SageMaker Pipelines evaluation `ProcessingStep` outputs `evaluation.json` to Amazon S3. You want to automatically register only the model from the same execution whose `metrics.recall.value` is at least 0.92. How can you branch based on the JSON from each execution without having a person transcribe the evaluation result?

choices.text: Pass the output path of the `ProcessingStep` to the condition as a string and compare it with 0.92.
choices.explanation: The output URI identifies the evaluation result, but by itself it does not extract the numeric value from the JSON.

choices.text: Associate a `PropertyFile` with the evaluation step, use `JsonGet` in a `ConditionStep` to retrieve and compare the value, and put model registration in the step that runs when the condition is met.
choices.explanation: This branches on the evaluation value at runtime, so only a model that passes the condition is registered.

choices.text: Define recall as a fixed `ParameterFloat` for reproducibility and set its value to 0.92.
choices.explanation: An execution input parameter can serve as a comparison threshold, but it is not the recall measured by the evaluation step.

choices.text: Run model registration unconditionally after the evaluation process succeeds and attach the evaluation JSON as model metrics during registration.
choices.explanation: The evaluation result can be tracked, but models that fail to meet the threshold would also be registered.

learning.reason: Associating the evaluation JSON with the processing step as a `PropertyFile` allows `JsonGet` to reference the output from the same execution. Downstream steps can branch based on whether the numeric comparison succeeds.
learning.concept: Using SageMaker `PropertyFile`, `JsonGet`, and `ConditionStep` as an evaluation gate

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Retaining model regression test results for audit by build
prompt: Before deploying a model with AWS CodeBuild, a developer runs regression tests and generates JUnit XML. The developer wants to review future results in CodeBuild for each build. The original XML must be retained for at least 90 days for auditing, and an existing audit S3 bucket meets the retention requirement. Which configuration should be added?

choices.text: Save the JUnit XML to S3 as a regular build artifact and do not create a report group.
choices.explanation: This can retain the XML for a long period, but it does not generate the detailed test report view in CodeBuild.

choices.text: Output the test and failure counts to CloudWatch Logs and extend the log retention period.
choices.explanation: This can retain aggregate counts for a long period, but it does not retain a per-build test report or the original JUnit XML.

choices.text: Use `reports` in the buildspec to ingest the JUnit XML into a report group, then export the raw data from that report group to S3.
choices.explanation: The details can be reviewed in CodeBuild, and the original files exported to S3 can be retained after the report expires.

choices.text: Use `reports` in the buildspec to ingest the XML and view the report in CodeBuild. Do not configure an S3 export.
choices.explanation: The report can be displayed for each build, but a CodeBuild test report expires after 30 days.

learning.reason: CodeBuild creates a per-build report from test files. Because service-hosted reports have an expiration period, long-term auditing requires exporting the source test files to S3.
learning.concept: The CodeBuild buildspec `reports` section and report-group S3 export

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Deleting only the validation stack while retaining the inference-results bucket
prompt: A SageMaker inference environment for validation is created with CloudFormation and is deleted as a stack after validation. An S3 bucket created in the stack contains inference results for auditing. The bucket and its objects must be retained while allowing the stack deletion to succeed. Which setting should be added to the bucket?

choices.text: Set only `UpdateReplacePolicy` to `Retain` on the S3 bucket resource.
choices.explanation: This affects the old resource when an update replaces the bucket, but this scenario deletes the stack.

choices.text: Enable termination protection for the stack.
choices.explanation: This blocks deletion of the entire stack and therefore does not satisfy the requirement to clean up only the inference environment.

choices.text: Leave the S3 bucket resource unchanged and use a bucket policy to deny deletion by CloudFormation.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation may fail when it attempts the deletion. This does not specify that the bucket should remain while the stack deletion succeeds.

choices.text: Set `DeletionPolicy` to `Retain` on the S3 bucket resource.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation retains the bucket and continues deleting the stack. The objects in the bucket are also not deleted by this operation.

learning.reason: To remove a specific resource from management without deleting it when a CloudFormation stack is deleted, set that resource's DeletionPolicy to Retain.
learning.concept: Using CloudFormation DeletionPolicy to retain an S3 bucket during stack deletion

examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Splitting one input file to use multiple transform instances
prompt: A large CSV is being used for inference with SageMaker Batch Transform. Even after increasing the job from one instance to eight, processing is slow and only one instance is processing the input. The input is a single object in S3, each CSV row is independent, and ordering is unnecessary. What should be changed to process the input in parallel across multiple instances?

choices.text: Split the CSV at record boundaries into multiple S3 objects and use them as inputs to the same job.
choices.explanation: Because the job processes multiple independent objects, different instances can handle different objects.

choices.text: Keep a single object and specify only `SplitType=Line` and `BatchStrategy=MultiRecord`.
choices.explanation: This changes how mini-batches are formed for the container, but the assignment of the input object to an instance remains unchanged.

choices.text: Keep a single object and increase `MaxConcurrentTransforms`.
choices.explanation: This controls the number of simultaneous requests that can be sent to each instance; it does not divide the job's input among different instances.

choices.text: Keep a single object and decrease `MaxPayloadInMB`.
choices.explanation: This changes the size limit for each request, but it does not divide the S3 object into eight objects.

learning.reason: Batch Transform assigns S3 input objects to instances by key. Mini-batches within the same object do not divide responsibility for the input file among different instances.
learning.concept: Distributing Batch Transform input at the S3-object level

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Continuing an inference session on the same model instance
prompt: An application sends an image only once and then makes multiple inference requests about that image. The container for the SageMaker real-time endpoint supports stateful sessions and retains the initial image only for the duration of the session. Put the steps in order to start a new session and route subsequent requests to the same instance.

choices.text: Obtain the new session ID from the response to the start request.
choices.explanation: This is required to identify the created session in subsequent calls.

choices.text: Set the returned session ID in `SessionId` and send subsequent inference requests about the image.
choices.explanation: Using the existing session ID routes the requests to the same model instance that retains the image.

choices.text: Send a start request to the endpoint containing the image and setting `SessionId=NEW_SESSION`.
choices.explanation: This requests that the container create a new session and retain the image.

learning.reason: Request a new session in the first InvokeEndpoint call. Passing the returned session ID in the next request causes SageMaker to route the request to the model instance that retains the session.
learning.concept: Distinguishing session creation and continuation with InvokeEndpoint and SessionId

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
