title: Run a Feature Engineering Job on an Existing EMR Cluster
prompt: In SageMaker Pipelines, use an existing Spark JAR to aggregate features before training. The company-standard EMR on EC2 cluster is running, and its libraries and access permissions are already configured. You want the pipeline to track job completion while leaving the cluster in place. Which step should you configure?

choices.text: Register a process that runs on a schedule on the existing cluster, and have the pipeline start the training step at the same time every run.
choices.explanation: This does not link aggregation success or completion to the start of training, so training might use the previous run's output.

choices.text: Specify the existing cluster's `cluster_id` and an `EMRStepConfig` containing the JAR location and arguments in an `EMRStep`.
choices.explanation: This submits the process to the running cluster and allows the pipeline to track the EMR step's success or failure.

choices.text: Pass a `cluster_config` for a new cluster to an `EMRStep` and specify the same name as the existing cluster.
choices.explanation: Even with the same name, this defines a new cluster configuration and does not reference the ID of the running cluster.

choices.text: Create a Spark `ProcessingStep`, pass it the JAR, and set the EMR cluster name as an environment variable.
choices.explanation: The process runs in the environment started by SageMaker Processing. Merely passing the cluster name does not submit a Spark job to the existing EMR cluster.

learning.reason: SageMaker Pipelines' EMRStep distinguishes submitting a process to an existing cluster from creating a new cluster. You can specify the existing cluster's ID and track the Spark step's status.
learning.concept: Using `cluster_id` and `EMRStepConfig` in an EMRStep to specify an existing EMR cluster

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Send Only Low-Confidence Predictions from a Custom Model for Human Review
prompt: Using an existing Amazon Augmented AI environment, integrate a custom classification model on SageMaker into a review interface. You want to request review from the work team for a custom task only when the confidence score is below 0.78. The flow definition for the custom task has already been created. Which method should you use to start the review?

choices.text: Add a condition to SageMaker Data Capture and start an A2I task when a low-confidence response is captured.
choices.explanation: Data Capture stores inference data; its configuration alone does not invoke the flow definition.

choices.text: Call `StartHumanLoop` for every prediction and instruct the work team to ignore high-confidence predictions.
choices.explanation: All predictions would be sent to the work team, so this does not meet the requirement to send only low-confidence predictions.

choices.text: Have the application evaluate the prediction's confidence score and, only when it is below 0.78, call `StartHumanLoop` with the custom task's flow definition specified.
choices.explanation: The caller determines whether a custom task is needed and sends only the required predictions to the work team.

choices.text: Add a confidence condition to the custom task's flow definition so that human review starts when the classifier is called.
choices.explanation: A2I custom task flow definitions do not support a confidence condition that automatically starts human review.

learning.reason: For an A2I custom task, the application implements the review-start condition and calls `StartHumanLoop`. Confidence conditions intended for built-in integrations are not specified in a custom task flow definition.
learning.concept: Conditions for calling `StartHumanLoop` from an application for an A2I custom task

category: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
examDomain: MLワークフローのデプロイとオーケストレーション
title: Test a New Model on the Same Requests Without Changing Production Responses
prompt: Before replacing the model on a SageMaker real-time endpoint, evaluate the candidate version's latency and error rate using the actual input distribution. Send the requests being evaluated to both the current and candidate versions, but always return only the current version's response to users. How should you connect the new candidate version?

choices.text: Add the candidate version as a production variant with a 5% weight.
choices.explanation: With normal variant distribution, one of the two variants handles each request, so some users receive the candidate version's response.

choices.text: Do not deploy the candidate version to the endpoint; add its benchmark results to the current version's metrics.
choices.explanation: This cannot evaluate the candidate version by copying production requests and does not meet the requirement to compare it using the actual input distribution.

choices.text: Specify the candidate version with `TargetVariant` for every request and record only the current version's model name in the response.
choices.explanation: Changing the recorded name does not change the fact that the candidate version's response is returned to the client.

choices.text: Deploy the candidate version as a shadow variant on the same endpoint and duplicate a configured percentage of requests.
choices.explanation: This measures behavior on the same inputs without returning the candidate version's response to the client.

learning.reason: Shadow testing duplicates requests from the production variant and runs them on the shadow variant. Only the production variant's response is returned to the client.
learning.concept: How SageMaker shadow variants duplicate requests while separating the response returned to users

title: Verify Whether Training Audit Logs Were Altered After Delivery
prompt: CloudTrail is delivering SageMaker operation logs to an audit S3 bucket. For the next audit period, the audit team wants to be able to verify whether delivered log files were altered or deleted afterward. S3 Versioning is already enabled. Which procedure should you add?

choices.text: Enable SSE-KMS and only verify that the retrieved logs can be decrypted.
choices.explanation: This verifies encryption at rest but cannot prove that all original delivered logs remain present and their contents are unchanged.

choices.text: Enable log file integrity validation for the trail and, during the audit, validate the target period with `aws cloudtrail validate-logs`.
choices.explanation: This verifies digest signatures and log hashes to determine whether delivered logs were modified or deleted.

choices.text: Configure S3 event notifications to notify the team whenever a new log object is delivered.
choices.explanation: This tracks log arrival but does not compare the signed delivery contents with the current files.

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail Insights and detect log deletion as an anomaly in the API call rate.
choices.explanation: This can detect API activity trends but does not validate the integrity of delivered files against their digests.

learning.reason: CloudTrail delivers signed digests for trails with integrity validation enabled. Verifying the digests and logs on the audit side detects changes or missing files after delivery.
learning.concept: CloudTrail log file integrity validation and signed digests

title: Verify that training buckets are not shared outside the permitted organization
prompt: Training data is managed across multiple AWS accounts. Sharing within the organization is permitted, but a bucket policy may previously have granted permissions to accounts in another organization. What should be used to detect access currently granted externally by the policy, even before the access is actually used?

choices.text: Use an unused access analyzer in IAM Access Analyzer to check only unused permissions for roles in the organization.
choices.explanation: Checking unused permissions for roles is a different evaluation from detecting exposure outside the organization through an S3 resource policy.

choices.text: Use an Amazon Macie sensitive data discovery job to classify the contents of the bucket.
choices.explanation: This can identify sensitive data, but the job alone cannot determine whether access was granted to principals outside the organization.

choices.text: Use an external access analyzer in the target Region with the organization as the trust zone.
choices.explanation: It can detect S3 bucket policies that grant access to external principals without waiting for the access to be exercised.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail S3 data events for each bucket to look for `GetObject` calls made from another organization.
choices.explanation: Actual API calls can be confirmed, but permissions that have not been used cannot be detected.

learning.reason: The IAM Access Analyzer external access analyzer produces findings when a resource-based policy grants access outside the trust zone. Setting the organization as the trust zone excludes internal sharing.
learning.concept: Detecting external access with an IAM Access Analyzer organization trust zone

title: Continuously measure the number of tokens used in inference logs
prompt: The inference application writes JSON logs in the standard CloudWatch Logs class, with a numeric `output_tokens` value for each request. Without redeploying the application, you want to publish the total number of tokens from new logs to CloudWatch every five minutes and set an alarm on that total. Which configuration should you choose?

choices.text: Publish a numeric value of 1 for each matching log event and set an alarm on the five-minute `Sum`.
choices.explanation: This counts requests, but it cannot add the different token counts for individual requests.

choices.text: Extend the log group's retention period and aggregate the data with Logs Insights only when needed.
choices.explanation: This supports analysis of historical logs, but it does not continuously publish numeric values from new logs for alarm evaluation.

choices.text: Use the `output_tokens` value as a dimension and publish a value of 1.
choices.explanation: This separates metrics by token count; it does not configure one metric that sums the token count for requests.

choices.text: Create a metric filter that extracts `output_tokens` and publishes that number as the value. Set an alarm on the five-minute `Sum`.
choices.explanation: The token count for each request, rather than the number of log events, is sent to CloudWatch, allowing the period total to be evaluated.

learning.reason: A metric filter for a log group can publish a numeric field from JSON as the metric value. Use the metric's Sum statistic to monitor the total during a period.
learning.concept: CloudWatch Logs JSON metric filters and aggregation of numeric fields

title: Handle missing data for a metric published only during anomalies
prompt: A post-inference inspection process publishes an error count to CloudWatch only when anomalous records are found; it does not publish the metric during periods with no anomalies. Separate liveness monitoring that detects the absence of traffic is already operating, and you want the error-count alarm to treat missing data points as normal. Which setting is appropriate?

choices.text: Set `TreatMissingData` to `notBreaching`.
choices.explanation: When missing-data handling is applied, the missing data points are evaluated as points that do not breach the threshold.

choices.text: Set `TreatMissingData` to `breaching`.
choices.explanation: This interprets periods with no published point because there was no anomaly as equivalent to a threshold breach.

choices.text: Set `TreatMissingData` to `ignore`.
choices.explanation: This keeps the alarm state when data is missing; it does not treat missing points as normal.

choices.text: Set `TreatMissingData` to `missing`.
choices.explanation: The alarm can become `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` when the evaluation range contains only missing data; this does not specify that missing data is normal.

learning.reason: When measured points required for evaluation are missing, a CloudWatch alarm can treat them as breaching, not breaching, ignored, or missing. A metric published only during anomalies can use the normal interpretation for periods without errors.
learning.concept: Using TreatMissingData=notBreaching for an intermittent error metric

title: Detect an unusual surge in the job-creation API
prompt: The CloudTrail trail captures write management events. Some weeks create training jobs frequently and other weeks create few jobs, so you do not want to maintain a fixed-count threshold. You want to investigate, as audit events, periods when `CreateTrainingJob` is called at an unusual rate compared with the normal pattern of management API calls. What should you configure?

choices.text: Add data events for the SageMaker inference endpoint and monitor the number of calls.
choices.explanation: The operation that invokes inference and the management operation that creates a training job are different.

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail Insights API call rate in the trail.
choices.explanation: It compares the call rate for write management events with the normal pattern and makes unusual periods available for investigation as Insights events.

choices.text: Enable only CloudTrail Insights API error rate.
choices.explanation: This detects anomalies in the error rate, but it does not detect a large increase in successful creation requests as a call-rate anomaly.

choices.text: Use only AWS Config configuration history and arrange job changes chronologically.
choices.explanation: Configuration history for resources is different from detecting deviation from the normal frequency of management API calls.

learning.reason: CloudTrail Insights API call rate compares the call rate of write management APIs with its baseline and identifies unusual activity as an Insights event.
learning.concept: Detecting a surge in management operations with CloudTrail Insights API call rate

title: Restricting a customer managed key to a specific inference log group
prompt: SageMaker inference diagnostic logs are delivered to CloudWatch Logs, and an AWS KMS customer managed key is associated with a specific log group. The security requirement is to restrict the key policy for CloudWatch Logs so that the key cannot be used to encrypt other log groups in the same Region. Which approach should be used?

choices.text: Restrict the Region using only the service name in `kms:ViaService`, without specifying the target log group ARN.
choices.explanation: This can restrict the service through which the request is made, but it does not constrain use to a particular log group.

choices.text: Encrypt the training job's temporary storage with the same key. Do not restrict the CloudWatch Logs permissions in the key policy.
choices.explanation: The training-storage configuration does not restrict key usage by log group.

choices.text: In the permission for the Regional CloudWatch Logs service principal, add a condition requiring `kms:EncryptionContext:aws:logs:arn` to equal the target log group ARN.
choices.explanation: Even for calls made by CloudWatch Logs, permission is granted only when the context matches the specified log group.

choices.text: Allow the Regional CloudWatch Logs service principal to encrypt and decrypt without a context condition.
choices.explanation: The service and Region are restricted, but the target log group within the same Region is not.

learning.reason: CloudWatch Logs includes the log group ARN in the KMS encryption context. Restricting both the service principal and the context in the key policy allows use only for the target log group.
learning.concept: The `kms:EncryptionContext:aws:logs:arn` key-policy condition for CloudWatch Logs

title: Promoting verified connection information to the current version
prompt: A job that retrieves training data obtains connection information from Secrets Manager without specifying a version. A Lambda rotation using alternating users has applied the new information to the service, and connectivity testing with the `AWSPENDING` information has succeeded. What should `finishSecret` do last?

choices.text: Remove `AWSPENDING` first and leave `AWSCURRENT` on the existing version.
choices.explanation: Callers that retrieve the secret normally would continue using the previous information.

choices.text: Modify all training jobs so that they always read `AWSPENDING` in the future.
choices.explanation: `AWSPENDING` identifies the candidate version during rotation; it does not identify the verified current version.

choices.text: Leave the version labels unchanged and only shorten the rotation interval.
choices.explanation: Changing the launch interval does not make the version verified in this rotation the normal version retrieved by callers.

choices.text: Move `AWSCURRENT` to the new version.
choices.explanation: The verified information becomes the normal version retrieved by callers. The previous current version is treated as `AWSPREVIOUS`.

learning.reason: During Secrets Manager rotation, `AWSCURRENT` is moved to the new version after connectivity testing succeeds. Retrieval without a version uses the information carrying that label.
learning.concept: Moving `AWSCURRENT` in `finishSecret` during Secrets Manager rotation

title: Reducing storage charges for incomplete artifact transfers
prompt: When a client uploading training artifacts is interrupted, incomplete parts of a multipart upload remain in Amazon S3. While retaining completed objects, what should be configured to automatically remove only upload parts that have remained incomplete for 10 days or more?

choices.text: Set `DaysAfterInitiation` to 10 for `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload`.
choices.explanation: Uploads that have not been completed within 10 days can be aborted, removing the stored parts.

choices.text: Set the expiration of the current version to 10 days in an S3 Lifecycle rule.
choices.explanation: This expires the current version of completed objects and cannot target only incomplete parts.

choices.text: Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to permanently delete noncurrent versions after 10 days.
choices.explanation: Incomplete parts are not noncurrent versions of completed objects.

choices.text: Transition completed objects with the same prefix to S3 Glacier.
choices.explanation: This changes the cost structure for completed objects, but it does not remove parts remaining in incomplete uploads.

learning.reason: The S3 Lifecycle abort-incomplete-multipart-upload action targets incomplete uploads whose age since initiation meets the condition. It does not apply to objects that have already been completed.
learning.concept: S3 Lifecycle `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` and `DaysAfterInitiation`

title: Detecting input-distribution changes when the schema is unchanged
prompt: An existing SageMaker Model Monitor monitors the `order_value` in inference inputs. The column name, numeric data type, and non-NULL rate are the same as in the baseline data, but the proportion of high-value orders has increased sharply. Which violation indicates that the distribution distance from the approved baseline data exceeded the configured comparison threshold?

choices.text: `extra_column_check`
choices.explanation: This checks for columns added relative to the baseline; it does not compare the value distribution of an existing column.

choices.text: `baseline_drift_check`
choices.explanation: This determines the distribution distance between current data and baseline data, so it can report a violation even when the column type and non-NULL rate are valid.

choices.text: `data_type_check`
choices.explanation: This checks for differences between the inference-input type and the baseline type. A change in the proportion of numeric values is not a reason for this violation when the type is unchanged.

choices.text: `completeness_check`
choices.explanation: This checks the proportion of non-NULL values, so it does not represent a distribution change when the missing-value rate remains the same.

learning.reason: Model Monitor's comparison with the baseline distribution is independent of checks for column presence, data type, and missing-value rate. When the distribution distance exceeds the comparison threshold, `baseline_drift_check` is reported.
learning.concept: SageMaker Model Monitor `baseline_drift_check` and `comparison_threshold`

title: Deploy multiple configuration checks across the organization for the learning environment
prompt: AWS Config recording has already been started in each member account of AWS Organizations. The organization administrator wants to specify the company’s set of Config rules and remediation configurations for the learning S3 bucket and inference network as one package, and deploy the same configuration to the same Region so that settings do not differ by team. Which configuration is appropriate?

choices.text: Describe the same configuration in an Audit Manager assessment and create an audit report.
choices.explanation: This can collect assessment evidence, but it does not configure Config rules or remediation for the member accounts.

choices.text: Write the list of Config rule names in an SCP and attach it to the Organizations root.
choices.explanation: An SCP defines the maximum permissions available in an account. It does not deploy a set of Config rules and remediation settings.

choices.text: Define the approved Config rules and required remediation actions in YAML, and deploy them as an organization conformance pack.
choices.explanation: An organization conformance pack can distribute common configuration checks and remediation as a package to accounts in the organization.

choices.text: Create only an AWS Config aggregator for the organization and aggregate data from all accounts.
choices.explanation: An aggregator can collect evaluation results from existing rules, but it does not deploy new rules or remediation actions to member accounts.

learning.reason: Multiple AWS Config rules and remediation actions can be defined as a conformance pack. A custom organization conformance pack can be distributed to member accounts in bulk.

title: Reduce ingestion charges for training debug logs that are rarely investigated
prompt: Diagnostic events from a SageMaker training container can be separated through application changes into logs for operational alarms and logs for detailed debugging. The detailed logs will be searched with Logs Insights only once every few months, and subscriptions and metric filters are not required. Which configuration should be selected to reduce future CloudWatch Logs ingestion charges for the detailed logs?

choices.text: Change only the class of the existing Standard group used for alarms to Infrequent Access.
choices.explanation: The class of a created log group cannot be changed. This also fails to separate the alarm logs from the detailed logs.

choices.text: Shorten only the retention period of the Standard group.
choices.explanation: This may reduce the amount of stored data, but it does not reduce future ingestion charges.

choices.text: Send the detailed logs to the Delivery class for Lambda and investigate everything with CloudWatch Logs Insights.
choices.explanation: The Delivery class is intended to deliver logs from services such as Lambda to specified destinations and does not fit a configuration based on Logs Insights searches.

choices.text: Create a new log group with the Infrequent Access class for detailed debugging and send future detailed logs there.
choices.explanation: This reduces the ingestion unit price for the target logs while retaining support for infrequent Logs Insights searches.

learning.reason: CloudWatch Logs Infrequent Access retains search capabilities while offering lower ingestion charges by omitting some Standard features. The class of an existing log group cannot be changed later.

title: Display invocation counts for changing endpoints in a single query
prompt: The operations team monitors the `Invocations` metric for SageMaker real-time endpoints in the same Region. Endpoints are deployed and retired regularly. Without updating the dashboard configuration each time, the team wants to display the total for all variants of each endpoint as separate time series. Which query should be selected?

choices.text: Select the time series containing endpoint and variant names with `SCHEMA`, and aggregate `SUM(Invocations)` with `GROUP BY EndpointName`.
choices.explanation: This separates each endpoint into its own series while summing the invocation counts of its variants.

choices.text: Select the same time series with `SCHEMA`, and aggregate `SUM(Invocations)` with `GROUP BY VariantName`.
choices.explanation: Because the grouping is by variant name, variants with the same name on different endpoints may be included in the same aggregation.

choices.text: Select the same time series with `SCHEMA` and retrieve `SUM(Invocations)` without grouping.
choices.explanation: This combines all endpoints into one total and therefore cannot display an individual series for each endpoint.

choices.text: List the current endpoint and variant names on the dashboard and add them with formulas by name.
choices.explanation: This can display the current endpoints, but the configuration must be updated when endpoints or variants are added.

learning.reason: Metrics Insights can group time series by metric dimensions. Selecting only time series with endpoint and variant names and grouping by endpoint name avoids combining results from different endpoints.
learning.concept: Dynamic aggregation with CloudWatch Metrics Insights `SCHEMA` and `GROUP BY`

title: Retire only a temporary KMS grant when it is no longer needed
prompt: During a model migration within the same account, a grant was created to allow limited KMS operations. The migration role is specified as the grant’s `RetiringPrincipal` and has not been granted permission to manage the key policy or `kms:RevokeGrant`. There is no explicit deny. After the migration, how can the role retire only this grant without affecting other workloads that use the same key?

choices.text: Only terminate the migration role’s session.
choices.explanation: Ending an individual session does not delete the KMS grant, so the permissions granted by it remain.

choices.text: From the migration role, call `RetireGrant` with the target key ID and grant ID.
choices.explanation: As the `RetiringPrincipal`, the role can retire the specified grant.

choices.text: From the migration role, call `RevokeGrant` with the target key ID and grant ID.
choices.explanation: The revoke operation additionally requires `kms:RevokeGrant`; specifying the retiring principal alone is not sufficient.

choices.text: From the migration role, disable the customer managed key.
choices.explanation: Disabling the key affects other uses of the same key and does not retire only one grant.

learning.reason: `RetireGrant` can be used by the retiring principal specified in the grant. It retires the target grant while leaving the key and other grants available.
learning.concept: The authorization difference between `RetireGrant` and `RevokeGrant` using a KMS `RetiringPrincipal`

title: Retain Deployment Images While Cleaning Up Old Untagged Images
prompt: A private ECR repository used for inference contains old untagged images created by multiple CI attempts. All images required for the current deployment and rollback are tagged. You must automatically delete only untagged images that are more than 30 days old and review the candidate list before applying the rule. Which actions should you take? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Apply the policy first, then review the candidate list in CloudTrail deletion records.
choices.explanation: The execution can be tracked, but this does not satisfy the requirement to review the candidates before activation.

choices.text: Create a rule that expires images with `tagStatus=untagged` and `countType=sinceImagePushed` when they are more than 30 days old.
choices.explanation: This selects untagged images that meet the age requirement based on the time since they were pushed, while excluding the tagged current and rollback versions.

choices.text: Run a preview of the created policy and review the candidate list.
choices.explanation: You can review the images targeted by the rule before enabling deletion.

choices.text: Create a rule that expires images more than 30 days old with `tagStatus=any`.
choices.explanation: Tagged images would also be evaluated, so deployment images that should be protected could be deleted.

choices.text: Make the repository tags immutable and wait for untagged images older than 30 days to be deleted.
choices.explanation: Preventing tag overwrites alone does not delete images based on their age.

learning.reason: ECR lifecycle rules can combine tag status and image age to limit the images selected for expiration. A policy preview lets you validate the deletion candidates before applying the policy.
learning.concept: Expiring only untagged images and previewing an ECR lifecycle policy

title: Detect Read Throttling for a Specific Feature Group
prompt: Several SageMaker Feature Store feature groups are used for online inference. In some periods, inference fails, and you want to monitor, in five-minute intervals, only the number of throttled single-record `GetRecord` reads for `payment-live`. Do not count 4xx errors caused by invalid input. Which CloudWatch configuration should you use?

choices.text: Monitor the five-minute `Sum` of `ConsumedReadCapacityUnits` with the same dimensions.
choices.explanation: This measures consumed read capacity, not the number of throttled requests.

choices.text: Monitor `ThrottledRequests` for all feature groups using only `OperationName=GetRecord`.
choices.explanation: For a single-record operation, the feature group dimension must also be used. Without the group name, the required feature group cannot be isolated.

choices.text: Monitor the five-minute `Sum` of `ThrottledRequests` with `FeatureGroupName=payment-live` and `OperationName=GetRecord`.
choices.explanation: This obtains the number of throttled requests for the specified feature group and operation.

choices.text: Monitor the five-minute `Sum` of `Operation4XXErrors` with the same dimensions.
choices.explanation: This includes other 4xx errors caused by invalid input or request conditions and therefore does not represent throttling alone.

learning.reason: Feature Store publishes a dedicated throttling metric. For non-batch operations, the metric can be filtered by feature group name and operation name, and `Sum` provides the number of occurrences during the period.
learning.concept: SageMaker Feature Store `ThrottledRequests` and feature-group and operation dimensions

prompt: A data-ingestion AWS account writes Parquet files to an S3 bucket in a separate training account. The writer's policy and the bucket policy already grant the required access. choices.text: Specify `Bucket owner preferred` and keep the client configured not to attach an ACL.
choices.explanation: For the bucket owner to own the object, the writer must specify the predefined `bucket-owner-full-control` ACL.

choices.text: Specify `Object writer` and add read permissions for the bucket-owning account.

choices.text: Enable only S3 Block Public Access on the bucket.

choices.text: Specify `Bucket owner enforced` and control access through policies.
choices.explanation: This does not require an ACL during writes and makes the bucket owner the owner of the objects.

learning.reason: With Bucket owner enforced, object ACLs are disabled and the bucket owner owns objects regardless of the account that writes them. Access is managed through policies.

title: Use Only Confirmed JSON Files as the Starting Point for Data Preparation
prompt: A training bucket receives source files under `raw/`, confirmed files under `ready/`, and audit `.csv` files in the same `ready/` prefix. You want the data-preparation Lambda to receive only events for `.json` objects created under `ready/`; the function itself will not filter them. Which filter should be configured for the S3 notification?

choices.text: For `s3:ObjectCreated:*`, specify `ready/*.json` as the prefix.
choices.explanation: Wildcards cannot be used as pattern matching in a key-filter prefix.

choices.text: For `s3:ObjectCreated:*`, specify the prefix `ready/` and the suffix `.json` in the same configuration.
choices.explanation: Confirmed JSON files match both conditions. JSON files under `raw/` and CSV files under `ready/` are excluded.

choices.text: For `s3:ObjectCreated:*`, specify only the prefix `ready/.
choices.explanation: This selects the confirmed path, but CSV files in the same path also generate notifications.

choices.text: For `s3:ObjectCreated:*`, specify only the suffix `.json`.
choices.explanation: This filters by file extension but also includes JSON files under `raw/`.

learning.reason: When an S3 event notification rule specifies both an object-key prefix and suffix, only keys matching both filters are selected.

title: Correct existing bounding boxes while preserving the original annotations
prompt: Ground Truth labeling for an image-training dataset is complete, but some bounding box positions must be corrected. Create a job through the API so workers can view and edit the existing boxes and the original attributes can later be compared with the corrections. Which two settings should be selected?

choices.text: Use the original output manifest as the input and select a task for adjusting bounding boxes.
choices.explanation: The images and original annotations are carried forward, allowing workers to edit the boxes directly.

choices.text: Specify a different `LabelAttributeName` from the original job for the corrected results.
choices.explanation: The original annotations and adjustment results receive different attribute names, allowing them to be compared later.

choices.text: Use the original output manifest and select a task for validating bounding boxes.
choices.explanation: This can evaluate existing labels, but it is not an adjustment task that directly changes the boxes.

choices.text: Create a new input manifest containing only image URIs and pass it to the adjustment job.
choices.explanation: The existing boxes to be displayed to workers would no longer be included in the input.

choices.text: Specify the same `LabelAttributeName` as the original job for the corrected results.
choices.explanation: Creating an adjustment job through the API requires a label attribute name different from that of the original job.

learning.reason: An adjustment job displays and lets workers edit labels from the original output manifest. Using a different LabelAttributeName for the output distinguishes the original annotations from the adjusted annotations.
learning.concept: Input manifests and a new LabelAttributeName for Ground Truth adjustment jobs

title: Protect existing columns and discover only added columns in the Data Catalog
prompt: Glue tables for one S3 prefix are crawled regularly. Columns added to new files must be registered in the catalog, but the data type of the existing `amount` column must not change because of a small number of malformed files. What should be selected for the crawler's table update behavior?

choices.text: Update the existing table definition with the complete schema detected by the crawler.
choices.explanation: In addition to new columns, the data types of existing columns could also be changed.

choices.text: Configure the crawler to inspect only new subfolders added since the last crawl.
choices.explanation: This changes folder selection; it does not specify how old and new columns are updated in the table.

choices.text: Use the setting that adds only added columns (`MergeNewColumns`).
choices.explanation: The crawler adds newly discovered columns without replacing existing columns.

choices.text: Always ignore crawler changes and do not update the existing table.
choices.explanation: This preserves existing column types, but new columns are not added automatically.

learning.reason: Glue crawlers can apply only added columns to an existing table. This meets the requirement to register new columns while preventing changes to the types of existing columns.
learning.concept: Glue Data Catalog crawler setting Add new columns only and `MergeNewColumns`

title: Split multiple nested arrays into tables that can be joined to the parent
prompt: Order JSON data in S3 contains a variable-length line-item array for each order. Each line item also contains an array of attributes. The data must be passed to downstream processing as multiple tables that retain every element and can be joined back to the parent order. Which transformation is appropriate?

choices.text: Expand only the first element of each array into columns of the parent `DynamicFrame`.
choices.explanation: This produces a flatter structure, but elements after the first are lost.

choices.text: Rename the array columns with `apply_mapping` and save them in a single `DynamicFrame` with the original structure.
choices.explanation: Column mapping specifies fields and types, but it does not generate multiple related tables.

choices.text: Convert each array to a JSON string and write a single CSV containing those columns.
choices.explanation: The values can be preserved, but this does not meet the requirement for separate tables that can be joined to the parent.

choices.text: Apply `relationalize` to the original `DynamicFrame` and output a root `DynamicFrame` and a `DynamicFrame` for each array.
choices.explanation: Variable-length arrays are converted into separate tables, and the original relationships can be reconstructed using the generated keys.

learning.reason: `DynamicFrame.relationalize` expands nested structures and separates arrays into related `DynamicFrame` objects that can be joined using generated keys.
learning.concept: Splitting arrays into tables and using join keys with `DynamicFrame.relationalize`

title: Prevent LOB truncation when ingesting data into S3
prompt: AWS DMS is moving product descriptions from a source database to an S3 bucket for training. The descriptions are in a LOB column, with a maximum source-side input size of 32 KiB. During a test transfer, descriptions longer than the 16 KiB limit were truncated. Which setting is appropriate to transfer the complete descriptions while retaining the S3 target?

choices.text: Use limited-size LOB mode and set `LobMaxSize` to at least 32 KiB.
choices.explanation: This supports the maximum source-column size and prevents truncation caused by the previous 16 KiB limit.

choices.text: Keep the S3 target and switch to full LOB mode, removing the size setting.
choices.explanation: S3 targets do not support full LOB mode.

choices.text: Keep the 16 KiB limit in limited-size LOB mode and increase the maximum size of DMS S3 output files.
choices.explanation: The size of each CSV file and the transfer limit for an individual LOB are separate; truncation would remain.

choices.text: Disable limited-size LOB mode and change the column type to string at the target.
choices.explanation: Specifying a target type does not configure DMS to read and transfer the complete LOB column.

learning.reason: In limited-size LOB mode, content exceeding the configured maximum size is truncated. Because S3 targets do not support full LOB mode, the limit must cover the known maximum source size.
learning.concept: `LimitedSizeLobMode` and `LobMaxSize` for DMS S3 targets

title: Pass Athena query results as Parquet without registering them in the catalog
prompt: A model evaluation specialist wants to extract a target period from an existing Athena table and pass the results as Parquet to a new S3 prefix. This is a one-time export, and the operator must not be granted permission to create a new table in the Data Catalog. Which query should be used?

choices.text: Save the extraction query with `CREATE VIEW`, then pass along an S3 key that points to the view.
choices.explanation: Creating a view definition does not export the query results as Parquet objects.

choices.text: Run `UNLOAD (SELECT ...) TO ... WITH (format = 'PARQUET')`.
choices.explanation: This writes the extracted results to S3 as Parquet without registering a new table.

choices.text: Run `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT` in Parquet format.
choices.explanation: This can produce Parquet output, but it also creates a new Athena table.

choices.text: Run a regular `SELECT` and change the result file extension to `.parquet`.
choices.explanation: Changing only the extension does not convert the result data to Parquet.

learning.reason: Athena UNLOAD writes SELECT results to S3 in the specified format without requiring a new table. For ordinary nonpartitioned output, choose an empty destination.
learning.concept: Using Athena UNLOAD to output Parquet without creating a table in the Data Catalog

title: Write events from a single producer while preserving device event order
prompt: The ingestion process for Kinesis Data Streams uses an explicit partition key. A single producer sends events from the same device serially, and the sequence numbers assigned to that device's events must increase strictly. Which method should be used?

choices.text: Assign a different partition key to each event and execute `PutRecord` in parallel.
choices.explanation: The events could be routed to different shards, and this is not serial writing that uses the result of the immediately preceding request.

choices.text: Add each event's send time to the data payload and execute `PutRecord` without ordering in parallel.
choices.explanation: The timestamp in the data can be used for sorting later, but it does not specify the order of the sequence numbers issued by the service.

choices.text: Use the device ID as the same partition key and pass the preceding response's `SequenceNumber` to the next `PutRecord.SequenceNumberForOrdering`.
choices.explanation: Receiving each result before issuing the next request creates a chain of serial writes and specifies ordering for the same device key.

choices.text: Use the same device ID as the partition key and arrange a batch `PutRecords` array in event order.
choices.explanation: Even with the same key, `PutRecords` does not guarantee ordering. Individual entries can fail and may need to be resent.

learning.reason: When `PutRecord` is executed serially from the same client with the same partition key, passing the previous result's sequence number lets the producer specify strict increasing order.
learning.concept: Kinesis `PutRecord`, `SequenceNumberForOrdering`, and the partition key

title: Configure post-transfer DataSync verification to match the operational requirements
prompt: Training materials are being copied in AWS DataSync Basic mode. Match one appropriate VerifyMode to each of the three tasks. Data integrity checks during transfer are performed for all tasks.

choices.text: `ONLY_FILES_TRANSFERRED`
choices.explanation: After completion, compare the checksums of the data and metadata transferred this time at the source and destination.

choices.text: `POINT_IN_TIME_CONSISTENT`
choices.explanation: After completion, check both locations and verify synchronization, including data that was not transferred this time.

choices.text: `NONE`
choices.explanation: Integrity verification during transfer continues, but no post-completion verification is performed.

learning.reason: VerifyMode determines how much additional checksum verification is performed after transfer, in addition to the checks during transfer: only the data transferred this time, the entire source and destination including unchanged data, or no additional verification.
learning.concept: DataSync `ONLY_FILES_TRANSFERRED`, `POINT_IN_TIME_CONSISTENT`, and `NONE`

title: Synthesize the minority class only on the training side while preserving the validation distribution
prompt: You are preparing data for a defect-classification model in SageMaker Data Wrangler. Positive examples account for 2% of the total. You want to augment training with examples interpolated from similar positive examples rather than simple duplicates of the original positive examples. The validation set must preserve the actual positive rate and data independence. In what order should the processing be performed?

choices.text: Apply SMOTE to the entire original dataset, then randomly split the result into training and validation sets.
choices.explanation: Synthetic examples can be mixed into the validation set, and similar original samples or derived examples could appear in both sets.

choices.text: After splitting, randomly oversample the positive examples in the training set with replacement.
choices.explanation: This preserves the validation distribution, but it duplicates existing positive examples rather than creating interpolated examples.

choices.text: After splitting, apply SMOTE separately to the training set and the validation set.
choices.explanation: Even without creating synthetic examples across the sets, the validation set's positive rate changes from the actual distribution.

choices.text: Split the original data into training and validation sets, then apply SMOTE only to the training set.
choices.explanation: This meets the requirement to increase positive examples through interpolation while leaving the validation-set distribution unchanged.

learning.reason: Splitting the real data first and applying SMOTE only to the training data creates interpolated minority-class examples without introducing synthetic examples or training-derived information into the validation set.
learning.concept: Oversampling only the training set with SMOTE in Data Wrangler

title: Aligning time series to fixed intervals by sensor
prompt: Sensor temperatures are recorded at different times for each device. The prediction model requires input at 15-minute intervals for each device, and when multiple observations fall within the same 15-minute window, their average must be used. Which transformation should be applied in SageMaker Data Wrangler?

choices.text: Treat each device as a separate series, resample the timestamps to 15-minute intervals, and average the temperatures within each window.
choices.explanation: This aligns the data to the required intervals without mixing devices and aggregates multiple observations in each window.

choices.text: Calculate a 15-observation moving average for each device while preserving the input timestamps.
choices.explanation: An observation-count-based average does not create 15-minute windows, and the output remains irregularly spaced.

choices.text: Impute missing temperatures in existing rows with the average without adding or aggregating rows.
choices.explanation: This can fill missing values, but it does not transform the timestamps into regular intervals.

choices.text: First combine all devices by timestamp, then aggregate the temperature in each 15-minute window into one value.
choices.explanation: The time windows are aligned, but measurements from different devices are mixed, so device-specific input cannot be created.

learning.reason: Time-series resampling aligns observations to regular intervals. Multiple observations within an interval can be aggregated using a method such as averaging, and multiple time series can be transformed by group.
learning.concept: Specify regular time windows and an aggregation method with Data Wrangler Resample

title: Reflecting partially processed consumer batches in the checkpoint
prompt: Lambda receives five records from a single Kinesis shard, represented in order as `s1` through `s5`. `s1` and `s2` succeed, and `s3` fails. `ReportBatchItemFailures` is enabled for the event source mapping, and batch bisecting is disabled. What should be returned to make the retry start at `s3`?

choices.text: Put the sequence number of `s2` in `batchItemFailures`.
choices.explanation: Returning the last successful position causes the retry to start from that record, going earlier than required.

choices.text: In a successful response, put the sequence number for `s3` in `itemIdentifier` within `batchItemFailures`.
choices.explanation: The retry starts at the failed record and does not include the preceding `s1` and `s2` at the beginning of the retry.

choices.text: Terminate the function with an exception and write the failure position to the logs instead of returning a response.
choices.explanation: The failure position is not communicated to the event source, so the entire batch is treated as failed.

choices.text: Return an empty `batchItemFailures` from the function.
choices.explanation: This reports all records as successful, so the failure of `s3` is not retried.

learning.reason: For a partial batch failure response for Kinesis, specify the failed record's sequence number. Lambda retries from the oldest failed item reported.
learning.concept: Sequence numbers in batchItemFailures for a Lambda event source using Kinesis

choices.text: Refresh the created materialized view with `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW`.
choices.explanation: Refreshing the view ingests data from the stream so that it can be used in queries.

choices.explanation: This defines the source in Redshift so that the stream can be referenced by the view.

choices.explanation: This specifies the view that reads the stream after the external schema has been created.

learning.reason: Redshift streaming ingestion requires an external schema mapped to Kinesis and a materialized view that references the stream. Refreshing the view retrieves data from the stream without using a staging layer.

title: Scaling Glue ETL workers with the processing volume

choices.explanation: This limits the number of parallel job runs; it does not adjust the number of workers within a run.

learning.reason: When Glue Auto Scaling is enabled, executors scale up or down according to processing parallelism, and workers are provisioned up to the maximum specified for the job.

choices.text: Use EMRFS to save the processing results to a dedicated S3 prefix and pass that location to subsequent jobs.
