title: Monitoring Short Bursts in 10-Second Intervals Instead of Averaging Them Over One Minute
prompt: A custom high-frequency inference service sometimes experiences a queue-depth spike lasting only 10 seconds. A value aggregated over one minute missed it. The application can retrieve the queue depth every second. Which combination of settings allows a CloudWatch custom metric to be evaluated by an alarm at 10-second intervals?

choices.text: Keep the metric at 60 seconds and set only the dashboard refresh interval to 10 seconds.
choices.explanation: Refreshing the display more frequently does not change the resolution of the underlying metric or the alarm interval.

choices.text: Publish the queue depth with `StorageResolution=1` and set the alarm `Period` to 10 seconds.
choices.explanation: A high-resolution time series can be evaluated with an alarm period of less than one minute.

choices.text: Publish at the standard 60-second resolution and set only the alarm to a 10-second interval.
choices.explanation: The metric remains at standard resolution and cannot provide data points for evaluation at the requested interval.

choices.text: Publish at high resolution but leave the alarm period at 60 seconds.
choices.explanation: The stored granularity becomes finer, but the alarm itself is not evaluated in 10-second intervals.

learning.reason: High-resolution custom metrics can be published with `StorageResolution=1`, which enables a 10-second alarm period. Specifying a shorter period without high-resolution metrics does not increase the number of available evaluation points.
learning.concept: CloudWatch custom metric high resolution and alarm periods

title: Delivering Scheduled EC2 Changes Supporting Inference to Operations Staff
prompt: An inference environment running ECS on EC2 is being operated. Before CPU utilization or response latency becomes abnormal, the operations team must receive account-level EC2 scheduled-change notifications issued by AWS Health. Notifications are consolidated in an existing Amazon SNS topic. Which event notification should be configured?

choices.text: Record EC2 start and stop API calls with CloudTrail and notify the SNS topic only about those calls.
choices.explanation: These records concern operations that have already been performed, not future AWS Health events that are scheduled to occur.

choices.text: Forward only events in which the ECS task status becomes `STOPPED` to the SNS topic.
choices.explanation: This reports a task after it stops and does not provide advance notice of a scheduled change.

choices.text: Use EventBridge to select EC2 scheduled-change events from the `aws.health` source and route them to the SNS topic.
choices.explanation: This delivers scheduled changes issued by AWS Health to the operations team before symptoms appear in the inference system.

choices.text: Create a response-time alarm in CloudWatch and treat it as notification of an EC2 scheduled change.
choices.explanation: This detects latency that has already occurred but does not receive upcoming change information from AWS Health.

learning.reason: AWS Health events can be received through EventBridge, filtered by event category and affected service, and sent to SNS. This information has a different source from anomaly detection on service metrics.
learning.concept: EventBridge rules for AWS Health EC2 scheduledChange events

title: Comparing Learning-Data Bucket Growth by Prefix
prompt: Several teams store learning data under different prefixes in the same S3 bucket. The operations team wants to compare on a dashboard which team’s prefix is growing, using daily aggregates and trends. Which feature should be used if the team does not want to aggregate and maintain object listings itself?

choices.text: Monitor only the bucket-level `BucketSizeBytes` metric for S3 in CloudWatch.
choices.explanation: This shows the capacity of the entire bucket but not which team’s prefix is growing.

choices.text: Generate an S3 Inventory, aggregate each prefix daily with SQL, and operate a custom graph.
choices.explanation: This permits comparison but does not meet the requirement to avoid maintaining the listing and aggregation.

choices.text: Count only PUT requests in S3 server access logs and treat the count as bytes.
choices.explanation: PUT counts cannot provide daily stored capacity that accounts for object sizes, overwrites, and deletions.

choices.text: Enable detailed metrics and prefix aggregation for the target bucket in S3 Storage Lens, then compare them in the console dashboard.
choices.explanation: This provides daily capacity trends by prefix without maintaining a custom object-list aggregation.

learning.reason: Detailed metrics in S3 Storage Lens can include prefix aggregation. After configuring the target bucket and aggregation conditions, capacity over time can be investigated in a dashboard.
learning.concept: Prefix aggregation in the advanced tier of S3 Storage Lens
